category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
title: Gradual deployment with automatic rollback
prompt: For the first monitoring interval, send 10% of production Lambda alias traffic to the new version. If the interval completes, proceed to 100%; if an error-rate alarm fires, return to the old version without human intervention.

choices.text: Update all traffic to the new version and then notify the operator.
choices.explanation: This provides neither a partial-traffic validation period nor an automatic rollback.

choices.text: Change only the new version's reserved concurrency.
choices.explanation: This does not manage the deployment traffic percentage or rollback to the old version.

choices.text: Manually set the Lambda alias weights and connect the alarm to an email notification.
choices.explanation: This allows a partial deployment but does not provide automatic promotion and rollback.

choices.text: Configure a Lambda canary deployment and automatic rollback with CodeDeploy.
choices.explanation: This supports gradual deployment through a weighted alias and alarm-triggered actions.

learning.reason: This supports gradual deployment through a weighted alias and alarm-triggered actions.
learning.concept: Choose a deployment alarm based on a metric that indicates the health of the change, such as the user error rate.

examDomain: SDLCの自動化

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
title: Deploying to many accounts
prompt: Automatically deploy audit resources to new accounts that join the Security OU. Apply the same definition to existing accounts as well. Manual role creation during account initialization is not possible.

choices.text: Manually create the same stack in each account.
choices.explanation: It will not be applied automatically when accounts are added in the future.

choices.text: Set up an AWS Config aggregator for the organization.
choices.explanation: This provides visibility but does not deploy the specified CloudFormation resources.

choices.text: Create an organization trail in CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This consolidates activity records but does not deploy a template.

choices.text: Configure automatic deployment with an Organizations-integrated service-managed StackSets permission model.
choices.explanation: First deploy the stack to the existing accounts in the target OU, then use automatic deployment to apply the same definition to accounts that are added to or moved into the OU later. With the service-managed model, the required IAM roles are created automatically.

learning.reason: First deploy the stack to the existing accounts in the target OU, then use automatic deployment to apply the same definition to accounts that are added to or moved into the OU later. With the service-managed model, the required IAM roles are created automatically.
learning.concept: Confirm the target OU, Regions, maximum concurrent accounts, and failure tolerance before deployment.

examDomain: 構成管理とIaC

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
title: Scheduled AMI Updates
prompt: Rebuild the shared AMI every week and replicate only versions that pass configuration tests to multiple Regions. Do not rely on manually patching existing EC2 instances to apply patches to the base OS.

choices.text: Increase the desired capacity of the Auto Scaling group
choices.explanation: This changes the number of instances launched but does not update the AMI contents.

choices.text: Build a pipeline with EC2 Image Builder to create, test, and distribute images
choices.explanation: This can manage recurring updates to the base image.

choices.text: Only patch running EC2 instances manually
choices.explanation: The AMI used by new EC2 instances remains unchanged unless it is updated separately.

choices.text: Distribute snapshots of running EC2 instances every week
choices.explanation: This replicates storage but does not integrate controlled image creation, testing, and distribution.

learning.reason: It can manage recurring updates to the base image.
learning.concept: Manage updates to existing instances separately from updates to the base image used when instances are recreated.

examDomain: 構成管理とIaC

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
title: Automated Remediation Trigger
prompt: Periodically evaluate existing S3 buckets for deviations from a required encryption setting, and automatically run an approved remediation procedure when a bucket is noncompliant. Do not treat the mere presence or absence of a change API call as proof of compliance.

choices.text: Use EventBridge to detect only new bucket creations
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate the state of existing buckets or deviations that occur after creation.

choices.text: Combine an AWS Config rule with remediation using Systems Manager Automation
choices.explanation: A compliance evaluation can trigger predefined remediation.

choices.text: Set up only a billing alarm
choices.explanation: Changes in charges cannot determine whether a bucket's configuration is noncompliant.

choices.text: Review CloudTrail history periodically
choices.explanation: This can track operations but does not perform remediation.

learning.reason: A compliance evaluation can trigger predefined remediation.
learning.concept: Limit remediation permissions to the required resources and operations, and preserve consistency if the process is run again.

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
title: Reducing Notifications with a Composite Alarm
prompt: CPU and application error rates are evaluated over different windows, and each already has an alarm. Send the on-call team a single notification only when both alarms are in the ALARM state, while preserving each alarm's evaluation criteria.

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch composite alarm with an AND condition for the ALARM states of both alarms
choices.explanation: It can combine the states of individual alarms for notification.

choices.text: Connect both individual alarms directly to the same SNS topic
choices.explanation: A threshold breach in either alarm would trigger a notification.

choices.text: Monitor the average of the two values with a new alarm
choices.explanation: The values have different units, and their average does not represent the logical AND of the existing alarm states.

choices.text: Only extend the metric retention period
choices.explanation: This does not affect how notification conditions are combined.

learning.reason: It can combine the states of individual alarms for notification.
learning.concept: When individual alarms have different evaluation periods, also check when their ALARM states overlap.

examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
title: Detecting Failed Deployments with ECS
prompt: A service uses the standard ECS rolling update. A new task crashes immediately after starting and never reaches a steady state. You want to return to a successful deployment without deploying a custom monitoring script.

choices.text: Only extend the health check grace period
choices.explanation: This can help with temporary initialization, but it does not automatically roll back a persistent failure.

choices.text: Only increase the number of containers and continue
choices.explanation: The cause of the startup failure remains, and this does not configure a rollback to the previous deployment.

choices.text: Shorten the image deletion policy
choices.explanation: This changes how long build artifacts are retained; it does not roll back a deployment after a startup failure.

choices.text: Enable rollback for the ECS deployment circuit breaker
choices.explanation: It can detect a failed deployment and roll back to the previous healthy deployment.

learning.reason: It can detect a failed deployment and roll back to the previous healthy deployment.
learning.concept: Design for detecting startup failures as well as patterns in which application metrics worsen after startup.

examDomain: SDLCの自動化

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
title: Build the Artifact Once
prompt: The container contents differ between development and production after approval. You want to promote the tested binary and deploy that same binary to production even if a shared tag is reassigned.

choices.text: Use the image digest produced after the build as the pipeline artifact, and update the production task definition to use that same digest
choices.explanation: This points to the tested content without going through a mutable tag.

choices.text: Append a timestamp to the tag just before the production deployment
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee that the digest it points to is the one that was tested.

choices.text: Use latest in each environment and deploy to test first
choices.explanation: The tag could move while approval is pending.

choices.text: Rebuild the same commit in production
choices.explanation: Updates to the base image or external dependencies could produce a different artifact.

learning.reason: This points to the tested content without going through a mutable tag.
learning.concept: Promote the immutable identifier of the verified artifact, not the name of its source.

examDomain: SDLCの自動化

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
title: Recovery Exercise During a Regional Outage
prompt: You test the DR environment every month, but do not want to affect production traffic. Automate everything from restoring business data to validating the application in an isolated environment. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Switch production weighted DNS to 100% to the DR site every month
choices.explanation: This affects customer traffic.

choices.text: Overwrite the existing production DB with a backup
choices.explanation: This affects production data and services.

choices.text: Restore from backups in the DR Region to an isolated environment, then use a runbook to validate consistency and recovery time
choices.explanation: You can validate the actual restore procedure without touching the existing service.

choices.text: Check only whether the backup job succeeded each month
choices.explanation: This does not measure restore duration or behavior.

learning.reason: You can validate the actual restore procedure without touching the existing service.
learning.concept: Measure successful backup creation separately from successful restoration within the target time.

examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Pin the Artifact During Approval
prompt: Multiple commits pass through the same pipeline. Approvers want to release the inspected build to production. Which design prevents the wrong artifact from being selected even if a new artifact is produced while approval is pending?

choices.text: Rebuild the same branch in production
choices.explanation: A different commit or dependency could be used.

choices.text: Approve the mutable latest tag
choices.explanation: It could point to different content after approval.

choices.text: Bind the execution ID and artifact digest to the approval record, and refer to the same digest when promoting
choices.explanation: The approved artifact and the deployed artifact are the same.

choices.text: Have the approver record only the time
choices.explanation: This does not uniquely identify the artifact.

learning.reason: The approved artifact and the deployed artifact are the same.
learning.concept: Tie approval to the contents of an execution and promote the artifact without rebuilding it in each environment.

examDomain: SDLCの自動化

category: CI/CD、自動化、耐障害性
version: オリジナル模試 2026-11 拡充版
title: Centralized Notifications for Release Failures
prompt: Multiple teams deploy with CodePipeline. You want to notify the central on-call team immediately when a failure occurs, without polling, and handle only the relevant pipelines.

choices.text: Monitor only CloudTrail StartPipelineExecution
choices.explanation: Recording a start does not reveal the result.

choices.text: List execution history every 15 minutes
choices.explanation: This does not meet the event-driven requirement.

choices.text: Aggregate only pipeline success emails
choices.explanation: This does not provide immediate failure notifications.

choices.text: Filter for FAILED pipeline execution state changes in EventBridge and send them to SNS
choices.explanation: This provides event-driven notifications filtered by pipeline and state, with a centrally managed destination.

learning.reason: This provides event-driven notifications filtered by pipeline and state, with a centrally managed destination.
learning.concept: An audit event recording that an operation was initiated differs from a state event notifying you of the result of a long-running process.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Apply Database Changes One at a Time in Arrival Order
prompt: A CodePipeline stage has one action that applies interdependent schema changes. When commits arrive in quick succession, executions build up waiting before the stage. Every waiting change must be applied to the database in arrival order, without skipping any. Source checkout and builds may run concurrently with database changes. Which setting should you choose?

choices.text: Configure retries for the database action and run it again whenever it returns a failure code.
choices.explanation: Retries are a recovery mechanism for failures; they do not guarantee arrival order or exclusive access to the stage.

choices.text: Set the V2 pipeline to PARALLEL and assign a unique RunOrder to each action in the stage.
choices.explanation: RunOrder defines ordering within one execution; it does not determine the application order across separate executions.

choices.text: Set the V2 pipeline to QUEUED.
choices.explanation: Executions arriving at the same stage wait in order.

choices.text: Set the pipeline to SUPERSEDED and manually approve pending executions.
choices.explanation: Adding an approval does not change the behavior that lets a newer execution overtake a pending one.

learning.reason: V2 QUEUED makes executions wait in the order they reach the stage and prevents concurrent execution of that stage.
learning.concept: Distinguish pipeline-wide concurrency from the ordering of executions waiting for the same stage.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Promote to Production Only During the Change Window
prompt: Integration testing completed at 3 p.m. Production deployments through CodePipeline are allowed only on weekdays from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m. Executions that arrive outside the window must fail without running the production action. Builds are allowed at all times. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Evaluate a DeploymentWindow with On Success after the production action succeeds, and treat executions outside the window as failed.
choices.explanation: The time is evaluated after the production action has already run.

choices.text: Use an Entry DeploymentWindow and set it to Fail outside the window.
choices.explanation: The time condition stops the execution before the production action starts.

choices.text: Set the production stage's Entry condition to Skip so that executions outside the window complete successfully.
choices.explanation: This can avoid the production action, but it does not record the required execution failure.

choices.text: Start the Source stage only from an EventBridge schedule at 10 p.m.
choices.explanation: This cannot guarantee when production is reached and does not meet the requirement to allow builds at all times.

learning.reason: Evaluate the time zone-aware change window when entering the production stage.
learning.concept: Control the time a release starts separately from the time a deployment is allowed.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Make Post-Deployment Monitoring a Promotion Condition
prompt: A CodePipeline V2 deployment action checks connectivity and reports success, but errors under high load do not appear until 20 minutes after deployment. Before proceeding to the next stage, you must evaluate an existing alarm and, if it indicates a problem, roll back to the previous successful execution in the current pipeline structure. What should you add?

choices.text: Configure Rollback on Failure and monitor and notify on the post-deployment CloudWatch alarm outside the pipeline.
choices.explanation: The described action succeeds, so this condition alone will not be triggered.

choices.text: Disable execution of subsequent stages and redeploy the same input artifact when the alarm fires.
choices.explanation: Redeploying the same new release does not roll back to the previous successful execution.

choices.text: Configure CloudWatchAlarm and a wait period on On Success, then roll back if the alarm indicates a problem.
choices.explanation: This handles errors that appear after the action succeeds and can roll back the targeted execution.

choices.text: Check the alarm in the stage's Entry condition before deployment.
choices.explanation: This cannot evaluate delayed errors caused by the production deployment after they occur.

learning.reason: Configure a wait period with an On Success CloudWatchAlarm rule, and roll back if it fails.
learning.concept: Check provisioning success and service health at separate stages.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Isolate Parallel Integration Tests
prompt: A V2 CodePipeline runs in PARALLEL mode, and each execution creates a temporary stack through a CloudFormation action. An execution for a different commit updated the same stack and caused the test to fail. How can you preserve parallel executions and individual cleanup after each execution finishes?

choices.text: Use a fixed stack name for creation, testing, and deletion, and assign a different RunOrder to each action.
choices.explanation: Name collisions across separate pipeline executions remain possible.

choices.text: Change the mode to QUEUED and share a fixed name across all executions.
choices.explanation: Serialization may prevent collisions, but it does not preserve parallel testing.

choices.text: Build the stack name from qa- and PipelineExecutionId.
choices.explanation: The two executions use separate resources, and each execution can delete its own environment.

choices.text: Add the branch name to the stack name, so executions from the same branch share the name.
choices.explanation: This problem recurs if successive commits on the same branch run concurrently.

learning.reason: A pipeline execution ID is unique throughout an execution. Derive the same name for creation, reference, and deletion.
learning.concept: Choose an isolation unit based on each execution that may run concurrently, not the branch name.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Run independent checks in parallel after a prerequisite build
prompt: A CodeBuild batch must report diagnostics for multiple platforms together. Each independent diagnostic should run in parallel, but only after compilation of the shared schema succeeds. Which buildspec structure should you use?

choices.text: Use build-graph and specify the compilation build as a dependency for each diagnostic.
choices.explanation: This expresses both prerequisite completion and parallel diagnostics in the same batch.

choices.text: List compilation and diagnostics in sequence in build-list.
choices.explanation: The order of entries in a parallel list does not mean that the later builds wait for earlier ones to succeed.

choices.text: Use environment variables in build-matrix to separate the shared compilation and diagnostic commands, and express dependencies through the matrix order.
choices.explanation: Matrix expansion into combinations does not define a standalone build that runs first.

choices.text: Run all diagnostics sequentially in a single build phase.
choices.explanation: This preserves the prerequisite but loses diagnostic parallelism and individual build reporting.

learning.reason: With build-graph, you can declare dependencies between builds identified by ID and run dependent builds after their prerequisites finish.
learning.concept: Choose a batch build strategy to match the execution pattern and dependencies.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Reduce rebuilds of the same Docker layers
prompt: A Linux CodeBuild project that is not connected to a VPC uses a Dockerfile whose base image and early build steps are mostly shared. There is no requirement to guarantee cache hits every time; Docker layers should be reused when the same build host can be reused. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Put only the image name in an S3 cache and leave the Docker daemon unchanged.
choices.explanation: An image name does not contain layer data.

choices.text: Use a custom cache to save only the application's dependency directory and expect Docker layers to be reused automatically as well.
choices.explanation: An application dependency directory and the Docker daemon cache are separate cache targets.

choices.text: Use local caching in Docker layer mode and enable privileged mode for the environment.
choices.explanation: Docker layers are stored on a reusable host and can be used by a subsequent build.

choices.text: Choose only source caching and restore Docker layers from it.
choices.explanation: Source caching covers Git metadata; it does not configure Docker layer caching.

learning.reason: The Linux local Docker layer cache resides on the build host, and Docker operations require privileged mode.
learning.concept: Ensure builds remain correct even without a cache, so cache availability does not affect artifact correctness.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Track test results and coverage over time
prompt: The test run can produce JUnit XML for results and Cobertura XML for line coverage. You want to track pass/fail details and line coverage for the same run separately in the CodeBuild console, without having to unzip the artifact ZIP each time. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Forward test logs to CloudWatch only on failure.
choices.explanation: This does not provide test summaries and line coverage, including for successful runs.

choices.text: Include both XML files in an S3 artifact and do not configure reports.
choices.explanation: The files can be retrieved, but they will not be registered for aggregation in CodeBuild reports.

choices.text: Collect JUnit and Cobertura reports in separate report groups of the corresponding types.
choices.explanation: Configuring the two distinct formats and report types lets each appear in CodeBuild reports.

choices.text: Specify both XML files in a JUnit report group, then distinguish test results from coverage by filename after collection.
choices.explanation: The coverage XML is not in the specified test result format.

learning.reason: In separate CodeBuild report groups, specify the test result format and the code coverage format.
learning.concept: Record test case outcomes and executed code coverage as separate quality metrics.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Pass artifacts to another account
prompt: Account A has CodePipeline and an S3 artifact store; account B has a deployment action role. You want B to read centrally stored, encrypted artifacts and perform deployments. What should you combine to grant access only to the required resources without adding long-term keys? Select TWO.

choices.text: Edit the key policy for A's AWS managed key to add B's role.
choices.explanation: Users cannot edit an AWS managed key policy to share the key.

choices.text: Encrypt the artifacts with a customer managed KMS key in A and allow B's action role the required decryption access.
choices.explanation: This lets a role in another account use the key in question.

choices.text: Do not share the store; create a bucket with the same name in B.
choices.explanation: Creating a bucket in B does not make A's artifacts available.

choices.text: Grant artifact decryption permission only, and remove S3 permissions.
choices.explanation: Allowing decryption does not grant permission to retrieve the objects.

choices.text: Allow assumption of the action role and allow B's role to read the relevant S3 artifacts in A.
choices.explanation: This limits the principal and lets it retrieve encrypted objects from the store.

learning.reason: Reading cross-account artifacts requires authorization in both S3 and KMS. You must also configure the trust relationship for the pipeline role to assume the action role.
learning.concept: Check the operating principal in the other account, object access, and permission to use the key separately.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Validate Before Returning an EC2 Instance to Service
prompt: For a CodeDeploy in-place deployment using an ALB, you want to take a target EC2 instance out of service and send a validation request to its local environment after the application starts. A host that fails validation must not receive user traffic again. Which hook should you use?

choices.text: Use ApplicationStop to test connectivity to the new version.
choices.explanation: This hook stops the previous version; it does not run after the new version starts.

choices.text: Run the check in ValidateService and return a failure if it does not pass.
choices.explanation: Traffic is not restored until the post-start validation is complete.

choices.text: Run a check against the new binary in BeforeInstall.
choices.explanation: The new application has not been installed yet, so its post-start state cannot be checked.

choices.text: Run a local check in AfterAllowTraffic and start a CodeDeploy rollback if it fails.
choices.explanation: The instance will already have received user traffic before the check finishes.

learning.reason: For EC2/on-premises in-place deployments, ValidateService runs after ApplicationStart and before AllowTraffic-related events.
learning.concept: Check the application's health between startup and the resumption of traffic.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Test Connectivity Before Switching the Production Listener
prompt: You use CodeDeploy for an ECS blue/green deployment behind an ALB. You want to run integration tests that include the HTTP path through the new task set. Until the tests pass, the production listener must remain on the old tasks, and the tests must reach only the new tasks. What should you configure?

choices.text: Configure a test listener and validate the replacement task set in a hook after the test traffic is shifted.
choices.explanation: This directs only the test path to the new set and lets you hold the production listener switch until validation results are available.

choices.text: Shift 10% of production traffic and run the integration tests using the same URL.
choices.explanation: The tests will not reach only the new set, and users may see the version before it is validated.

choices.text: Test the target group attached to the old task set and use the results for the replacement set too.
choices.explanation: This does not test the replacement set's HTTP path.

choices.text: Move all production traffic immediately while testing, then revert to the old version if a test fails.
choices.explanation: This cannot prevent production traffic from reaching the version before it passes validation.

learning.reason: Use a test listener separate from the production listener, then validate after shifting test traffic.
learning.concept: Separating the user path from the test path lets you try the replacement version before moving production traffic.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Protect Internal Packages While Keeping Public Dependencies Available
prompt: In a single CodeArtifact repository, your internal npm packages are published directly by internal CI, while other dependencies are obtained through an external connection. For a known internal package name, you want to prevent future versions from being pulled in from external sources. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Set the internal package's origin controls to Publish ALLOW and Upstream BLOCK.
choices.explanation: This keeps direct publishing of the package available while closing the path for new versions to arrive from upstream repositories or the external connection.

choices.text: Remove the repository's external connection and use only the content already cached.
choices.explanation: This may protect internal packages, but it does not keep other public dependencies available.

choices.text: Set the internal package's origin controls to Publish BLOCK and Upstream ALLOW.
choices.explanation: This prevents internal CI from publishing and allows packages to be pulled in from upstream.

choices.text: Allow both origins for every package and list only the latest public version in the lockfile.
choices.explanation: The repository can still pull in an external version with the same name as an internal package.

learning.reason: Allow Publish and block Upstream for the internal package to preserve direct publishing while stopping upstream ingestion.
learning.concept: Distinguish which registries are available from which sources may supply versions for a particular package.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Specify the Change for Each Execution
prompt: With CodePipeline V2 managing a production database, the person running a release must provide the tenant identifier from the release request when starting a manual execution. Use the same pipeline and actions; the value is not secret, and neither the source nor the shared buildspec can be changed for each execution. What should you use?

choices.text: Commit the identifier to the source repository before starting the execution.
choices.explanation: This makes the input for each execution depend on a source change.

choices.text: Edit a configuration file in shared S3 before execution and have each deployment read the same object immediately before deploying.
choices.explanation: This does not isolate the value for each execution and changes what other executions may read.

choices.text: Update the CodeBuild project's default environment variable before each execution.
choices.explanation: The setting is shared by the project, so concurrent executions could receive mixed values.

choices.text: Make the identifier a pipeline-level variable and pass it with each execution.
choices.explanation: This preserves the shared definition while delivering a value specific to each execution.

learning.reason: You can leave a pipeline-level variable without a default, provide its value at execution time, and reference it from actions.
learning.concept: Keep runtime inputs isolated per execution instead of updating shared settings to pass them along.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Reuse only development tags
prompt: In the same private ECR repository, release tags must not be reassigned to a different digest after they have been published. Tags beginning with dev- may be overwritten during routine testing. How can this be enforced without an operator monitoring each push?

choices.text: Make all tags IMMUTABLE and allow development tags to be overwritten.
choices.explanation: This would also reject overwrites of development tags.

choices.text: Expire old development images with a lifecycle policy and make all tags MUTABLE.
choices.explanation: Controlling image retention does not prevent release tags from being reassigned.

choices.text: Make all tags MUTABLE and notify an administrator through EventBridge when a release name is detected.
choices.explanation: A notification after the event cannot reject a tag reassignment.

choices.text: Set tag mutability to IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION and add dev-* as an exclusion filter.
choices.explanation: This protects release tags while excluding only development tags from the restriction.

learning.reason: The immutable setting with exclusions protects ordinary tags while allowing tags matching the wildcard to be updated.
learning.concept: Tag mutability and when image data is deleted are controlled by separate policies.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Keep integration tests private while fetching dependencies
prompt: Add integration tests that connect from CodeBuild to a private RDS database. The build also fetches dependencies from a public package registry. Which combination keeps the test database private and ensures that no public IP is assigned to the CodeBuild network interface? Select two.

choices.text: Route traffic from the build subnet to the public registry through a NAT gateway.
choices.explanation: The build can fetch public dependencies even when its network interface has no public IP.

choices.text: Assign a public IP to RDS and allow access from the entire internet only during testing.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirements to keep the database private and restrict the scope of access.

choices.text: Configure only a public subnet and an internet gateway.
choices.explanation: A public IP cannot be assigned to the CodeBuild network interface, so this configuration alone cannot reach public destinations.

choices.text: Connect CodeBuild to a private subnet and an appropriate security group, and allow only the required traffic to RDS from that group.
choices.explanation: This keeps the database private while allowing the build to reach it over the test path.

choices.text: Add an S3 gateway endpoint and use it to provide a route to public registries as well.
choices.explanation: An endpoint dedicated to S3 does not forward traffic to arbitrary public destinations.

learning.reason: A CodeBuild VPC connection provides access to the internal database, while traffic to the public internet uses a route from the private subnet through NAT.
learning.concept: Check private-resource reachability separately from the route that lets the build fetch public dependencies.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Retain the old volume when it is replaced
prompt: A standalone EBS volume managed by CloudFormation must be replaced through a property update to move it to another Availability Zone. Keep the old volume for migration verification, but delete the volume managed by the stack at that time as usual if the stack is deleted later. Which settings should be specified in advance?

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain and DeletionPolicy to Delete.
choices.explanation: This retains the old volume during replacement and deletes the volume managed at the time of a later stack deletion.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Snapshot and DeletionPolicy to Delete.
choices.explanation: This retains a snapshot of the old data but not the old volume itself, as required.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Delete and DeletionPolicy to Retain.
choices.explanation: This deletes the old volume during replacement and retains the new volume when the stack is deleted later.

choices.text: Enable termination protection for the stack and leave both attributes at their default values.
choices.explanation: Termination protection controls stack deletion; it does not retain the old volume after replacement.

learning.reason: UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain preserves the old physical resource when a property update replaces it. DeletionPolicy: Delete applies to resources managed by the stack when the stack is deleted.
learning.concept: Choose retention attributes according to the event that causes the stack to stop managing a resource.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Review replacement impact before approval
prompt: An IaC review must determine whether an RDS update requires replacement. The person who submits a change and the person who approves its execution are different, and the production stack must not be changed before review. Which CloudFormation feature should be incorporated?

choices.text: Run drift detection and apply the template if no differences are found in the existing resources.
choices.explanation: Drift describes current differences; it does not show whether the proposed update will replace a resource.

choices.text: Create a change set and review the changes to the RDS resource and its Replacement field before executing it.
choices.explanation: Creating a change set alone does not apply the update.

choices.text: Validate the syntax with ValidateTemplate and, if it succeeds, conclude that RDS will not be replaced.
choices.explanation: Syntax validation does not include an update plan against the current stack.

choices.text: Run UpdateStack and inspect resource events after the status becomes UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS.
choices.explanation: The actual update starts before it has been reviewed.

learning.reason: The resource change list and Replacement field in a change set can be used to review an update before executing it.
learning.concept: Syntax validation, drift detection against existing resources, and a plan for a future update are different checks.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Stop Rollouts After a Failure in an Earlier Region
prompt: You are rolling out a StackSets update to three Regions. If the first Region exceeds the failure tolerance, do not send changes to the remaining Regions. You also want to reduce the number of accounts running concurrently in response to failures in the earlier Region. Which two settings should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Use Soft Failure Tolerance and maintain the specified maximum concurrency.
choices.explanation: Even if failures occur within a Region, this does not reduce concurrency as required.

choices.text: Place the earlier Region first and set Region concurrency to Sequential.
choices.explanation: The next Region does not start until the outcome in the earlier Region is known.

choices.text: Disable automatic deployment and set the failure tolerance to the maximum value.
choices.explanation: Automatic deployment when an account joins an OU is separate from failure controls for a running operation.

choices.text: Specify the account failure tolerance and select Strict Failure Tolerance.
choices.explanation: Reduce the number of accounts running concurrently within a Region in response to failures, and stop the rollout if the tolerance is exceeded.

choices.text: Set Region concurrency to Parallel.
choices.explanation: Other Regions start before the outcome in the earlier Region is known.

learning.reason: Sequential delays the start of deployment in subsequent Regions, while Strict Failure Tolerance reduces account concurrency when failures occur.
learning.concept: Concurrency limits within accounts and the order of deployments across Regions are independent deployment settings.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Bring an Existing Resource Under Stack Management
prompt: An existing S3 bucket containing several years of logs is still managed manually. You want to bring it under CloudFormation management without recreating the bucket or moving the active log delivery. The bucket does not belong to another stack. What should you do?

choices.text: Create it using a regular CREATE change set with the same bucket name.
choices.explanation: This attempts to create a new bucket with the same name; it does not import the existing bucket into management.

choices.text: Empty and delete the bucket, then create it from a stack using the same name.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to preserve the logs and log delivery.

choices.text: Register the bucket name in another stack's Outputs, then reference the bucket from a new management stack with ImportValue.
choices.explanation: This lets you reference the name, but does not register the referenced resource as managed by the stack.

choices.text: Specify the existing bucket name in a resource definition with a DeletionPolicy, then import the resource.
choices.explanation: This brings the existing bucket under management while allowing it to remain in use.

learning.reason: Resource import associates a template definition with the identifier of an existing physical resource.
learning.concept: Distinguish between referencing a resource in a template, registering it under management, and creating a new resource.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Detect Drift in Nested Stack Settings
prompt: A production parent stack contains multiple nested stacks. You want to detect changes to default values that the child templates do not explicitly specify as well. Currently, you run drift detection only on the parent stack. How should you change your monitoring approach?

choices.text: Use a stack policy to reject updates to child stacks, and do not inspect them after changes.
choices.explanation: This does not measure existing differences or detect out-of-band changes.

choices.text: Specify the properties to inspect and run drift detection on each child stack individually.
choices.explanation: This defines the comparison targets and includes child stacks that are not inspected automatically from the parent.

choices.text: Leave default values implicit in the child templates and repeat drift detection on the parent at shorter intervals to monitor for changes.
choices.explanation: Running the detection more often does not expand its coverage.

choices.text: Compare only the last-updated timestamp of each child stack.
choices.explanation: This does not compare actual property values changed directly in the console.

learning.reason: Drift detection on a parent does not evaluate child stacks recursively. Explicitly specify the expected values for the settings you want to detect.
learning.concept: Identify the resources and properties covered by drift detection before using its results as evidence of compliance.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Protect a Critical Resource from Routine Updates
prompt: Application resources in the same stack change every week. You normally want to prevent the critical database from being deleted, replaced, or modified by a stack update, allowing those changes only through an update with an explicit exception procedure. What should you configure while still allowing routine application updates?

choices.text: Enable termination protection for the stack only.
choices.explanation: This can prevent deletion of the entire stack, but does not prevent replacement or updates to individual resources.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy Retain on the database.
choices.explanation: Specifying that the resource should be retained does not reject routine template changes.

choices.text: Remove stack update permissions from application update owners and ask an administrator to perform updates for each scheduled release.
choices.explanation: This might prevent database changes, but it also blocks routine application updates.

choices.text: Use a stack policy to deny Update for the database's logical ID.
choices.explanation: This restricts updates to the protected resource while allowing other resources in the same stack to be updated.

learning.reason: A stack policy controls CloudFormation update operations by logical ID; a temporary policy can be used for an exception update.
learning.concept: Use stack termination protection and protection of individual resources during updates for their distinct purposes.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Separate CDK asset publishing permissions from deployment permissions
prompt: CI synthesizes Lambda ZIP files and container images with CDK. The target account and Region have not been bootstrapped, and permissions for publishing assets and provisioning resources through CloudFormation must be managed separately. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Bootstrap the target environment and use separate publishing and execution roles.
choices.explanation: This creates an asset store and allows publishing and resource creation to be authorized through separate roles.

choices.text: Give administrator permissions to the user who installed CDK locally, and use that user for both publishing and deployment.
choices.explanation: This does not separate publishing permissions from execution permissions.

choices.text: Bootstrap only the developer account and define no roles in the target environment.
choices.explanation: This does not provide the required asset store and execution roles in the target account and Region.

choices.text: Run CDK synth to generate the template, assuming the publishing role and artifact store are created during synthesis.
choices.explanation: Synthesis does not create the target environment’s asset store or roles.

learning.reason: The current bootstrap setup provides roles for publishing file and image assets, deploying, and executing CloudFormation.
learning.concept: Synthesis, asset publishing, stack operations, and operations on resources in a template are separate stages.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Validate cross-field conditions before distributing a configuration
prompt: In AppConfig free-form JSON, minWorkers and maxWorkers must each be integers within their allowed ranges. In addition, reject any combination where minWorkers exceeds maxWorkers before the configuration is distributed. How can you do this while preserving the existing gradual deployment?

choices.text: In the configuration profile’s JSON Schema, set each property to an integer and require its individual value to be within its allowed range.
choices.explanation: This does not specify the relationship between the two dynamic values.

choices.text: Add a monitoring alarm and wait until the production application reports an error.
choices.explanation: This addresses a failure after distribution; it does not reject an invalid configuration beforehand.

choices.text: Complete the deployment and then halve the gradual deployment percentage.
choices.explanation: This does not validate the configuration before distribution.

choices.text: Use a Lambda validator to compare the two values and reject an invalid configuration.
choices.explanation: This evaluates the cross-field condition before the configuration is distributed to the application.

learning.reason: A Lambda validator receives the configuration content and can check custom semantic consistency.
learning.concept: In addition to syntax constraints on individual fields, validate that combinations of fields are operationally valid.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Keep configuration consistent on newly added managed nodes
prompt: EC2 instances are continuously replaced by Auto Scaling. SSM managed nodes have role tags. You need to keep the agent configuration in a defined state on nodes with the target role and operate new nodes added later under the same policy. What should you do?

choices.text: Target a State Manager association by role tag.
choices.explanation: This can continuously apply the same configuration to current and future matching nodes.

choices.text: Put a manually edited configuration in the EC2 launch template and leave existing nodes unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not provide ongoing configuration management for existing nodes.

choices.text: Each time a new instance ID appears in the logs, add it to an inventory and investigate configuration differences later.
choices.explanation: This may help with inventory, but it does not apply and maintain the specified configuration.

choices.text: List the running instance IDs and issue Run Command once.
choices.explanation: New nodes will not be in the initial list, and later configuration drift will not be corrected.

learning.reason: Target a State Manager association by tags, and specify the desired configuration and application schedule.
learning.concept: Associate the desired state with attributes of managed nodes instead of a fixed list of instance IDs.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Stop new patch operations before the maintenance window ends
prompt: Run a patching Automation runbook in SSM Maintenance Windows. During the final hour of a 3-hour window, do not start new invocations on the targets, while allowing Automations started earlier to continue. How should the task be configured when registered?

choices.text: Set Duration to 3 hours and Cutoff to 1 hour, and leave the Automation task’s CutoffBehavior at its default, CONTINUE_TASK.
choices.explanation: After the cutoff, running tasks may still start new invocations.

choices.text: Set Duration to 3 hours and Cutoff to 1 hour, and set the Automation task’s CutoffBehavior to CANCEL_TASK.
choices.explanation: After 2 hours, stop new invocations while allowing Automations that have already started to continue.

choices.text: With the same time settings, register a Run Command task and set CutoffBehavior to CANCEL_TASK.
choices.explanation: For Run Command, reaching the cutoff also attempts to cancel commands that are already running.

choices.text: Set Duration to 3 hours and Cutoff to 0 hours, and set CANCEL_TASK.
choices.explanation: This allows new invocations to start during the final hour.

learning.reason: Duration and Cutoff determine when invocations stop. For an Automation task, CANCEL_TASK lets running invocations continue and prevents new invocations from starting.
learning.concept: Configure the window end time, the time to stop invocations, and the handling of running invocations separately.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Gradually migrating references to a shared output
prompt: A network stack exports SubnetId, and several stacks owned by another team reference it with Fn::ImportValue. You want to migrate to a new subnet in stages while keeping the references used by teams that have not migrated valid. Which update order should you use?

choices.text: Tag the physical resources in all stacks first so Fn::ImportValue can select the new ID from the tags.
choices.explanation: Fn::ImportValue references an export name; it does not resolve a migration target from tags.

choices.text: Keep the original export name and change only its value first.
choices.explanation: The value cannot be changed while dependent stacks are still referencing the export.

choices.text: Add a new output under a different name, migrate the dependent stacks individually, and then delete the old export.
choices.explanation: The old and new references can coexist, and the old one can be removed after no stacks depend on it.

choices.text: Delete the old export and subnet before updating the dependent stacks one by one.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the reference used by dependent stacks before they are updated.

learning.reason: An export that is being imported cannot be changed or deleted. Add a new export under a different name and migrate the dependents to it.
learning.concept: To migrate a shared output, add it on the provider side, migrate consumers, and then remove the old reference.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Switching the write target for planned maintenance
prompt: Both Regions in an Aurora Global Database are healthy, and the secondary cluster has a DB instance. For maintenance during a holiday, you want to move the write target to the secondary and operate the former primary as the secondary in the same global database. A brief write interruption is acceptable, but committed changes must not be lost. Which procedure should you choose?

choices.text: Stop monitoring lag and perform a failover that permits data loss.
choices.explanation: This cannot ensure zero data loss as required for planned maintenance.

choices.text: Detach the secondary DB cluster and promote it to a standalone database, while keeping the former primary in the same global configuration.
choices.explanation: A detached database is no longer part of the same global database, so this does not swap the roles as required.

choices.text: Switch the application's write target to the secondary cluster and leave the Aurora roles unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the connection target alone does not transfer the writable primary role.

choices.text: Perform a planned switchover of the global database.
choices.explanation: After synchronization, the roles switch, allowing the change without losing committed data.

learning.reason: A planned switchover synchronizes the secondary DB cluster before switching the primary role.
learning.concept: For a planned switch, synchronization can complete before the change. During failover after an outage, replication lag at the time of interruption affects the recovery point.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Automatically stopping a recovery exercise based on the error rate
prompt: You are running an AWS FIS exercise that disrupts an access point. If the users' HTTP 5xx rate exceeds the acceptable value, you want the exercise to stop even when no operator is watching the console. The workload already has a CloudWatch alarm that uses that metric. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Set a fixed run duration for the experiment actions and display the alarm only on a dashboard.
choices.explanation: Even if conditions worsen during the run, the alarm will not cause the experiment to stop.

choices.text: Use the existing alarm only to notify the on-call team through SNS.
choices.explanation: This sends a notification, but the experiment will not stop unless an operator intervenes.

choices.text: Specify the existing CloudWatch alarm as a stop condition in the experiment template.
choices.explanation: FIS uses the alarm's state transition to decide when to stop the experiment.

choices.text: Save FIS logs and force all actions to run before analyzing them.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to stop the experiment when the error rate exceeds the limit.

learning.reason: When an alarm specified as a stop condition for FIS enters the ALARM state, FIS stops the experiment.
learning.concept: Control whether an exercise starts and continues based on the health of the target system.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Preventing conflicts on the same item with write ownership
prompt: You use DynamoDB global tables with multi-Region eventual consistency. During normal operation, updates to the same delivery item from different Regions conflict, and one change is lost. How can you structurally prevent conflicts during normal operation while preserving the item schema and keeping the data readable from every Region?

choices.text: Use conditional updates to the same item in each Region, relying on local conditions alone to prevent simultaneous changes across all Regions.
choices.explanation: A condition evaluated locally does not lock out simultaneous changes in another Region.

choices.text: Set ConsistentRead for reads and continue accepting writes in every Region.
choices.explanation: Specifying read consistency does not prevent write conflicts on the same item.

choices.text: Assign one Region to own writes for each delivery item, and route updates from applications in other Regions to its owner.
choices.explanation: This prevents cross-Region conflicts on the same item, while replication remains available for reads.

choices.text: Use DynamoDB Streams to notify the on-call team after a conflict, without changing write routing.
choices.explanation: This detects conflicts and supports post-incident response, but does not prevent the write conflicts themselves.

learning.reason: With MREC, simultaneous changes to the same item across Regions can result in the last write winning. Assigning one write-owning Region per item removes the path to that conflict.
learning.concept: Distinguish a design that replicates data from one that arbitrates writes to the same item.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Hand Off Incomplete Work Before Instance Termination
prompt: A batch worker in an EC2 Auto Scaling group is terminated during scale-in. Stop the instance selected for termination from taking new work, return its incomplete work to the queue, and then terminate the instance. Processing time varies. Which combination should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Send lifecycle heartbeats as needed during the handoff, then call CompleteLifecycleAction when it is complete.
choices.explanation: This accommodates variable processing times and allows instance termination to proceed after a successful handoff.

choices.text: Use an EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING hook to restore work from nodes that were terminated previously.
choices.explanation: This does not let you pause the node that is about to be terminated.

choices.text: Create an autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING hook and, upon notification, stop the instance from taking new work and hand off its in-progress work.
choices.explanation: This uses the termination wait state to drain work before the instance stops.

choices.text: Enable scale-in protection permanently on all nodes and do not send a completion notification.
choices.explanation: The requested scale-in of the group will not proceed.

choices.text: Configure only the ALB deregistration delay without adding batch queue controls.
choices.explanation: This controls the draining of HTTP connections; it does not stop batch work from being received or return work to the queue.

learning.reason: The termination hook moves the instance into Terminating:Wait. Send heartbeats as needed while work is in progress, then signal completion after the handoff.
learning.concept: Allow time for termination draining while ensuring the work can be handed off before the hook times out.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Keep Baseline Capacity on On-Demand
prompt: For an ECS service on Fargate, place the first four tasks on interruption-resistant On-Demand capacity. Starting with the fifth task, distribute tasks approximately 1:3 between FARGATE and FARGATE_SPOT using the service's placement strategy. Which capacity provider strategy should you use?

choices.text: Set weight 4 for FARGATE and weight 3 for FARGATE_SPOT, with base set to 0 for both.
choices.explanation: All tasks are subject to the weights, so this does not guarantee that the first four use On-Demand capacity.

choices.text: Set base 4 for FARGATE_SPOT and weight 1 for FARGATE.
choices.explanation: The baseline capacity would be on Spot, which does not meet the interruption-resistance requirement.

choices.text: Set base 4 and weight 1 for FARGATE, and weight 3 for FARGATE_SPOT.
choices.explanation: This puts the baseline capacity on On-Demand and distributes only the additional tasks by the specified ratio.

choices.text: Set base 4 for both providers and adjust the total weight.
choices.explanation: A strategy can specify base for only one capacity provider.

learning.reason: base specifies the number of tasks to place first; after base is satisfied, weight distributes additional tasks.
learning.concept: Use separate settings for the required interruption-resistant baseline and the distribution of additional capacity.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Limit Redelivery During Long Processing and Handle Duplicates
prompt: Video processing on an SQS standard queue usually takes 1 minute, but some messages take 5 minutes. The initial visibility timeout expires while processing is still in progress, so another worker starts the same work. You want work from a stopped worker to be retried promptly. Which combination should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Set a relatively short initial visibility timeout and extend it with ChangeMessageVisibility only while you can confirm processing is continuing.
choices.explanation: This reduces duplicate work during long runs while allowing retry if the worker stops and no longer extends visibility.

choices.text: Set a fixed 12-hour visibility timeout for all messages.
choices.explanation: A stopped task would take a long time to become available for retry.

choices.text: Make processing idempotent using a processing ID, and delete the message only after committing the result.
choices.explanation: This handles redelivery on a standard queue and prevents duplicate effects if the worker stops just after committing.

choices.text: Delete the message immediately after receiving it, and use the worker's logs to determine whether processing succeeded.
choices.explanation: The message cannot be redelivered if the worker stops partway through processing.

choices.text: Increase the long polling wait time.
choices.explanation: This improves efficiency while waiting to receive messages but does not extend visibility after a message is received.

learning.reason: Extend visibility only while work is in progress, and delete the message after successful completion. Make the processing itself idempotent to account for possible duplicates on a standard queue.
learning.concept: Combine control over the time until redelivery with protection against applying results twice.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Verify Capacity After Shifting Traffic Away from a Zone
prompt: An ALB-backed service runs across three AZs, and you have enabled manual ARC zonal shift. You need to handle the current peak even when traffic is shifted away from one AZ. Capacity takes time to provision, so you cannot rely on scaling out after an incident. What should you prepare?

choices.text: Reduce capacity equally across all AZs when a zonal shift begins.
choices.explanation: This further reduces the service's available capacity after the shift.

choices.text: Pre-provision enough capacity for the remaining AZs to handle peak load regardless of which one AZ is shifted away, and verify it with load tests.
choices.explanation: The remaining AZs can handle the load even when additional capacity cannot be added after an incident.

choices.text: Fix the shift destination to one other AZ and leave the third AZ's capacity unused.
choices.explanation: This gives up usable AZ capacity without validating the required fault-tolerance condition.

choices.text: Provision only enough total capacity across all three AZs for the peak, then scale after a zonal shift.
choices.explanation: The remaining capacity cannot handle the peak, and scaling would have to complete first.

learning.reason: While an AZ is shifted away, its load moves to the remaining AZs. Operate and test with the failure-time capacity you expect to have available.
learning.concept: Validate the processing capacity that remains after a failure, rather than only the maximum capacity available under normal conditions.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Prevent duplicate processing of confirmed charges
prompt: A Step Functions task calls a payment API. Transient network interruptions can be distinguished from permanent input errors. If the response is lost immediately after the payment provider confirms a charge, you want the provider's idempotency key feature to prevent a duplicate charge. How should you configure the workflow while preserving a path to investigate failures?

choices.text: Keep retrying with States.ALL, including for permanent errors, and manually check each payment after the state machine ends.
choices.explanation: This does not branch on permanent errors or provide reconciliation when processing ends.

choices.text: Use a new payment key for every retry and track the response to each operation.
choices.explanation: The payment provider may treat each attempt as a separate transaction, so this does not prevent duplicate charges.

choices.text: Treat a missing payment response as success and continue without recording the state.
choices.explanation: This treats even an unconfirmed payment as successful and loses the reconciliation path.

choices.text: Pass a stable idempotency key, use Retry only for transient errors, and use Catch for reconciliation otherwise.
choices.explanation: This prepares for retries when the outcome is unknown while avoiding repeated attempts for permanent errors.

learning.reason: Pass a fixed idempotency key with the operation, limit Retry to transient errors, and use Catch for persistent failures or permanent errors.
learning.concept: A communication failure and whether an external system has committed an effect are not the same state.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Prevent both endpoints from being disabled at the same time
prompt: Use two Route 53 ARC routing controls to manage failover for two Regions. During an exercise or a real incident, you want to reject a state transition that would accidentally turn both controls Off, while allowing both to be On if needed. Which safety rule should you configure?

choices.text: Configure an assertion rule for both controls that requires at least one to be On.
choices.explanation: It evaluates the result of the requested operation and rejects a change that would leave both controls Off.

choices.text: Configure an assertion rule that requires both controls to be On.
choices.explanation: It would also block a valid failover to either single control.

choices.text: Only shorten the Route 53 TTL.
choices.explanation: Changing how quickly a routing change propagates does not reject an invalid state transition.

choices.text: Create a gating rule that allows an operation if either control is On beforehand, and skip checking the resulting state.
choices.explanation: Having a control On before the change does not prevent the change from leaving both controls Off.

learning.reason: An assertion rule evaluates the state after the change and can express the condition that at least one control must be On.
learning.concept: Add an invariant to the set of states allowed by an operation that changes DNS routing.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Make a recovery point usable from another account
prompt: An application in production account A, which belongs to the same AWS Organizations organization, has stopped. A recovery point exists in a standard AWS Backup vault, but the operating policy allows new compute resources to be launched only in account B. The resource supports cross-account copy, and the relevant service is available in both accounts. In what order should you recover the application?

choices.text: Notify B of only the backup plan ARN, then create an empty recovery point with the same name in B.
choices.explanation: The backup data has not been made available in B.

choices.text: Configure the destination vault's permissions and encryption in B, copy A's recovery point to B, and restore it in B.
choices.explanation: B can create resources using a recovery point in its own vault and a restore role in B.

choices.text: Give the AWS Backup tags on A's source recovery point the same values as B's tags.
choices.explanation: Tags alone do not make the recovery point usable for restoration in B.

choices.text: Add B's restore role directly to A's vault, then reference A's recovery point from B and run StartRestoreJob.
choices.explanation: A standard vault does not let you restore a recovery point directly as a resource in another account without copying it.

learning.reason: For a standard cross-account recovery, copy the recovery point to B and then restore from the recovery point in B.
learning.concept: Separate permission to copy a backup from another account from permission to restore within the destination account.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Separate request tracing from metric aggregation granularity
prompt: A payment service logs data to CloudWatch Logs in EMF and aggregates processing time by service name and environment. Investigators also want to search the logs by individual requestId. After a sudden increase in metric charges, they find that a combination containing requestId is being emitted for each request. Which change meets both requirements?

choices.text: Limit Dimensions to the service name and environment, and keep requestId as a log attribute.
choices.explanation: This supports individual tracing through log search while allowing metrics to be aggregated by service and environment.

choices.text: Remove requestId from the logs, keep environment as a metric dimension, and investigate individual requests by metric timestamps.
choices.explanation: This may reduce the cost driver, but it does not meet the requirement to find individual requests.

choices.text: Keep requestId in Dimensions and emit metrics at a lower resolution.
choices.explanation: Changing the resolution does not eliminate the separate series created for different dimension values.

choices.text: Include two EMF dimension sets: one with service name and environment, and another with requestId alone.
choices.explanation: The additional set would still create a separate series for each requestId.

learning.reason: In EMF, dimension sets determine metric series. Keeping requestId as a regular log attribute allows it to be searched while limiting the number of series.
learning.concept: Exclude high-cardinality attributes used for individual investigation from aggregation groups.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Continuously stream metrics while reducing polling
prompt: You want to send CloudWatch metrics from multiple AWS services to an external monitoring platform. The platform can receive data from Firehose, and the team currently polls each metrics API individually on a schedule. How can you continuously stream selected namespaces?

choices.text: Use a Metric Stream to select the namespaces and choose a Firehose stream that delivers data to the external monitoring platform.
choices.explanation: This continuously delivers metrics to a supported destination without maintaining individual polling processes.

choices.text: Standardize on sending CloudWatch alarm state changes through SNS.
choices.explanation: Alarm state transitions can be sent this way, but continuous metric measurements cannot.

choices.text: Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter directly on existing platform metrics.
choices.explanation: Subscription filters apply to log events; they do not forward CloudWatch metric namespaces.

choices.text: Specify the external vendor's URL in Metric Math and configure it to send the calculation results.
choices.explanation: Metric Math does not deliver data to external destinations.

learning.reason: CloudWatch Metric Streams can continuously deliver selected metrics through Firehose.
learning.concept: A metric collection path carries different information from notifications that report state changes.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Avoid paging on outliers during low-traffic periods
prompt: A CloudWatch p99 latency alarm fires on an isolated outlier during the middle of the night, when there are almost no requests. You want to keep the usual p99 statistic and threshold, and prevent the alarm state from changing during evaluation periods with too few samples to be statistically significant. What should you configure?

choices.text: Set the low-sample-count evaluation for the percentile alarm to ignore.
choices.explanation: This keeps the metric and threshold unchanged and avoids state changes due to insufficient samples.

choices.text: Only set missing data treatment to notBreaching.
choices.explanation: A data point with few samples is different from missing data.

choices.text: Change the statistic to Maximum and keep the current threshold.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to retain p99 and allows an isolated outlier to dominate.

choices.text: Disable SNS notifications while allowing the alarm state to change as before.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to prevent the alarm state from changing.

learning.reason: Setting low-sample-count evaluation for a percentile alarm to ignore suppresses state changes during periods with insufficient statistical samples.
learning.concept: Distinguish between a missing data point and a low number of samples used to calculate a statistic.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Investigate multi-account operational logs without changing where they are stored
prompt: A central SRE team needs to query CloudWatch Logs Insights across multiple application teams in the same Region. Keep the source retention settings, do not create copies of the logs centrally, and show the SRE team only log groups whose names begin with an operations prefix. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Link each source to a monitoring sink and limit sharing with a log name filter.
choices.explanation: This preserves the source storage locations and lets the central account view authorized log groups.

choices.text: Create empty log groups centrally with the same names and retention periods.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a way to query log events stored in the source accounts.

choices.text: Use a subscription for each log to replicate records to a central account log destination.
choices.explanation: This enables searching, but violates the requirement not to create another copy.

choices.text: Share only the source metrics across accounts and expect the same settings to expose source log groups.
choices.explanation: Sharing metrics alone does not share log groups.

learning.reason: CloudWatch cross-account observability connects monitoring accounts to source accounts and allows sharing to be limited by log group name.
learning.concept: Distinguish cross-account access to view logs from a storage design that creates physical copies.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Determine where a 502 was generated
prompt: When reviewing ALB access logs, you find multiple records for the same URL with an elb_status_code of 502. One record has a target_status_code of 502, while another has a hyphen. How do you distinguish an HTTP response returned by a target from an event in which the ALB did not obtain a response code from a target?

choices.text: Treat a hyphen as shorthand indicating that the target returned a successful response.
choices.explanation: It does not mean that a successful target status code was recorded.

choices.text: Conclude that the ALB did not forward a request to a target when target_status_code is present.
choices.explanation: This contradicts the fact that a target response code was recorded.

choices.text: Treat every record with an elb_status_code of 502 as a 502 returned by the target, even when target_status_code is absent.
choices.explanation: The ALB code alone cannot establish which response the target actually returned.

choices.text: Read 502 as the target's response and a hyphen as indicating that there is no target response code.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes the code sent from the ALB to the client from the code sent from the target to the ALB.

learning.reason: target_status_code indicates the response code received from a target. A hyphen means that a target response code was not recorded.
learning.concept: Even when the status code is the same, the point where it originated determines what evidence to check next.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Trace the original source through a transit path
prompt: You are analyzing VPC Flow Logs for a NAT gateway network interface. You need to distinguish the address of the transit interface itself from the source address the packet originally had. Which fields should you add to the custom format?

choices.text: Record only srcport and dstport.
choices.explanation: Port numbers do not reveal the packet’s original source IP address.

choices.text: Record srcaddr and pkt-srcaddr, then compare them.
choices.explanation: This lets you distinguish the transit address from the original packet-level address.

choices.text: Record only flow-direction and assume the source IP based on ingress.
choices.explanation: This indicates direction relative to the interface but does not record the original address.

choices.text: Reconstruct the source from action and tcp-flags.
choices.explanation: The traffic disposition and TCP flags do not provide address information.

learning.reason: pkt-srcaddr identifies the original source at the packet level and can be compared with srcaddr, which is associated with the interface.
learning.concept: Use the recorded observation fields to distinguish an intermediary’s address from the communication’s source.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Investigate an organization’s API events by principal
prompt: An organization already uses CloudTrail Lake and stores management events from multiple accounts in an event data store. During a particular time window, an incident responder needs to review configuration changes made using a specific IAM role, broken down by event name and account. How can they investigate without moving the data to a new location?

choices.text: Retrieve CloudWatch API call count metrics and reconstruct each operation from the totals.
choices.explanation: Aggregated values do not include the principal or individual operation details.

choices.text: Run SQL against the organization event data store with conditions for time, principal, and event name.
choices.explanation: This lets you centrally search existing records from multiple accounts using conditions.

choices.text: Start a new trail for the time being investigated and assume that it will automatically include past records.
choices.explanation: A new trail does not search past events that have already been ingested.

choices.text: List only the current IAM policies in each account and infer past API operations from their contents.
choices.explanation: Current permissions do not identify which operations were actually performed in the past.

learning.reason: You can query an existing event data store with SQL conditions such as event time and principal to audit recorded events.
learning.concept: Collected activity records show actual operations that cannot be inferred from current policies.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Trace latency across a queue
prompt: The order API’s publishing operation is already instrumented with X-Ray, and Lambda processes orders through SQS. You want to correlate the publisher and consumer in CloudWatch and investigate where latency occurs for each request. What should you use?

choices.text: Record Lambda concurrency metrics at one-minute intervals and use them in place of individual request traces.
choices.explanation: Concurrency aggregates do not show the processing path for a specific request.

choices.text: Enable X-Ray tracing for Lambda and inspect the linked traces for the publisher and the consumer reached through SQS.
choices.explanation: This lets you correlate instrumentation data from before and after the queue.

choices.text: Disable tracing for the publisher and measure separate requests only in Lambda.
choices.explanation: You could measure the consumer, but you could not trace its relationship to the publisher.

choices.text: Monitor only the SQS ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric to identify Lambda processing time for the order in question.
choices.explanation: A queue-wide aggregate does not identify an individual consumer operation.

learning.reason: In a supported SQS and Lambda configuration, the publisher and consumer traces are linked and can be navigated in CloudWatch.
learning.concept: A queue-wide latency metric and the processing path for one request are separate observations.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Measure availability per request without weighting time windows equally
