prompt: Traffic volumes differ greatly between weekday afternoons and late nights. The service owner checks whether 99.9% of all requests over the most recent 28 days succeeded. They do not want a low-traffic minute and a high-traffic minute to have equal weight. What should they configure in Application Signals?

choices.text: Average daily success rates with equal weight for each day.
choices.explanation: Because the number of requests varies by day, this does not equal the success rate across all requests.

choices.text: Create a request-based SLO for the proportion of successful requests and specify a 28-day rolling interval.
choices.explanation: This calculates attainment across all requests in the specified number of days, looking back from any point in time.

choices.text: Create a period-based SLO that counts each one-minute interval as a pass or fail, with a 28-day interval.
choices.explanation: This counts successful minutes individually and does not account for the number of requests in each minute.

choices.text: Evaluate a request-based SLO over calendar months.
choices.explanation: This follows calendar-month boundaries instead of the most recent 28 days.

learning.reason: A request-based SLO is evaluated by event count, and a rolling interval aggregates the specified number of days back from the present.
learning.concept: Whether the denominator is the number of periods or requests changes the evaluation when traffic varies.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Verify the purchase flow even when no one is using it
prompt: The internal sales application is in a private VPC, and actual usage is almost nonexistent at night. You want to verify every five minutes, without exposing it publicly, that a test account can sign in and complete a test order. Which approach is appropriate?

choices.text: Expose the production application to the internet and send only unauthenticated GET requests from the monitoring source.
choices.explanation: This violates the private-access requirement and does not verify the sequence of actions after sign-in.

choices.text: Change the load balancer health check to the sign-in page URL.
choices.explanation: This checks only the response from a single page; it does not verify order completion after sign-in.

choices.text: Run a Synthetics canary on a schedule inside the VPC, using a dedicated account to perform the steps.
choices.explanation: This verifies the private user flow on a schedule, regardless of actual usage.

choices.text: Set an alarm on the error rate from actual usage, and treat missing data during periods with no access as proof that the order flow worked correctly.
choices.explanation: This does not actively test the flow when there is no usage.

learning.reason: CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that support VPCs can run a scenario on a schedule in a specified network.
learning.concept: Complement monitoring based on real traffic with monitoring that actively tests the application on a schedule.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Recover per target when delivery fails
prompt: A single EventBridge rule delivers audit input to two targets. One target may reject delivery during an outage, potentially after its existing retry conditions have been exhausted. The other target is receiving events normally. Going forward, you want to inspect the failed side’s event payload and delivery error later, then recover without redelivering events to the healthy target. What should you configure?

choices.text: Increase the retry interval for the affected target and do not configure a DLQ.
choices.explanation: There is no path to retain events after retries are exhausted, so you cannot retrieve their payloads later.

choices.text: Enable an archive for the bus and replay all events from the outage period to the same rule.
choices.explanation: The time range in the archive includes successful deliveries, so events may also reach the rule’s healthy target.

choices.text: Record the rule’s failure count in CloudWatch, then reconstruct undelivered inputs from the metric’s timestamps and increments during incident response.
choices.explanation: An aggregate value does not provide the payloads of undelivered events.

choices.text: Configure a standard SQS queue as a DLQ for the failing target and allow EventBridge to send messages to it.
choices.explanation: This retains undelivered payloads and target-specific failure information, allowing you to control reprocessing for that target.

learning.reason: The per-target DLQ receives undelivered events along with the original target ARN and error information.
learning.concept: Track event-bus ingestion separately from successful delivery to each target.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Replay events only to the rules being recovered
prompt: An EventBridge archive is available. To make up for processing that stopped during an outage, you want to replay events from that 30-minute period to the original bus. You want to use only a recovery rule and avoid triggering rules owned by other teams that were operating normally. What should you configure?

choices.text: Move the recovery rule to another bus, but do not start an archive replay.
choices.explanation: No events from the outage period are delivered from the archive.

choices.text: Specify only a time range for the bus replay and leave all existing rules enabled.
choices.explanation: Events may also be delivered to healthy rules that match the same events.

choices.text: Specify the archive and time range, and set only the recovery rule’s ARN in ReplayDestination.FilterArns.
choices.explanation: This sends events back to the original bus while limiting which rules are invoked by the replay.

choices.text: Set a new retention period on the original archive, then resume normal event delivery.
choices.explanation: Changing the retention period does not replay past events.

learning.reason: For a replay, specify the event time range and use FilterArns in ReplayDestination to limit the rules.
learning.concept: When replaying past events, restrict both the time range and the destinations that may be run again.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Pause only the remediation that requires approval
prompt: An SSM Automation runbook performs steps from incident information gathering through remediation. You want information gathering to happen immediately, but you need approval from two on-call operators before remediation restarts a production instance. Which configuration prevents the restart from proceeding unless it is approved?

choices.text: Place aws:approve between information gathering and the restart, and specify the approvers and the required number of approvals.
choices.explanation: The same Automation execution record ensures that the restart happens only after the required approval is obtained.

choices.text: Use aws:sleep to pause for a set period, then always restart the instance.
choices.explanation: The passage of time does not constitute approval by the on-call operators.

choices.text: Notify operators through SNS after the restart, and track approval in email replies.
choices.explanation: The operation has already affected production by the time the notification is sent.

choices.text: Configure remediation to begin when the instance health check fails.
choices.explanation: This can detect a failure, but it does not require approval from the on-call operators.

learning.reason: aws:approve can pause subsequent steps until the specified approvers provide at least the required number of approvals.
learning.concept: Control automated information gathering and approval for production changes in the same execution record.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Centralize account impact across the organization
prompt: You want to centrally manage account-specific AWS Health events across the organization without adding notification settings to each account. During an incident, the on-call responder needs to identify the affected accounts and resources. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Collect CloudTrail management events in an organization trail and use them in place of AWS Health impact information.
choices.explanation: API audit records do not provide the list of affected accounts identified by AWS Health.

choices.text: Add more Regions to a CloudWatch dashboard without configuring account access for AWS Health.
choices.explanation: Displaying metrics from more Regions does not aggregate AWS Health events across the organization.

choices.text: Enable the AWS Health organizational view and use a central access principal to review events and affected accounts.
choices.explanation: You can understand the organization-wide impact without switching between accounts.

choices.text: Refer only to public AWS Health events and assume they affect every account in the same way.
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish the account-specific resources or impact.

learning.reason: The AWS Health organizational view aggregates account-specific events across accounts in AWS Organizations.
learning.concept: Distinguish public service health from account-specific impact within an organization.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Distinguish command acceptance from successful recovery
prompt: Step Functions calls SSM SendCommand and receives a CommandId. The next step returns the repaired node to service, but the node is not recovered when the command is merely accepted. How should you verify that the command succeeded before returning the node to service, while also setting a timeout?

choices.text: After confirming HTTP 200 from SendCommand and the CommandId in the response, record that execution on the node succeeded and return it to service.
choices.explanation: The managed node can fail after the API accepts the command.

choices.text: Retry SendCommand and return the node to service once you receive another CommandId.
choices.explanation: This confirms only that a new command was accepted; it does not verify the result of any execution.

choices.text: Wait once for slightly longer than the usual execution time, then return the node to service without checking its status.
choices.explanation: This can miss a long-running or failed execution and does not establish the status immediately before recovery.

choices.text: Poll by CommandId until a terminal status is reached, and make success the only condition for returning the node to service.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes the asynchronous execution result from the success of the start API and avoids waiting indefinitely.

learning.reason: After SendCommand is accepted, use CommandId and the target node to check the result with GetCommandInvocation. Also account for eventual consistency immediately after execution starts.
learning.concept: For asynchronous work, distinguish acceptance, execution in progress, and terminal status before proceeding.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Return partial failures while preserving FIFO order
prompt: A Lambda function processes an SQS FIFO batch containing messages from the same message group. The third message fails. You do not want to retry the completed first and second messages, but messages from the fourth onward must not be processed before the third message is retried. Which two actions should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Return only the failed ID and respond while leaving messages from the fourth onward unprocessed.
choices.explanation: An unprocessed ID that is not in the failure list is not treated as an input that needs to be retried.

choices.text: Stop processing at the first failure and include the failed ID and the IDs of subsequent unprocessed messages in batchItemFailures.
choices.explanation: This avoids completing later messages first and leaves completed IDs out of the retry set.

choices.text: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures in the event source mapping.
choices.explanation: This lets the function return only messages that have not completed.

choices.text: Throw an exception for the entire function as soon as the first message fails.
choices.explanation: The whole batch fails, causing earlier successful messages to be retried as well.

choices.text: Complete messages from the fourth onward first, then retry the third message.
choices.explanation: This violates the processing order for messages in the same group.

learning.reason: Configure partial batch responses on the event source. For FIFO, stop at the first failure and return the IDs of failed and unprocessed messages.
learning.concept: When FIFO ordering applies, return later unprocessed messages for retry as well.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Exclude a load test from normal-range learning
prompt: A CloudWatch anomaly detection model learns the usual patterns by day of week and time of day. Including last week's large-scale load test would widen the normal upper range. How can you keep using the existing day-of-week variation while preventing the model from learning from the test period?

choices.text: Replace the anomaly detection model with fixed thresholds and manage separate thresholds for each day and time period.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to keep using a model of normal variation.

choices.text: Specify the load-test time range in ExcludedTimeRanges.
choices.explanation: This excludes the specified period from training while allowing the model to use other historical data.

choices.text: Disable alarm notifications only during that period.
choices.explanation: Suppressing notifications does not prevent the metrics from being used for training.

choices.text: Shorten the alarm Period to one minute.
choices.explanation: This changes the evaluation granularity but does not exclude the load-test period from training.

learning.reason: Anomaly detection settings let you specify periods when data should be excluded from the training range.
learning.concept: Excluding observations from notifications and excluding them from training are configured separately.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Transform event correlation data into a notification
prompt: Messages sent from an EventBridge rule to the on-call SNS topic must include the original event ID, detail.operationId, and a fixed owner label. The event selection criteria are already correct, and you cannot add a dedicated transformation Lambda. What should you do?

choices.text: Hard-code an example correlation ID in the target's constant Input.
choices.explanation: This would not pass along the correlation ID from each actual event.

choices.text: Put the notification body in the event pattern and have it generate the body when a match occurs.
choices.explanation: An event pattern defines matching criteria; it does not construct the body passed to the target.

choices.text: Use InputPath to select the entire detail object and deliver it to SNS, assuming it also includes the original event ID and fixed label.
choices.explanation: A single path cannot construct an output that combines the event ID and a fixed label.

choices.text: Use an Input Transformer to extract the required values and combine them with the fixed label.
choices.explanation: It can transform values from matching events into the notification format.

learning.reason: A target's Input Transformer can map JSON paths to variables and insert them into a template that includes constants.
learning.concept: Configure event selection, notification formatting, and the destination independently.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Keep permissions granted to team-created roles within an approved boundary
prompt: You want to let a development team create its own IAM execution roles under a specific path. The team must be able to choose an identity-based policy for each workload, but permissions granted by those policies must stay within an organization-approved scope. The account is shared with other teams. Which two measures should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Restrict the development team from removing or replacing the boundary and from changing the boundary policy definition.
choices.explanation: This prevents the team from removing the limit after role creation or weakening the boundary itself.

choices.text: Restrict the path where roles can be created, and allow CreateRole with the approved permissions boundary specified by the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition.
choices.explanation: This disallows creating roles without a boundary or with a different boundary.

choices.text: Document that users should attach a session policy when they call AssumeRole, without setting an IAM boundary condition.
choices.explanation: Instructions for callers cannot enforce an upper limit on newly created roles.

choices.text: Limit principals in the role's trust policy to the team's account and delegate editing of the permissions policy.
choices.explanation: A trust policy controls who can assume the role; it does not set an upper limit on the actions the role can perform.

choices.text: Require each developer to use the approved boundary on their own identity, but make attaching a boundary to roles they create optional.
choices.explanation: A creator's boundary is not automatically inherited by newly created roles.

learning.reason: A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions available to the identity-based policies attached to a role. Require the approved boundary at creation, and do not delegate authority to remove, replace, or change its definition.
learning.concept: Treat the policy that grants a role specific actions separately from the policy that sets its maximum permissions.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Verify production deployment identity with short-term credentials
prompt: You release to production on AWS from GitHub Actions. You must not store long-term access keys, and you want to allow only tokens issued for the main branch of a specified repository in your organization. You do not use GitHub Environments. What should you configure?

choices.text: In an OIDC trust policy, restrict aud and sub to the specified repository's main branch.
choices.explanation: Only runs that satisfy these conditions can obtain short-term credentials for the role.

choices.text: Trust only the GitHub issuer and accept every token it issues.
choices.explanation: This cannot distinguish other repositories or branches.

choices.text: Include the string main in the IAM role name and leave token conditions out of the trust policy.
choices.explanation: A name does not validate where a run originated.

choices.text: Store a dedicated IAM user's access key in GitHub Secrets and configure the workflow to retrieve it only for releases from main.
choices.explanation: This still stores a long-term key and does not validate the token's origin on AWS.

learning.reason: Use a role that trusts GitHub OIDC, and validate the token's audience and repository and branch with aud and sub.
learning.concept: The trust policy validates the token's audience and origin; the permissions policy controls actions after the role is assumed.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Restrict use of unapproved Regions across the organization
prompt: For workload OUs in your organization, you want to allow creation of regional resources only in two approved Regions. Approved global services such as IAM and Route 53 must remain available, and you cannot rely only on the roles in each account. What should you configure?

choices.text: Apply a Region-restriction SCP that excludes global operations to the target OUs.
choices.explanation: This sets an upper bound on permissions in accounts in those OUs while allowing the required global services.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to detect resources in unapproved Regions and then notify the owners.
choices.explanation: Detection after creation cannot deny use of a Region at the time of the request.

choices.text: Restrict only the team's administrator role to approved Regions, and leave Region restrictions and policies for other execution roles to each team.
choices.explanation: This does not set an organization-wide limit on actions performed through other roles.

choices.text: Add only the approved Regions to the console bookmarks.
choices.explanation: Guidance in the console does not control API calls made in other Regions.

learning.reason: You can use aws:RequestedRegion as a condition for the deny. Use NotAction to limit exceptions for out-of-Region requests to the necessary global operations.
learning.concept: An SCP sets an upper bound on permissions in the member accounts it targets.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Prevent noncompliant stacks from being created
prompt: In an OU governed by Control Tower, all in-scope resource changes go through CloudFormation. You want property validation to reject resources that do not conform to approved templates before creation, without waiting for remediation afterward. Which type of control applies to the resource properties?

choices.text: Enable the applicable proactive control to evaluate compliance before resources are created or updated.
choices.explanation: This prevents resources with invalid properties from being created through CloudFormation.

choices.text: Deny all create operations in the OU, blocking compliant changes as well, with no exceptions.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to create compliant resources based on their properties.

choices.text: Change only the display format in the management console and skip template validation.
choices.explanation: This does not validate change operations or input properties.

choices.text: Enable only detective controls and remediate after receiving a noncompliance notification.
choices.explanation: This evaluates the resource after it has been created.

learning.reason: Proactive controls use CloudFormation Hooks to evaluate resource properties before creation or update.
learning.concept: Choose between responding after detection and validating resource input before it is applied.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: View account records centrally
prompt: Use AWS Config across multiple accounts and Regions in Organizations. A central auditor needs to read configuration and compliance data, but must not be able to directly change source recording settings or rules from the central account. New sources also need a process to enable recording. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Use only an organization trail in CloudTrail and treat the recorded API history as compliance data evaluated by Config.
choices.explanation: API activity history alone does not provide the compliance evaluations made by Config.

choices.text: Create a rule-administrator role in every account and have auditors sign in with it.
choices.explanation: This grants permission to change source settings when the requirement is read-only access.

choices.text: Maintain AWS Config recording in each source and create an organization multi-account, multi-Region aggregator centrally.
choices.explanation: The aggregator provides a central view of records but does not automatically change source settings.

choices.text: Start only the Config recorder in the central account to begin recording in the other accounts as well.
choices.explanation: The central recorder does not automatically start recording in other accounts and Regions.

learning.reason: A Config aggregator is a read-oriented feature that collects source configuration and compliance data; recording must be enabled at each source.
learning.concept: Separate access to the aggregated view from configuration of the sources that generate the records.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Deliver new members’ API audit events to a central destination
prompt: Continuously retain management events made by all member accounts in Organizations in a central S3 bucket across all Regions. For accounts that join in the future, you do not want to configure trails individually or give teams permission to stop them. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Create a standard account trail only in the management account and select all Regions.
choices.explanation: This does not include other member accounts, even if more Regions are added.

choices.text: Configure the required bucket policy on the logging S3 bucket and create a multi-Region organization trail.
choices.explanation: New members are included in the organization trail, and individual accounts cannot modify that trail.

choices.text: Manually export each member’s event history when events are collected.
choices.explanation: This does not automate continuous delivery or ensure coverage of new members.

choices.text: Give each team permission to write logs to a shared S3 bucket at its discretion.
choices.explanation: This does not configure a mechanism that ensures the organization’s API activity is recorded.

learning.reason: A multi-Region organization trail applies to member accounts and delivers logs to the specified S3 bucket.
learning.concept: Manage an organization trail’s collection scope separately from access permissions on its storage destination.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Separate signing and verification permissions
prompt: CI signs build artifact digests with an asymmetric AWS KMS key. An auditing application uses the same KMS key to verify signatures, but must not be able to create new signatures or change the key. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Assign the same key-administrator role to both CI and auditing.
choices.explanation: This does not restrict key-management permissions or separate responsibilities.

choices.text: For a SIGN_VERIFY key, allow kms:Sign for CI and kms:Verify for auditing.
choices.explanation: This lets the auditing role verify signatures without granting it permission to create signatures or manage the key.

choices.text: Allow kms:Sign for the same key to both execution roles and rely on the auditing application’s procedures to prevent signing.
choices.explanation: This does not remove the auditing role’s signing capability through permissions.

choices.text: Set the key usage to ENCRYPT_DECRYPT and use the encryption result as a signature.
choices.explanation: Encryption and signing serve different purposes and use different APIs; this key usage cannot verify signatures.

learning.reason: With an asymmetric key whose usage is SIGN_VERIFY, signing and verification operations can be granted to separate principals.
learning.concept: Restrict signature creation to the issuer and grant verification separately to the principals that need it.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Promote New Credentials Only After Testing Them
prompt: A Lambda function rotates credentials in Secrets Manager. After generating a new value, you want to move the new version to AWSCURRENT, which applications retrieve, only if it can actually connect to the target. What sequence should the runbook follow?

choices.text: Create AWSPENDING, set it on the target, test the target with the new value, and move AWSCURRENT only after the test succeeds.
choices.explanation: This prevents an untested value from being treated as current and keeps the previous version traceable by its label.

choices.text: Switch AWSCURRENT to the new value first, and set it on the target only if users report failures.
choices.explanation: Applications can retrieve the value before it has been verified.

choices.text: Create AWSPENDING, check only the credential format without setting it on the target, and move AWSCURRENT.
choices.explanation: This skips the required check that the value can actually connect to the target.

choices.text: Put the new value in AWSPREVIOUS and finish rotation without changing the credentials on the target.
choices.explanation: The new value is neither applied to the target nor tested for connectivity.

learning.reason: Follow createSecret, setSecret, testSecret, and finishSecret in that order, moving the current label only after the test.
learning.concept: Manage the label for the rotation candidate separately from the current label used by applications.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Reflect New Vulnerability Findings for Existing Images
prompt: Running ECR images are updated weekly. When new vulnerability information is published, you want to obtain findings for repositories under continuous monitoring without pushing the images again. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Use basic scanning with scan-on-push and evaluate images only when their tags are updated.
choices.explanation: This does not configure ongoing reassessment in response to new information.

choices.text: Enable ECR enhanced scanning and include the relevant repositories in continuous scanning.
choices.explanation: While an image remains in scope for monitoring, findings can be updated in response to new vulnerabilities.

choices.text: Make ECR image tags immutable and disable scanning after publication.
choices.explanation: Preventing version changes is separate from updating findings for an image.

choices.text: Shorten the image retention period and do not notify teams about vulnerabilities found before expiration.
choices.explanation: Changing retention does not replace evaluation and notification.

learning.reason: Enhanced scanning integrates with Amazon Inspector and reassesses images in continuous scanning in response to new vulnerability information.
learning.concept: Both a new image and newly discovered vulnerabilities can trigger ongoing evaluation.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Prioritize Findings for Critical Resources Before Notification
prompt: The operations team creates notifications from Security Hub CSPM findings. When new or updated findings for specified production resources arrive with HIGH severity, the team wants to raise only those findings themselves to CRITICAL. An existing EventBridge rule uses the updated severity for notifications. What should you configure? EventBridge

choices.text: Group findings by severity in Insights.
choices.explanation: Insights can group findings, but they do not change the severity of individual findings.

choices.text: Use an EventBridge Input Transformer to display CRITICAL only in the notification body. EventBridge
choices.explanation: This changes the notification text, but not the finding value in Security Hub CSPM.

choices.text: Create an automation rule that matches the resource ID and original HIGH severity, then changes the severity to CRITICAL.
choices.explanation: This updates only the specified findings before notification.

choices.text: Add a Critical tag to the target resources without creating a Security Hub CSPM rule.
choices.explanation: A tag alone does not define the condition and action needed to change the severity of a finding.

learning.reason: A Security Hub CSPM automation rule changes the severity of findings that match its criteria. The EventBridge rule can evaluate the updated value after the configured rule is applied.
learning.concept: Distinguish updating an attribute on the finding itself from sending a notification after receiving the finding.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Distribute Rules and Remediation Settings Together Across an Organization
prompt: Config recording is enabled in multiple accounts. You want to distribute shared Config rules and their corresponding remediation settings from one template, then update them centrally when policies change. Which configuration also prevents member accounts from individually changing the deployed definitions?

choices.text: Use only an SCP to describe the shared evaluation criteria and automatic remediation procedures.
choices.explanation: An SCP sets a ceiling on API permissions; it does not define Config evaluations or remediation actions.

choices.text: Create a Config aggregator and configure it to distribute any new rules to all accounts.
choices.explanation: An aggregator collects data; it does not deploy rules and remediation settings.

choices.text: Manually create rules with the same names in multiple accounts, and leave remediation settings to each team.
choices.explanation: This does not provide repeatable deployment from a shared template.

choices.text: Deploy an organization conformance pack containing the rules and remediation settings to the target Regions.
choices.explanation: An organization conformance pack distributes Config rules and remediation actions from a single template and can be updated centrally. Member accounts where it has been deployed cannot individually modify the distributed rules and remediation actions.

learning.reason: An organization conformance pack distributes Config rules and remediation actions from a single template and can be updated centrally. Member accounts where it has been deployed cannot individually modify the distributed rules and remediation actions.
learning.concept: Separate distributing configuration across the organization from reading compliance results after deployment.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Apply Rotated Secrets Without Waiting for Another Deployment
prompt: A Lambda function resolves a database password from a CloudFormation Secrets Manager dynamic reference and receives it as an environment variable. After the password is rotated, the function must use the current value for new connections without waiting for a stack update. How should this be changed?

choices.text: Pin the existing version ID in the dynamic reference.
choices.explanation: The function would always use the pinned version.

choices.text: Set the plaintext password as the template default and update it manually each time.
choices.explanation: This does not handle rotation independently, and the password remains in the template.

choices.text: Use the same dynamic reference for the environment variable and configure the Lambda environment variable to update when Secrets Manager changes the value.
choices.explanation: Changing the secret does not cause the deployed resource property to be resolved again.

choices.text: Allow read access to the execution role and retrieve the current value at runtime.
choices.explanation: The function can use the rotated value independently of stack updates.

learning.reason: Dynamic references are resolved when a resource is created or updated. They do not retrieve the value again at runtime.
learning.concept: The identifier for a secret and the timing of updates to its current value are different.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Restrict Build S3 Access to Buckets in the Organization
prompt: Traffic from the dedicated CodeBuild subnets to S3 can pass only through a gateway endpoint. Multiple buckets in accounts within the organization must be allowed, including buckets added in the future, while access to buckets outside the organization through this route must be denied. What should be configured?

choices.text: Restrict the source of access to the organization using only aws:PrincipalOrgID.
choices.explanation: Even if the caller belongs to the organization, the target bucket could be owned by another organization.

choices.text: Use the S3 managed prefix list as the route destination and treat a matching destination IP as proof that a bucket belongs to the organization.
choices.explanation: The S3 destination network range does not identify the organization that owns a bucket.

choices.text: Restrict aws:ResourceOrgID to the organization in the S3 endpoint policy.
choices.explanation: This allows only resources owned by the correct organization to use this S3 route.

choices.text: Configure S3 Block Public Access only on existing buckets in the organization.
choices.explanation: This does not control the caller's permissions or route when accessing buckets outside the organization.

learning.reason: aws:ResourceOrgID can compare the organization of the account that owns an S3 resource. The endpoint policy restricts which resources can use the endpoint.
learning.concept: Evaluate the organization of the principal and that of the destination resource separately.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Avoid Building for Unrelated Changes in a Monorepo
prompt: A CodePipeline V2 pipeline for the API is triggered from GitHub's main branch. It should process only pushes that change files under services/api/ or libs/shared/. Which configuration creates no execution history for changes limited to docs/?

choices.text: Configure the pipeline to run on every push to main and set a duration constraint on the deploy stage.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate changed files; the duration is checked after the pipeline starts.

choices.text: Define a push trigger for docs/ only, then invert the check in the build.
choices.explanation: A push that changes only an API path would not trigger the pipeline.

choices.text: Include main and both target paths in the push trigger for the connection source.
choices.explanation: The trigger evaluates the target branch and file paths.

choices.text: Always start the pipeline from the source and have the first CodeBuild step inspect changed paths and end processing.
choices.explanation: This can shorten the build, but an unnecessary pipeline execution still occurs.

learning.reason: The trigger evaluates the target branch and file paths.
learning.concept: Filtering events before they start prevents unnecessary executions.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Resume from the Failure Without Repeating Successful Builds
prompt: One of several actions in a deploy stage failed because a temporary dependency was unavailable. Which operation recovers using the same execution and input artifacts, without rerunning actions that succeeded in that stage?

choices.text: Restart the pipeline from the latest source.
choices.explanation: This creates a different execution, and the source content may also have changed.

choices.text: Roll back the stage to its last successful state and start a new deployment as a separate execution.
choices.explanation: This does not resume the failed action in the execution being recovered with the same input.

choices.text: Retry only the failed action in the failed stage of that execution.
choices.explanation: This uses the input associated with the execution and preserves the actions that succeeded in the stage.

choices.text: Retry all actions in the stage in the same execution.
choices.explanation: This reruns actions that already succeeded.

learning.reason: This uses the input associated with the execution and preserves the actions that succeeded in the stage.
learning.concept: Choosing the retry unit avoids repeating side effects that have already completed.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Run a pipeline with a previously approved commit
prompt: In a CodePipeline V2 pipeline that uses a connection, the tip of main has moved on to prepare the next release. To reproduce a production incident, you need to use a compatible earlier commit for one run only. How can you start the run without changing the trigger or main?

choices.text: If a stage in the earlier run succeeded, choose to retry the failed action.
choices.explanation: This does not start a single new run with the specified commit.

choices.text: Start the run with a revision override of COMMIT_ID on the source action.
choices.explanation: You can select the target commit for an individual run.

choices.text: Put the old SHA in a CodeBuild environment variable and let the source action retrieve the latest revision.
choices.explanation: The source artifact's revision does not change unless an implementation uses that variable.

choices.text: Force-update the source branch to the earlier commit, then restore it after starting the pipeline.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to avoid changing the tip and may affect triggers in the meantime.

learning.reason: You can select the target commit for an individual run.
learning.concept: Distinguish a permanent change to the pipeline definition from specifying a source revision for a single run.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Pass a build-determined value to a later action
prompt: A package identifier is determined during a CodeBuild build. You want to reference it in a later action's configuration without creating a new artifact file or adding a script to read one. What should you specify?

choices.text: Give a source action variable the same name as the identifier and reference its value from before the change.
choices.explanation: A value determined during the build is not reflected in a variable from the preceding source action.

choices.text: Write the value to the build log and enter the same variable name directly in the later action.
choices.explanation: Writing to the log does not pass a value into an action's configuration.

choices.text: Specify exported-variables in the buildspec and reference the value from a later action through a namespace.
choices.explanation: The value determined by the build is made available to later CodePipeline actions.

choices.text: Export a variable in the CodeBuild shell and read it from a later action under the same environment variable name, without using a namespace.
choices.explanation: Each action has a separate execution environment, and shell variables do not cross process boundaries.

learning.reason: The value determined by the build is made available to later CodePipeline actions.
learning.concept: When passing a value obtained at runtime to a later action, distinguish the build's local environment from the pipeline namespace.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Clean up a temporary environment even when a test fails
prompt: You start a temporary container in CodeBuild to run integration tests. If a test command fails partway through, you still need to collect logs in the same phase and stop the container. The build must remain failed when a test fails. Which buildspec structure is appropriate?

choices.text: Put the tests in commands and log collection and shutdown in finally in the same phase.
choices.explanation: finally runs even if a failure in commands stops the remaining commands.

choices.text: List all operations in commands and end the same phase before running anything that follows if a command fails.
choices.explanation: The phase ends before logs are collected and the container is stopped.

choices.text: Put container shutdown and log collection in an action in a later stage that receives a successful build artifact.
choices.explanation: On failure, the pipeline does not proceed to that stage, and its environment is separate from the temporary container's.

choices.text: Convert the test command's failure status to success, then collect logs in the next command.
choices.explanation: This allows cleanup to continue, but the original test failure is not reflected in the build result.

learning.reason: finally runs even if a failure in commands stops the remaining commands.
learning.concept: Separate control that preserves the main operation's result from cleanup that must always run.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Separate outputs by purpose in one build
prompt: A CodePipeline has one CodeBuild action. You want to pass a Linux distribution package and a Lambda ZIP from that action as separate outputs to two later deployment actions. How should you configure this without running two builds?

choices.text: Make each identifier in secondary-artifacts match an output name in the pipeline.
choices.explanation: This binds separate outputs from the same build.

choices.text: Write both to S3 in sequence under the same file name and have the later actions refer to the same key.
choices.explanation: The second write overwrites the object, so the two distribution packages cannot be distinguished.

choices.text: Specify two output names as environment variables and use artifacts to combine the generated files into one default ZIP.
choices.explanation: The files cannot be passed as separate outputs after the build.

choices.text: Put both files in one ZIP and configure the same ZIP as the input to each deployment action.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement for each action to receive its own artifact directly.

learning.reason: This binds separate outputs from the same build.
learning.concept: Map pipeline output names to artifact identifiers in the buildspec so inputs can be passed according to their purpose.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Reduce startup delays for frequent short builds
prompt: A team runs short CodeBuild builds every few minutes during business hours in a supported Linux environment. The command duration for each build is stable, but startup delays exceed the target. The cost of keeping capacity reserved at all times is acceptable. Which change directly reduces the wait time?

choices.text: Shorten the retention period for build logs to speed up image preparation.
choices.explanation: Log retention is unrelated to reserving the execution environment in advance.

choices.text: Double the CPU for on-demand builds and start the same image each time.
choices.explanation: This can improve processing performance, but it does not provide a pre-provisioned startup path.

choices.text: Associate the project with a provisioned CodeBuild capacity fleet.
choices.explanation: This reserves available warm capacity and can reduce the need to prepare a new environment for every build.

choices.text: Increase the timeout so builds do not fail when startup takes longer.
choices.explanation: Reducing the chance of failure does not shorten startup time.

learning.reason: This reserves available warm capacity and can reduce the need to prepare a new environment for every build.
learning.concept: Measure the speed of compute resources during execution separately from the time spent preparing the execution environment.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Minimize information exposed in public build status
prompt: A public SDK needs to display only recent build status. You can create a separate project whose build project name and latest status may be public, while keeping internal build logs and artifacts access-controlled. Which configuration meets this goal?

choices.text: Enable build badges for the project intended for public display and show the badge URL.
choices.explanation: A badge displays build status without granting access to detailed logs or artifacts.

choices.text: Make CloudWatch Logs public and ask readers to find the latest completion line in the README.
choices.explanation: This exposes internal build logs just to show the status.

choices.text: Make the artifact bucket public and use updated files as a substitute for status.
choices.explanation: This exposes the artifacts and does not directly show whether the build succeeded or failed.

choices.text: Make the internal project a public build project and link to the public build details in the README.
choices.explanation: This exposes more than just the status.

learning.reason: A badge displays build status without granting access to detailed logs or artifacts.
learning.concept: Control publication of status independently from permissions to access logs and results.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Maintain the required fleet size during an in-place update
prompt: An in-place CodeDeploy update is being performed across 20 EC2 instances. Keep at least 16 healthy during the update, regardless of Availability Zone, and update as many instances as possible while maintaining that level. Apply the same proportion if the fleet size changes in the future, rather than using a fixed minimum count. What should you configure?

choices.text: Set the minimum number of healthy hosts to 16 in a custom deployment configuration.
choices.explanation: This works for the current fleet size, but does not meet the requirement to keep the same 80% in the future.

choices.text: Use CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime and set the Auto Scaling minimum capacity to 16.
choices.explanation: The group's minimum capacity does not control the percentage of healthy hosts during an update.

choices.text: Set the minimum healthy hosts to 80% of the fleet in a custom deployment configuration.
choices.explanation: The same proportion will apply when the fleet size changes.

choices.text: Use CodeDeployDefault.AllAtOnce and only shorten the load balancer's health check interval.
choices.explanation: This does not limit how many hosts can be taken out of service at once during the update.

learning.reason: The same proportion will apply when the fleet size changes.
learning.concept: Choose in-place update concurrency based on the minimum number of healthy hosts required during deployment.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Identify overwritten S3 inputs by execution
prompt: Build archives are repeatedly delivered to the same S3 key. When using it as a CodePipeline S3 source, you want to identify which update to that key was used by the object version. What must the source bucket have?

choices.text: Change the S3 storage class and use the filename as the execution ID without versioning the key.
choices.explanation: This cannot uniquely identify multiple contents stored under the same key.

choices.text: Overwrite the same path and rely only on the previous day's S3 Inventory listing to determine the input for an execution.
choices.explanation: A daily inventory listing cannot specify the version for an S3 source.

choices.text: Enable S3 Versioning on the source bucket and specify the archive key in the source action.
choices.explanation: This is required for a CodePipeline S3 source and distinguishes inputs under the same key by version.

choices.text: Encrypt the source and use the SSE-KMS key ID as the upload version number.
choices.explanation: The encryption key ID is not an identifier for the uploaded generation.

learning.reason: This is required for a CodePipeline S3 source and distinguishes inputs under the same key by version.
learning.concept: When the same key is overwritten, the key name alone cannot identify the contents of a release input.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Automating published function versions
prompt: Lambda is updated from a SAM package. The API is configured with a fixed live alias ARN, and each template update that changes the function code should publish a new version and advance the alias when the application is released. A gradual rollout is not needed this time. What should you specify?

choices.text: Pin the API to a numbered version ARN and manually update the API configuration for each release.
choices.explanation: This does not use a fixed live alias.

choices.text: Set AutoPublishAlias to live on the SAM function and connect the API to that alias.
choices.explanation: SAM manages the versions and alias.

choices.text: Set the function's reserved concurrency so that each change generates a new published version.
choices.explanation: A concurrency setting does not publish a version.

choices.text: Connect the API to the unqualified function ARN and define neither published versions nor an alias.
choices.explanation: Even though the invocation path uses a fixed name, it does not use published versions.

learning.reason: SAM manages the versions and alias.
learning.concept: Separate changing versions from the fixed name presented to callers.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Using one tag for architecture-specific images
prompt: The same application is distributed to x86_64 and ARM64 hosts. Each executable image has already been built, and the deployment side should specify the same repository and release tag. How should you store the images in ECR?

choices.text: Push each image and apply the release tag to a manifest list that references both.
choices.explanation: The same reference can select the image for the runtime environment.

choices.text: Store only the ARM image and configure ECR to generate the x86 binaries when the image is pushed.
choices.explanation: The registry does not recompile binaries.

choices.text: Push each platform's image under the same tag in sequence, overwriting it each time.
choices.explanation: Only the last image pushed will be referenced by the tag.

choices.text: Assign a separate tag to each image and manually select the platform for every deployment.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to specify a single tag.

learning.reason: The same reference can select the image for the runtime environment.
learning.concept: Separate the release tag from the platform-specific image it resolves to.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Making past releases available from another Region
prompt: Enable cross-Region replication for ECR today. The production recovery destination must be able to retrieve future images and the two past versions that existed before replication was configured. What should you do?

choices.text: Push only new releases after configuration and wait for all older images to be replicated in the background.
choices.explanation: Existing images are not migrated by configuration alone.

choices.text: Create only repositories with the same names in the recovery destination and list the past version tags in the release procedure.
choices.explanation: Matching repository and tag names does not make the image data available there.

choices.text: Extend the retention period at the source and assume that retrieving an image from the recovery destination will automatically place the same image there.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle settings do not trigger cross-Region copying.

choices.text: New pushes after replication is configured are copied automatically. Copy the two existing versions separately and verify the digests in both Regions.
choices.explanation: Images that existed before configuration are not replicated retroactively.

learning.reason: Images that existed before configuration are not replicated retroactively.
learning.concept: Distinguish changes covered after replication is enabled from migration of existing data.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Matching package authentication to a role session
prompt: The CI temporary role has a 30-minute expiration. You want to avoid a design in which a CodeArtifact authentication token remains usable after the role session ends, and make the token's validity match the remaining session time when it is issued. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Set the longest expiration and remove the value from the CodeBuild environment variable.
choices.explanation: Removing it locally does not shorten the validity period of an issued token.

choices.text: Issue the CodeArtifact token for its default duration and treat its expiration as matching the end of the role session.
choices.explanation: The default CodeArtifact token duration is not tied to the session duration.

choices.text: Use duration-seconds of 0 when retrieving the token with the assumed role.
choices.explanation: The expiration then matches the remaining role session time.

choices.text: Always set the token expiration to 30 minutes and ignore the remaining session time.
choices.explanation: If issued partway through the session, the token could remain valid after the session ends.

learning.reason: The expiration then matches the remaining role session time.
learning.concept: When a token issued with temporary credentials has its own expiration, configure both durations.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Use commit history and tags during a build
prompt: Artifacts imported into CodePipeline from a connection source are inspected by CodeBuild. Generating the release number requires commit history and tags, but the default ZIP does not include Git history. What should you change without adding credentials outside the pipeline? Select TWO.

choices.text: Add the source branch name as an environment variable and infer the history from the ZIP filename.
choices.explanation: The original commit history and tags are not included.

choices.text: Keep the connection output as a ZIP and initialize it with git init after extraction.
choices.explanation: Initializing a new repository does not restore the original history.

choices.text: Make the CodeBuild output an S3 artifact and extend the log retention period without changing the input.
choices.explanation: Changing the output destination does not add Git metadata to the input.

choices.text: Set the connection source output format to Full clone.
choices.explanation: This outputs a reference from the connection that provides Git information instead of a ZIP.

choices.text: Add permission to use the connection to the CodeBuild role.
choices.explanation: The build can use the supplied reference to retrieve the repository.

learning.reason: Output a connection reference that provides Git information instead of a ZIP. The build can use the supplied reference to retrieve the repository.
learning.concept: A file snapshot and a source reference that can retrieve its history are different output formats.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Set separate limits for queue wait and build runtime
prompt: A high volume of concurrent requests to CodeBuild causes some builds to wait 15 minutes before starting. You want a build to fail if no capacity is available after waiting 10 minutes, but once it starts, it needs 40 minutes to run tests. Which time limits should you set?

choices.text: Set the execution limit to 40 minutes and have a script check the queue wait time after the build starts.
choices.explanation: This cannot end the wait at the 10-minute mark.

choices.text: Set only the execution limit to 10 minutes and leave the queue limit at its default.
choices.explanation: The required 40-minute test would be interrupted, and the 10-minute wait limit would not be configured.

choices.text: Set the queue limit to 10 minutes and the build execution limit to at least 40 minutes.
choices.explanation: The time before a build starts and its runtime can be limited separately.

choices.text: Set the queue limit to 40 minutes and reduce concurrency to control the wait.
choices.explanation: This does not limit the wait to 10 minutes, and reducing concurrency could worsen congestion.

learning.reason: The time before a build starts and its runtime can be limited separately.
learning.concept: Queue wait time and runtime after a build starts are controlled by independent limits.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Close the production stage entrance while keeping upstream checks running
prompt: While investigating a production incident, you need to stop new executions from entering the production stage of CodePipeline. Builds and tests from new commits, as well as deployments to the validation environment, must continue. Executions already inside the production stage have been handled separately. Which action should you take?

choices.text: Stop only the one execution currently shown and leave the entrance configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not stop another execution triggered by the next commit from reaching the stage.

choices.text: Disable the inbound transition for the production stage.
choices.explanation: This keeps upstream processing running while preventing new executions from entering production.

choices.text: Disable the inbound transition for the stage after production.
choices.explanation: This does not prevent executions from entering the production stage.

choices.text: Disable source change detection to stop all new pipeline executions.
choices.explanation: This would also stop builds and updates to the validation environment.

learning.reason: This keeps upstream processing running while preventing new executions from entering production.
learning.concept: Use the stage entrance control to block new arrivals, and handle executions already in progress separately.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Resume a failed update rollback
prompt: A CloudFormation rollback stopped because an IAM role lacked permission, leaving the stack in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED. The required permission can be restored. You want to return to a consistent state from before the change and then release again. What sequence should you follow?

choices.text: Retry UpdateStack on the failed stack with the new template version.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the failed rollback state.

choices.text: Change only the resources to their previous names outside the stack service.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the CloudFormation rollback state.

choices.text: Skip all failed resources without fixing the cause, then apply the new version.
choices.explanation: Skipping can leave differences between the actual resources and the template that must be reconciled before the next update.

choices.text: Fix the role's permissions, then use ContinueUpdateRollback to complete the original rollback.
choices.explanation: After the cause is fixed, you can continue the failed rollback.

learning.reason: After the cause is fixed, you can continue the failed rollback.
learning.concept: When the cause of a stopped rollback can be fixed, recover without leaving discrepancies by skipping resources.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Wait for EC2 initialization to succeed before proceeding
prompt: After creating a new EC2 instance, UserData prepares its configuration and dependencies. Because the prerequisites are not ready when the instance reaches the running state, you want CloudFormation to wait for initialization to succeed before proceeding with downstream resources. Which methods should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Send the initialization result from UserData to CloudFormation with cfn-signal.
choices.explanation: This reports whether initialization succeeded, not merely whether the instance started.

choices.text: Set a CreationPolicy with ResourceSignal on the instance.
choices.explanation: You can specify the required number of signals and a timeout for CloudFormation.

choices.text: Record a fixed wait time in the runbook and assume creation will finish during that period.
choices.explanation: The stack cannot distinguish a failed configuration from a successful one.

choices.text: Set only DependsOn on downstream resources, without signaling when UserData finishes.
choices.explanation: This specifies creation order but does not tell CloudFormation whether UserData succeeded.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain and wait for an initialization response.
choices.explanation: This attribute determines how the old resource is handled during replacement; it does not configure an initialization wait.

learning.reason: CloudFormation can be configured with the required number of signals and a timeout. The signal reports whether initialization succeeded, not merely whether the instance started.
learning.concept: Use a separate signal for the instance state and the application initialization result.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Distribute a shared configuration as a reusable template component
prompt: Each team uses an independent CloudFormation stack. Operations wants to package shared definitions for a log group, retention, and encryption as a single unit, and have each template refer to an organization-approved version by one logical name. They do not want a child stack dedicated to the component. What should they do?

choices.text: Use StackSets to deploy the same stack to every team at once and eliminate each team's independent configuration.
choices.explanation: This does not make the component available for adoption from each existing template.

choices.text: Register the shared definition as a CloudFormation module and reference the module type in each consuming template.
choices.explanation: An approved pattern can be reused as a definition within each stack.

choices.text: Copy the Nested Stack URL and create a dedicated child stack from every stack.
choices.explanation: This enables reuse, but violates the requirement not to create a child stack.

choices.text: Distribute complete templates to each team and have them copy the same resource definitions every time.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a versioned shared component that teams can reference.

learning.reason: An approved pattern can be reused as a definition within each stack.
learning.concept: Distinguish the version of a template component that combines multiple resources from the boundary of the stack that gets created.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Separate pipeline permissions from resource creation permissions
prompt: An application team's pipeline should be allowed to update a specific stack. Permissions to create the IAM and VPC resources in that stack must be limited to CloudFormation execution; the pipeline must not call the individual APIs directly. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Allow the pipeline role to manage IAM and VPC resources, and let CloudFormation use that role's permissions.
choices.explanation: The pipeline could also call the relevant APIs directly.

choices.text: Enable termination protection on the stack, then give the team a shared administrator role.
choices.explanation: Termination protection does not restrict direct resource API calls.

choices.text: List only the physical names of each resource in the pipeline's resource policy.
choices.explanation: This does not specify the service role CloudFormation uses.

choices.text: Assign a dedicated service role to the stack and limit the pipeline's permissions to stack operations and the necessary role handoff.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation executes the APIs for the target resources.

learning.reason: CloudFormation executes the APIs for the target resources.
learning.concept: Separate the principal that operates the stack from the principal that accesses resources on the stack's behalf.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Measure the impact of hooks before enforcing them
prompt: A custom CloudFormation hook checks internal standards when resources are created or updated. During the first week, you want violations to be visible but do not want to reject updates from existing teams. You also need to be able to switch to rejection the following week. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Leave the hook disabled and check only the number of successful stack creations.
choices.explanation: Violations detected by the hook will not be recorded.

choices.text: Set the hook to FAIL from the first week and have teams with violations retry the same update.
choices.explanation: Their updates will still fail during the first week as long as the cause remains.

choices.text: Replace the hook with drift detection and do not register a hook for create or update operations later.
choices.explanation: This does not check declared resource configurations before provisioning.

choices.text: Introduce the hook in WARN mode, review the warnings, and then switch it to FAIL.
choices.explanation: This applies the same check in stages without blocking updates for violations during the first week.

learning.reason: This applies the same check in stages without blocking updates for violations during the first week.
learning.concept: Configure the hook's check separately from whether its result blocks provisioning.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Keep environment lookups consistent between development and CI during synthesis
prompt: CDK performs a VPC lookup during synthesis. Immediately after the account state changes, the local environment and CI select different VPCs. Which approach versions the lookup results so they can be updated and reviewed only when intended?

choices.text: Store the synthesized template in a bucket, but continue performing the lookup on every run in both development and CI.
choices.explanation: Updates to the lookup results are not subject to review.

choices.text: Always clear the context when CI starts and look up the account again each time.
choices.explanation: This still allows local and CI runs to incorporate different states.

choices.text: Include cdk.context.json in the source and explicitly refresh the relevant context.
choices.explanation: This pins lookup results during synthesis so changes can be reviewed as a diff.

choices.text: Record the VPC name in a local environment variable and remove it from the CI environment.
choices.explanation: The synthesis inputs cannot be shared.

learning.reason: This pins lookup results during synthesis so changes can be reviewed as a diff.
learning.concept: Treat environment information used during synthesis as an input to template generation.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Apply a cross-cutting check to existing constructs
prompt: A CDK app uses many internal constructs. You want synthesis to check the encryption configuration of S3 buckets created under a stack, without repeating the same check in each construct's production code. What should you use?

choices.text: Manually register each bucket name in the stack's Outputs, then inspect the list only at runtime.
choices.explanation: This skips application before synthesis and also requires per-resource registration.

choices.text: Write the same check in each bucket's production code and copy it whenever a bucket is added.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement for a reusable cross-cutting check.

choices.text: Add tags to the CDK bootstrap stack and treat every bucket as encrypted.
choices.explanation: Tags on a different stack do not check the target resources' configuration.

choices.text: Add an Aspect to the root stack and inspect the configuration of the target nodes.
choices.explanation: An Aspect can traverse constructs in the specified scope and apply a shared check.

learning.reason: An Aspect can traverse constructs in the specified scope and apply a shared check.
learning.concept: Applying a cross-cutting policy to the construct tree separates resource definitions from consistency checks.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Read central configuration from another account without duplicating it
prompt: A non-sensitive application setting managed in one account is retrieved by an application in another account through the Parameter Store API. Which configuration avoids maintaining a copy of the value and lets you manage IAM appropriately on the retrieving side?

choices.text: Make the full parameter list in the central account public, and let consumers select by key name.
choices.explanation: This does not scope sharing to specific parameters or provide the identifier needed for an API reference from another account.

choices.text: Share an Advanced parameter using AWS RAM, and retrieve it from the consumer account by its full parameter ARN.
choices.explanation: The owner maintains one value, and consumers can reference the shared setting.

choices.text: Create a parameter with the same key in the other account and assume that it syncs automatically when the central value changes.
choices.explanation: Parameters with the same name in different accounts do not sync automatically.

choices.text: Export a Standard parameter to S3 and copy it to Parameter Store in the other account every day.
choices.explanation: This requires operating a copy and does not reference the central value directly.

learning.reason: The owner maintains one value, and consumers can reference the shared setting.
learning.concept: When configuration owners and consumers differ, consider both the sharing mechanism and read authorization.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Pin patch selection across multiple batches to the same point in time
prompt: Outside a maintenance window, you use AWS-RunPatchBaseline in multiple Run Commands. If new patches meet the approval criteria during the process, you still want the same patch list applied to this group of nodes, which uses the same baseline. What should you specify?

choices.text: Specify the same Snapshot ID in each command outside the window, and apply it while the snapshot is valid.
choices.explanation: This lets the commands use the snapshot of approved patches for the same baseline.

choices.text: Use the same patch-targeting tags, but do not align when each command generates its patch list.
choices.explanation: Settings that narrow the target nodes do not pin the approved patch list.

choices.text: Generate a different Snapshot ID for each command and specify only the same baseline name.
choices.explanation: This does not ensure the commands use the approved patch list from the same point in time.

choices.text: Standardize the nodes on the same AMI before deployment, then have each node retrieve the latest patches independently.
choices.explanation: The starting image is consistent, but the evaluation time for the patches to apply is not pinned.

learning.reason: This lets the commands use the snapshot of approved patches for the same baseline.
learning.concept: Even with the same baseline rules, the patches selected can vary depending on when they are evaluated.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Reevaluate parameters from the original template
prompt: CloudFormation uses AWS::LanguageExtensions. A list parameter was updated, but the previous list remained when the option to use the existing template was selected. How can you have the macro regenerate resource definitions from the current input?

choices.text: Run drift detection only and add new resource definitions from the current input.
choices.explanation: Drift detection does not transform or update the template.

choices.text: Resubmit the original template and provide the new parameter value when updating.
choices.explanation: The transform can reevaluate expressions using the new input.

choices.text: Specify the existing transformed template and assume its old literals will be rewritten automatically.
choices.explanation: The reused template contains the previous literal values.

choices.text: Rerun the previous change set to apply the parameter change.
choices.explanation: Content already processed previously is not regenerated from new input.

learning.reason: The transform can reevaluate expressions using the new input.
learning.concept: Distinguish the template before transformation from the transformed result, in which expressions have been replaced with literal values.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Allow time to observe after the rollout completes
prompt: You are deploying a new configuration progressively with AWS AppConfig over 20 minutes. After it reaches all targets, you also want to monitor an existing CloudWatch alarm for 10 minutes and automatically revert to the previous configuration if an issue occurs. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Use the environment alarm only for SNS notifications and end the deployment as soon as it reaches all targets.
choices.explanation: Notifications alone do not configure final observation or automatic rollback.

choices.text: Set the deployment duration to 30 minutes, delay the end of the progressive rollout, and set the bake time to 0.
choices.explanation: This provides no 10-minute observation period after all targets are reached.

choices.text: Validate the configuration syntax with a validator and do not associate an alarm with the environment.
choices.explanation: Even valid syntax cannot make post-deployment impact a condition for automatic rollback.

choices.text: Set the deployment duration to 20 minutes and the final bake time to 10 minutes, and associate the monitoring alarm with the environment.
choices.explanation: This ties issues during both the progressive deployment and final observation to rollback.

learning.reason: This ties issues during both the progressive deployment and final observation to rollback.
learning.concept: Distinguish the time spent increasing deployment coverage from the time spent checking stability after all targets receive the configuration.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Evaluate configuration rules declaratively
prompt: You need to evaluate a configuration condition that is not covered by an AWS Config managed rule. The condition can be evaluated using only the target resource's configuration items, and you do not want to maintain a scheduled Lambda function or a custom execution role. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Use CloudFormation termination protection to restrict resource creation without evaluating whether existing resources are compliant.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate configuration changes to resources in operation.

choices.text: Set a condition expression only on the aggregator and stop evaluations in each source account.
choices.explanation: An aggregator collects configuration and compliance data; it does not run the target rule.

choices.text: Create an AWS Config custom policy rule with the condition expressed in Guard.
choices.explanation: Config can perform declarative evaluations in response to configuration changes.

choices.text: Create an AWS Config custom Lambda rule and operate the same function and role in every account.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid maintaining a custom function and permissions.

learning.reason: Config can perform declarative evaluations in response to configuration changes.
learning.concept: When a decision can be made entirely from recorded configuration items, it can be implemented without maintaining an external evaluation program.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Account for defaults in newly added accounts
prompt: An OU uses StackSets automatic deployments. You override the retention period to 90 days for one existing account. A different account that later joins the same OU receives the template's default of 30 days. What explains this?

choices.text: Automatic deployments average the overrides from existing accounts, so 30 days was set as a weighted average.
choices.explanation: There is no aggregation of override values like this.

choices.text: Changing the Region order causes existing account overrides to be inherited by new accounts.
choices.explanation: Region order and account-specific parameter overrides are separate.

choices.text: When an account joins the OU, CloudFormation removes the retention period setting and uses only each service's default.
choices.explanation: New stack instances use the StackSet default.

choices.text: Parameter overrides on existing instances are not inherited by accounts that join later.
choices.explanation: New instances are created using the StackSet default value.

learning.reason: New instances are created using the StackSet default value.
learning.concept: Distinguish the StackSet default from a value overridden for a specific stack instance.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Distribute reads without overloading the write path
