prompt: An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster has a writer and two DB instances that can serve reads. Keep the write path as it is, and distribute new dashboard connections across the read instances. How should the connections be routed?

choices.text: Switch both reads and writes to the reader endpoint.
choices.explanation: The reader endpoint normally routes connections to read-only instances.

choices.text: Use the writer endpoint for writes and the reader endpoint for the dashboard.
choices.explanation: New read connections can be distributed across the reader instances.

choices.text: Keep all connections on the writer endpoint and have the dashboard send only SELECT statements.
choices.explanation: Even when the SQL is read-only, the connection still goes to the writer.

choices.text: Pin the dashboard to one instance endpoint and let RDS handle the distribution.
choices.explanation: This pins connections to a specific instance; it does not distribute them across multiple readers.

learning.reason: New read connections can be distributed across the reader instances.
learning.concept: Choose DB cluster endpoints according to the workload and availability role.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Understand what remains at the destination after a deletion
prompt: A prefix in a versioned S3 bucket is replicated to another Region. The rule enables replication of delete markers created by users. A user then deletes a specific source version by specifying its VersionId. What is the effect on the destination?

choices.text: The deletion that specifies a VersionId is not replicated, so the corresponding version already created at the destination remains.
choices.explanation: Replicating delete markers does not replicate the permanent deletion of a specific version.

choices.text: The specific-version deletion is reflected at the destination and removes all versions of the same key.
choices.explanation: An operation that includes a deleted version ID is not replicated this way.

choices.text: A delete marker is first added only at the destination for every version of the replicated object.
choices.explanation: This operation differs from a regular DELETE that adds a marker.

choices.text: A deletion that specifies a VersionId is replicated if versioning is Enabled at the destination.
choices.explanation: This deletion operation is outside replication even when versioning is enabled.

learning.reason: Replicating delete markers does not replicate the permanent deletion of a specific version.
learning.concept: A logical delete marker and an operation that physically deletes a specific version are different.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Access shared files from each AZ without crossing zones
prompt: An EC2 application in three AZs reads and writes the same shared file system. If a zone failure makes one connection endpoint unavailable, EC2 instances in the remaining AZs must still use the same data through a local endpoint in each AZ. How should this be configured? Select 2.

choices.text: Use a Regional EFS file system as the storage-class prerequisite.
choices.explanation: The same file system's data can be used across multiple AZs.

choices.text: Create EFS One Zone in one AZ and mount it from EC2 instances in the other AZs as well.
choices.explanation: The shared data remains dependent on the original AZ if that AZ fails.

choices.text: Create Regional EFS, but place a mount target in only one AZ.
choices.explanation: The other AZs cannot use independent local connection endpoints.

choices.text: Place a mount target for the file system in each AZ where the application runs.
choices.explanation: Each active AZ can have its own local connection endpoint.

choices.text: Create separate EBS volumes in each AZ and mount them all under the same name.
choices.explanation: Writes cannot be shared as one file system.

learning.reason: The same file system's data can be used across multiple AZs. Each active AZ can have its own local connection endpoint.
learning.concept: Design both the file system's availability across the Region and the connection interface in each AZ.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Spread replicas of the same application across multiple AZs
prompt: EKS nodes are in three AZs, but immediately after deployment, Pods for the same workload are concentrated in one AZ. You want the Pods distributed across AZs that have available nodes, and you want a Pod to remain unscheduled if the difference in Pod counts exceeds 1. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Use a node selector to specify one AZ, then increase the Deployment replicas to distribute them evenly, at most one per AZ.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve concentration in the specified zone.

choices.text: Configure topologySpreadConstraints to spread Pods by zone, with maxSkew 1 and DoNotSchedule.
choices.explanation: This applies a distribution constraint to Pods in the same workload.

choices.text: Specify only a PodDisruptionBudget, without defining Pod placement.
choices.explanation: Controlling voluntary disruptions does not determine the initial placement across zones.

choices.text: Set only the Deployment's maxUnavailable, without a zone key.
choices.explanation: This controls how many Pods can be unavailable during a rolling update, but does not spread them evenly across AZs.

learning.reason: This applies a distribution constraint to Pods in the same workload.
learning.concept: Configure node group placement and Pod scheduling constraints separately.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Preserving the Pod disruption budget during a node update
prompt: An update to an EKS managed node group stopped with PodEvictionFailure. The target Deployment has three healthy replicas, and the PDB's minAvailable is also 3. An additional replica can start on another node. What is the appropriate recovery action?

choices.text: Increase placement capacity and the replica count to allow enough Pods to be evicted, then retry the normal update.
choices.explanation: Pods can be moved while satisfying the PDB constraint.

choices.text: Force the update, expecting EKS to adjust it within the number of evictions allowed by the PDB.
choices.explanation: A forced update can terminate Pods while ignoring the PDB constraint.

choices.text: Directly delete the Pods running on the node and do not retry the EKS update.
choices.explanation: This does not complete a PDB-compliant eviction and node group update.

choices.text: Delete the PDB and leave the service's permitted downtime undefined until the node update finishes.
choices.explanation: The service contract must still be honored during the update.

learning.reason: Pods can be moved while satisfying the PDB constraint.
learning.concept: Consider update parallelism separately from the number of unavailable replicas the application can tolerate.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Promoting a cache writer during an outage
prompt: You run node-based Valkey on ElastiCache in a non-cluster-mode replication group. If the primary's AZ becomes unavailable, the application must resume writes without waiting for an operator to promote a replica. Which two measures should you combine?

choices.text: Pin the original node's IP address as the write destination.
choices.explanation: The application will keep connecting to the original destination even after promotion.

choices.text: Use Multi-AZ with a replica in another AZ and enable automatic failover.
choices.explanation: A viable replica is promoted when the primary fails.

choices.text: Use the read endpoint for all writes.
choices.explanation: A read endpoint does not represent the writer role.

choices.text: Have the application use the primary endpoint and re-resolve it and reconnect after failover.
choices.explanation: The application can reconnect to the promoted writer.

choices.text: Place replicas only in the same AZ and promote one if the entire AZ becomes unavailable.
choices.explanation: The stated failure affects both the primary and its replicas.

learning.reason: A viable replica is promoted when the primary fails. The application can reconnect to the promoted writer.
learning.concept: Check cross-AZ replication, promotion behavior, and the endpoint the application uses.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Restoring to just before a damaging change
prompt: An accidental operation updated production data in RDS for PostgreSQL. The database is within the automated backup retention period. You want to restore the state from just before the change to a separate instance, validate it, and decide whether to cut over while keeping the existing database intact. What should you use?

choices.text: Change the current DB instance's class to restore the data from before the change.
choices.explanation: Changing compute capacity does not restore a previous data state.

choices.text: Restore only the oldest manual snapshot and cut over immediately without checking the differences.
choices.explanation: This neither selects the relevant point in time nor validates the restored database before cutover.

choices.text: Perform a Multi-AZ failover and assume the synchronized copy is still at the state from just before the accidental change.
choices.explanation: High-availability replication does not restore data to an arbitrary point before an accidental change.

choices.text: Use PITR to restore a new DB instance to a point just before the change, validate its contents, and then change the endpoint.
choices.explanation: This lets you inspect a copy from the specified point in time without overwriting the original database in place.

learning.reason: This lets you inspect a copy from the specified point in time without overwriting the original database in place.
learning.concept: Treat validation of restored data and switching the production endpoint as separate operations.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Preventing one queue from exhausting shared capacity
prompt: The same Lambda function is invoked by two standard SQS queues with different priorities. The low-priority queue can see a surge during an outage. You want to limit only the low-priority queue's concurrent function invocations, without changing the high-priority queue's event source mapping. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Change only the low-priority SQS batch size to 1.
choices.explanation: This reduces the number of messages per invocation but does not cap the number of concurrent invocations.

choices.text: Lower the function's reserved concurrency for the low-priority queue and leave the high-priority queue's existing event source configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: This limits all invocations of the function and also affects the high-priority queue.

choices.text: Set MaximumConcurrency only on the low-priority event source.
choices.explanation: This caps concurrent invocations for the selected SQS source only.

choices.text: Increase the message retention period for the high-priority SQS queue.
choices.explanation: Changing how long messages are retained does not limit concurrency from the low-priority queue.

learning.reason: This caps concurrent invocations for the selected SQS source only.
learning.concept: Function-wide capacity allocation and the concurrency allowed from each event source can be configured separately.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Switch DNS responses based on load balancer health
prompt: Expose ALBs in two Regions under the same application name in Route 53. Normally, respond only with the primary, and return the secondary if the ALB in the primary Region becomes unhealthy. You do not want to create a separate internet-facing health check; instead, use the ALB's health status. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Register both ALBs as alias records with equal weights, and do not evaluate target group health.
choices.explanation: This does not define primary preference under normal conditions or failover when it becomes unhealthy.

choices.text: Use failover alias records and enable Evaluate Target Health.
choices.explanation: This uses the ALB's health status and prefers the healthy primary.

choices.text: Use latency records to return the Region with the lowest latency, and disable health evaluation.
choices.explanation: This selects based on distance and does not detect failures.

choices.text: Assign a name only to the primary and use a short TTL as a substitute for health evaluation.
choices.explanation: This shortens the response cache time but cannot select the secondary.

learning.reason: Use the ALB's health status and prefer the healthy primary.
learning.concept: Combine DNS routing priorities with health evaluation of the alias target.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Pause an AMI refresh at checkpoints
prompt: Replace the instances in the same Auto Scaling group with a new AMI. Pause for 10 minutes of observation each time the replacement percentage reaches 20% and 50%. The individual warm-up settings after health checks are already configured. What should you add?

choices.text: Extend only the post-initialization warm-up uniformly by 10 minutes for every instance, without configuring pauses by progress percentage.
choices.explanation: This only waits for each individual launch and does not specify inspection points at 20% and 50%.

choices.text: Set the minimum healthy percentage to 20% and the maximum healthy percentage to 50%.
choices.explanation: Healthy percentages are distinct from replacement progress and do not configure the requested checkpoints.

choices.text: Suspend new launches in Auto Scaling and have a person calculate the replacement percentage before starting the refresh.
choices.explanation: This does not define observation points during the automatic replacement process.

choices.text: Set Instance Refresh checkpoints to 20% and 50%, with a 10-minute delay.
choices.explanation: This pauses additional replacements at the specified progress points.

learning.reason: This pauses additional replacements at the specified progress points.
learning.concept: Distinguish per-instance preparation time from checks performed at checkpoints in the overall replacement progress.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Prevent a small number of bad inputs from failing the entire batch
prompt: A Standard Step Functions workflow processes 200,000 records from S3 using a Distributed Map. Some bad records should remain as failed child executions, and the parent workflow should fail the batch if the failure rate exceeds 1%. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Limit Map MaxConcurrency to an appropriate number of parallel executions, and use the same field to determine the number of failures that can be exceeded.
choices.explanation: This setting controls concurrency; it does not evaluate the failure rate.

choices.text: Retry every child an unlimited number of times and allow the parent to succeed only if every record succeeds.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to finish while leaving a small number of bad inputs as failures.

choices.text: Set ToleratedFailurePercentage to 1 and handle the error raised when the threshold is exceeded.
choices.explanation: This preserves item-level failures and lets the parent use the failure rate in its decision.

choices.text: Replace each child error with success and let the parent finish without using the failure count.
choices.explanation: The parent cannot correctly evaluate the child failure rate.

learning.reason: This preserves item-level failures and lets the parent use the failure rate in its decision.
learning.concept: Distinguish individual item outcomes from the failure rate allowed for the batch as a whole.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Find a correlation ID efficiently across large volumes of logs
prompt: You often investigate JSON logs in the Standard log class after the fact by specifying the same transactionId. You want to reduce the amount of data scanned for equality searches over logs ingested in the future, without changing the retention period. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Remove transactionId during log ingestion and investigate using only the event timestamp.
choices.explanation: This loses the correlation key needed to trace the same operation accurately.

choices.text: Apply sort first in each query, then filter by transactionId.
choices.explanation: Specifying display order does not eliminate the need to read the original logs.

choices.text: Create a metric filter that records the count for each transactionId, and leave Logs Insights as a full-text search.
choices.explanation: Aggregating counts does not limit the scope scanned by a log query.

choices.text: Create a field index for transactionId and search using an equality condition on that value.
choices.explanation: The index can reduce scanning of log events that are unrelated to the search.

learning.reason: The index can reduce scanning of log events that are unrelated to the search.
learning.concept: Indexing fields used in equality searches can reduce the need to read all logs each time.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Record zero when there are no errors
prompt: Application logs arrive every minute, and a metric filter matches only when ERROR appears. No dimensions are used. You want a data point reporting zero errors for minutes that contain only routine logs. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Set the value for a match to 1 and the filter's default value to 0.
choices.explanation: This records zero during intervals with log input but no matches.

choices.text: Leave the filter's default value unset and set the alarm's missing-data treatment to notBreaching.
choices.explanation: This changes how the alarm evaluates missing data, but it does not emit a zero-valued data point.

choices.text: Set the value for an ERROR match to 0 and the value for logs without ERROR to 1.
choices.explanation: This reverses the requirement to count each error as 1.

choices.text: Shorten the retention period so that counts for periods with deleted logs become zero.
choices.explanation: The retention setting does not cause the filter to emit zero.

learning.reason: This records zero during intervals with log input but no matches.
learning.concept: Distinguish between receiving input with no matches and receiving no log input at all.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Monitor the error rate as traffic changes
prompt: You have a series representing the ALB's RequestCount for requests for which it selected a target, and a series representing the number of target 5xx errors. RequestCount is positive during the period being measured. You want an alarm for the percentage of 5xx errors relative to requests in the same period, rather than the absolute error count. What should you use?

choices.text: Use Metric Math to calculate the percentage from the 5xx count and request count, using the same period and statistic for both.
choices.explanation: This evaluates service quality on the same scale even as the total number of requests changes.

choices.text: Combine two threshold alarms with an AND in a composite alarm.
choices.explanation: Logical operations on alarm states cannot calculate the ratio of two measurements.

choices.text: Use the maximum request count and average 5xx count from separate periods to calculate a ratio.
choices.explanation: The denominator and numerator would not represent counts from the same observation window.

choices.text: Alarm only on the 5xx count and set a fixed threshold based on average weekday traffic.
choices.explanation: This does not use the actual request count for each evaluation period.

learning.reason: This evaluates service quality on the same scale even as the total number of requests changes.
learning.concept: When turning independent counters into a rate, use aggregates from the same time window.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Change the log class without losing required search features
prompt: You ingest infrequently accessed logs into an Essentials (formerly Infrequent Access) log group. You need to retain the existing group, and future logs now need to be investigated as they arrive using CloudWatch Logs Live Tail. Which change should you make?

choices.text: Create a new Standard log group that supports Live Tail and direct future log output to it.
choices.explanation: This lets you use Live Tail for new logs while retaining existing logs.

choices.text: Export the logs to S3 and open new objects directly with CloudWatch Logs Live Tail.
choices.explanation: Live Tail is a feature for supported CloudWatch log groups; it does not open S3 objects directly.

choices.text: Assign the Standard class to only some of the logs stored in the current group.
choices.explanation: The class is not a setting that can be assigned to individual events.

choices.text: Change the retention period for the current log group and update its class to Standard at the same time.
choices.explanation: You cannot change the class of a log group after it has been created.

learning.reason: This lets you use Live Tail for new logs while retaining existing logs.
learning.concept: A log group's class cannot be changed after creation, and available features vary by class.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Restrict access to personal information even during incident investigations
prompt: New logs ingested into CloudWatch Logs Standard contain email addresses. You want routine investigators to see masked values and only a designated investigation role to view the originals when needed. What should you configure?

choices.text: Encrypt the log group with KMS and leave Logs Insights users with the same viewing permissions.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest alone does not mask part of a query result.

choices.text: Hide the email column in a standard query template and retain users' permissions to view raw logs.
choices.explanation: Users could see the original values in queries that do not use the template.

choices.text: Mask the data with a data protection policy and allow only the required investigation role to use logs:Unmask.
choices.explanation: This masks data in routine views and lets you control exception access individually.

choices.text: Completely delete email addresses in the application and let the investigation role unmask them when needed.
choices.explanation: The values cannot be unmasked later because they were never stored.

learning.reason: This masks data in routine views and lets you control exception access individually.
learning.concept: Separate permission to send logs from permission to display ingested sensitive data in unmasked form.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Continuously deliver logs instead of exporting them daily
prompt: You want to send each application log that enters CloudWatch Logs Standard to a central S3 bucket for long-term retention within a few minutes. You also want Firehose buffering before delivery. What should you configure to replace the daily export?

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch Metric Stream and select the log group name as the namespace.
choices.explanation: A Metric Stream delivers metrics, not log content.

choices.text: Use a subscription filter on the log group to deliver logs to Firehose, then store them in S3.
choices.explanation: This continuously forwards ingested logs, and Firehose can buffer and store them.

choices.text: Download only the aggregated CSV results from Logs Insights every hour.
choices.explanation: This does not continuously deliver all logs or retain their original content.

choices.text: Change the same group's Export task from daily to weekly and extend the retention period in S3.
choices.explanation: This makes the delivery interval even longer and does not meet the requirement to deliver logs within minutes of ingestion.

learning.reason: This continuously forwards ingested logs, and Firehose can buffer and store them.
learning.concept: An export that batches retained logs is a different path from one that streams newly ingested logs.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Correlate cluster health with Pod status
prompt: During an EKS incident, standard EC2 metrics cannot identify Pod restarts or CPU and memory usage at the container level. You want to monitor the corresponding cluster systematically through CloudWatch, with the required permissions configured. What should you do?

choices.text: Overwrite all workload logs at a single S3 key and treat the update rate as a Pod resource.
choices.explanation: The log storage method alone does not provide resource consumption inside containers.

choices.text: Enable detailed EC2 monitoring and use instance CPU alone to allocate usage to each Pod.
choices.explanation: EC2 measurements do not include resource consumption per Pod.

choices.text: Use Container Insights with the CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on.
choices.explanation: It sends detailed EKS hierarchy and container-level observability data to CloudWatch.

choices.text: Enable collection of EKS CloudTrail management events and aggregate management API call history as container-level usage.
choices.explanation: Auditing management API calls does not reveal container runtime status.

learning.reason: It sends detailed EKS hierarchy and container-level observability data to CloudWatch.
learning.concept: Infrastructure instance metrics and orchestrator or container metrics have different levels of granularity.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Measure EC2 memory and operating system utilization
prompt: EC2's standard CloudWatch metrics include CPU and network metrics. This task requires memory utilization for each Linux server and utilization of its working filesystem. What is the most direct way to add these operating system metrics?

choices.text: Use the ALB's active connection count as a substitute for both memory and disk alarms.
choices.explanation: Connection counts cannot measure the resource utilization of each operating system.

choices.text: Collect guest memory and disk utilization with CloudWatch Agent.
choices.explanation: It can publish guest operating system measurements to CloudWatch.

choices.text: Infer used filesystem space from EBS volume IOPS.
choices.explanation: The number of I/O operations is not filesystem utilization.

choices.text: Enable detailed monitoring for EC2 standard metrics to increase the frequency of CPU and network measurements.
choices.explanation: Changing the measurement frequency does not add guest memory utilization.

learning.reason: It can publish guest operating system measurements to CloudWatch.
learning.concept: Distinguish hypervisor-level measurements from guest operating system resource information.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Set separate retention periods for short-term search and long-term storage
prompt: In CloudWatch Logs, you need to be able to search directly only for the most recent 30 days. The S3 copy, which is already being delivered continuously, must be retained for 365 days for audits. How can you automatically apply both retention periods while controlling costs? Select two.

choices.text: Set a lifecycle rule on the S3 audit prefix to expire objects after 365 days.
choices.explanation: This manages the expiration of the audit copy independently of CloudWatch Logs.

choices.text: Delete both CloudWatch Logs and S3 data after 30 days, then retrieve older data when needed.
choices.explanation: This loses the long-term retention required for audits.

choices.text: Set the log group's retention period in CloudWatch Logs to 30 days.
choices.explanation: This retains searchable logs for the required period.

choices.text: Set CloudWatch Logs retention to 30 days and assume that S3 data will also be deleted automatically after 365 days.
choices.explanation: The destinations are independent, so the original retention setting is not inherited by S3.

choices.text: Retain both indefinitely, then have an operator check the dates and delete data at year-end.
choices.explanation: This does not provide automated 30-day control for the searchable layer or 365-day retention control.

learning.reason: This retains searchable logs for the required period. Manage the expiration of the audit copy independently of CloudWatch Logs.
learning.concept: Retention must be configured separately for the searchable observability layer and the storage layer.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Audit specific data read operations
prompt: CloudTrail is recording management events, but you cannot determine who retrieved objects from an S3 bucket containing customer data. Going forward, the requirement is to collect only reads under a specific prefix at the API level. What should you configure?

choices.text: Generate S3 Inventory daily and reconstruct read history from the list of existing objects.
choices.explanation: An inventory list does not record past GetObject requests.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail data events for the target S3 objects, with prefix and read conditions.
choices.explanation: This records object operations such as GetObject within the specified scope.

choices.text: Add write management events so that object reads are included as well.
choices.explanation: Management events do not automatically include object-level operations.

choices.text: Store only the CloudWatch BytesDownloaded metric and aggregate it as the caller of API requests.
choices.explanation: A data-transfer metric cannot identify the principal and object involved in each operation.

learning.reason: This records object operations such as GetObject within the specified scope.
learning.concept: Distinguish auditing API calls that change bucket configuration from auditing API calls that operate on the objects themselves.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Evaluate nonconsecutive breaches within the same window
prompt: You want to monitor an error-rate metric collected every minute. Trigger an alarm if it exceeds the threshold three times in the last five minutes. The breaches do not need to be consecutive. Missing-data treatment is configured separately. How should you specify this?

choices.text: Set Period to 1 minute and set EvaluationPeriods and DatapointsToAlarm to 3.
choices.explanation: This requires a breach in all three most recent data points and does not use a five-minute window.

choices.text: Set Period to 1 minute, EvaluationPeriods to 5, and DatapointsToAlarm to 5.
choices.explanation: This requires breaches in all five data points, rather than the required three.

choices.text: Set Period to 1 minute, EvaluationPeriods to 5, and DatapointsToAlarm to 3.
choices.explanation: This evaluates whether three of the five most recent data points breach the threshold.

choices.text: Set Period to 5 minutes and compare the threshold with one five-minute average data point.
choices.explanation: This does not count breaches in each one-minute data point.

learning.reason: This evaluates whether three of the five most recent data points breach the threshold.
learning.concept: Configure the number of data points evaluated independently from the number that must breach the threshold.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Track alarms as operational work
prompt: On-call responders want to manage ownership and related AWS resources for a series of events identified by CloudWatch alarms in the same operations view. A one-time SNS notification does not preserve handoff status. What should they use?

choices.text: Associate the alarm with the creation of an OpsItem in OpsCenter.
choices.explanation: Responders can track it as an operational item that includes the affected resource and related information.

choices.text: Register the on-call team's email address with SNS and edit the existing subscription status when each event is resolved.
choices.explanation: Subscription status is different from the response status of an individual incident.

choices.text: Extend the metric retention period and use data point values to record who is responsible for the response.
choices.explanation: Measurements do not record work status or related resources.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to record only changes to alarm settings, not the incidents.
choices.explanation: Auditing alarm configuration does not create a work item for the issue being handled.

learning.reason: Responders can track it as an operational item that includes the affected resource and related information.
learning.concept: Distinguish notification delivery from a work record that maintains response status.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Retry only events that failed in a partially failed submission
prompt: You sent multiple events to an existing bus using EventBridge PutEvents. The response was HTTP 200, but it included retryable errors for individual entries. How can you resend the failed entries without deliberately resending entries that succeeded?

choices.text: Treat all inputs as successful if the response is HTTP 200, and consider the failed entries processed.
choices.explanation: This ignores individual errors in the batch response.

choices.text: Always resend the entire original batch if even one entry fails.
choices.explanation: This resends successful inputs too, so duplicates cannot be avoided.

choices.text: Check the target's DLQ and conclude that no retry is needed for each failed submission.
choices.explanation: An input that failed at the publishing stage never reached the target.

choices.text: Match each response entry to the original input in order, then send only the retryable failures.
choices.explanation: This lets you retry entries that failed while excluding successful entries.

learning.reason: This lets you retry entries that failed while excluding successful entries.
learning.concept: Distinguish the batch API's response code from the outcome of each individual input.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Gradually redrive messages from a DLQ after fixing the consumer
prompt: You fixed a defect in a standard SQS consumer. A large number of messages have accumulated in the DLQ. You want to return them gradually to the repaired source queue and check that they do not overwhelm current input. Which recovery methods should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Extend the source queue's retention period so that old messages in the DLQ are returned automatically.
choices.explanation: Changing retention does not start a redrive from the DLQ.

choices.text: Delete the DLQ and wait for the source queue to read the original messages again.
choices.explanation: This loses the input stored in the DLQ.

choices.text: Increase the source queue's visibility timeout and connect the DLQ as the original input.
choices.explanation: Changing visibility does not control redelivery or its rate for existing DLQ messages.

choices.text: Set a cap on the custom message delivery rate based on available processing capacity.
choices.explanation: This redrives messages at a rate the system can handle alongside existing input.

choices.text: Start a DLQ redrive task and set the recovered source queue as its destination.
choices.explanation: This returns the failed input to the same processing system.

learning.reason: Return the original failed input to the same processing system, and redrive it at a rate the system can handle alongside existing input.
learning.concept: Control the recovery destination and the load caused by redrive separately.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Run an approved follow-up once
prompt: After an incident, start a state machine exactly once at a time chosen by the responder. Do not add a standing recurring rule, allow delay within a flexible window such as 15 minutes, and automatically clean up the schedule after it completes. Which settings should you use?

choices.text: Keep a daily cron rule at the same time indefinitely, and have the state machine decide which days are unnecessary.
choices.explanation: This continues unnecessary executions and does not provide a one-time schedule with automatic cleanup.

choices.text: Set the SQS retention period to the planned execution time and use message deletion as the signal to start the state machine.
choices.explanation: This does not define a path that starts the state machine when the message expires.

choices.text: Specify an at expression and a 15-minute FlexibleTimeWindow, assume it will start in the same minute, and have a responder delete the completed schedule.
choices.explanation: The start time can vary within that window.

choices.text: Specify an at expression, set FlexibleTimeWindow to OFF, and set ActionAfterCompletion to DELETE.
choices.explanation: These settings suit a one-time invocation and remove the schedule after it is no longer needed.

learning.reason: These settings suit a one-time invocation and remove the schedule after it is no longer needed.
learning.concept: A one-time schedule, execution-time flexibility, and post-completion cleanup can each be configured separately.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Keep a state pending until an external recovery completion notice arrives
prompt: A Standard Step Functions workflow creates an internal recovery ticket. Several hours later, a coordinating Lambda in the same account will report that the ticket is complete. You want to avoid polling and resume the original execution when the work is complete. What should you use?

choices.text: Wait using waitForTaskToken, then call SendTaskSuccess when the work is complete.
choices.explanation: The token associates the waiting task with the external completion.

choices.text: Start a new state machine execution every minute and automatically replace the previous execution.
choices.explanation: This does not resume the original execution when completion is reported.

choices.text: Use a Request Response integration and pass the HTTP 200 response confirming ticket creation to the next step as a report that recovery is already complete.
choices.explanation: Ticket acceptance and actual recovery are different events.

choices.text: Always add the same one-hour Wait after creating the ticket.
choices.explanation: The resume time is not tied to when the work actually completes.

learning.reason: The token associates the waiting task with the external completion.
learning.concept: Distinguish the response that starts work, completion of the external work, and resumption of the workflow.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Recover an instance after a physical host failure
prompt: In EC2, process monitoring inside the OS is healthy, but StatusCheckFailed_System has detected an infrastructure failure. The instance type supports action-based recovery. How should you recover the instance while retaining its instance ID and other attributes?

choices.text: Send a notification based on CPUUtilization and save only the application logs when the alarm goes off.
choices.explanation: This does not configure instance recovery triggered by the relevant status check.

choices.text: Configure an EC2 recovery action on an alarm for StatusCheckFailed_System.
choices.explanation: The action can move the corresponding instance to different hardware while preserving attributes such as its instance ID.

choices.text: Restart OS processes based on StatusCheckFailed_Instance and use the same recovery for an infrastructure check failure.
choices.explanation: Guest-level actions alone do not recover the infrastructure host.

choices.text: Terminate the original EC2 instance, create another from an AMI, and expect it to have the same instance ID.
choices.explanation: A recreated instance has a different instance ID.

learning.reason: The action can move the corresponding instance to different hardware while preserving attributes such as its instance ID.
learning.concept: The appropriate status check and recovery action differ for guest OS problems and infrastructure host failures.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Preventing an S3 index from reverting because of a delayed notification
prompt: An application receives S3 PUT and DELETE notifications through SQS and updates a search index for each key. Notifications for the same key can arrive out of order. How can it prevent an older notification from reverting the index after a newer operation has been applied?

choices.text: Record the time each notification is received from the queue and always apply the operation from the most recently received notification.
choices.explanation: The order in which notifications are received does not necessarily match the order of operations in S3, so an older operation could be applied later.

choices.text: Order S3 VersionId values as strings and apply the operation with the largest value to the index as the latest operation.
choices.explanation: VersionId identifies a version; it is not a value for comparing the chronological order of operations.

choices.text: Keep the last sequencer for each key and update the index only for a larger value.
choices.explanation: Compare sequencers for the same key as hexadecimal numbers, and make the update conditional on the previous value to prevent an older notification from reverting the index.

choices.text: Compare all buckets using a single sequencer and process only the largest value, including across different keys.
choices.explanation: Sequencers can be used to compare order only for the same object key.

learning.reason: Compare sequencers for the same key as hexadecimal numbers, and make the update conditional on the previous value to prevent an older notification from reverting the index.
learning.concept: Distinguish the order of operations on the same key from the order in which notifications are received from the queue.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Remediating in specified accounts from a central control plane
prompt: From Systems Manager Automation in a central account, run the same approved runbook in accounts in a specific OU. Do not distribute the central account's long-term credentials to all accounts, and limit the actual operations in each target account to the permissions needed. What should you prepare? Select TWO.

choices.text: Store each account administrator's access key in the central runbook.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement not to distribute long-term credentials.

choices.text: Give members in every account permission to edit the central runbook.
choices.explanation: This does not define the delegation needed for remote execution or the permissions in the target accounts.

choices.text: Create an Automation administration role in the central account and specify the target accounts and Regions.
choices.explanation: The central execution can orchestrate Automation within the specified scope.

choices.text: In the target accounts, provide least-privilege execution roles that the central administration role can use.
choices.explanation: This limits operations to the permissions of the target accounts.

choices.text: Create only the central administration role, without configuring a trust relationship or execution role on the target side.
choices.explanation: This does not provide permissions for the runbook's operations in the target accounts.

learning.reason: The central execution can orchestrate Automation within the specified scope. The operations can be limited to the permissions of the target accounts.
learning.concept: Separate delegation for the central account that directs the work from the roles that actually operate on resources in each target account.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Routing messages without losing those filtered out
prompt: An EventBridge Pipes pipe reads an SQS queue containing several types of messages and processes only one type. Messages used by another team's process did not reach a target and were also deleted from the source queue. Which design can process every type going forward?

choices.text: Enable only a target dead-letter queue (DLQ) and handle all nonmatching input as though it will be sent there.
choices.explanation: A filter mismatch is not a target delivery failure.

choices.text: Create another pipe that reads the same SQS queue and assume that nonmatching input will remain until it matches the condition of one of the pipes.
choices.explanation: A message that does not match can be deleted regardless of which pipe receives it first.

choices.text: Increase the source queue's visibility timeout and wait for nonmatching messages to reappear eventually.
choices.explanation: Nonmatching messages are deleted; they do not simply remain hidden.

choices.text: Have the publisher send each message type to a separate queue, and have each pipe read its own queue.
choices.explanation: An SQS source deletes messages that do not match its filter, so separate the messages before consumption to retain input for other uses.

learning.reason: An SQS source deletes messages that do not match its filter, so separate the messages before consumption to retain input for other uses.
learning.concept: Choose between filtering while consuming from a queue and routing messages by use before they are consumed.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Temporarily suspending automatic remediation for approved exceptions
prompt: Continue evaluating a Config rule across all buckets. For one bucket used by a legacy integration, temporarily stop automatic remediation until an approved expiration date, while recording it as noncompliant and continuing remediation as before for other buckets. What should you configure?

choices.text: Register a time-limited remediation exception for the rule and bucket combination.
choices.explanation: This preserves evaluation and exempts only remediation for that resource.

choices.text: Exclude the bucket from evaluation by the rule so that remediation is not triggered.
choices.explanation: This also prevents the noncompliant evaluation result from being recorded.

choices.text: Disable automatic remediation for the entire rule and handle other buckets manually until the approved expiration date.
choices.explanation: The exception affects a broader scope than required.

choices.text: Temporarily remove the bucket from Config history and record it again when the expiration date arrives.
choices.explanation: This interrupts evaluation and compromises the existing record for the resource.

learning.reason: This preserves evaluation and exempts only remediation for that resource.
learning.concept: Excluding a resource from compliance evaluation is different from making an exception only for remediation when the resource is noncompliant.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Detect permissions granted to resources outside the organization
prompt: You manage S3 and KMS resource policies in two Regions. Sharing within the same AWS Organizations organization is approved, so you want to detect only unintended sharing with entities outside the organization. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Create an external access analyzer in each applicable Region, with the organization as its trusted zone.
choices.explanation: It reports policy permissions on supported resources that cross the organization boundary.

choices.text: Set each account as its own trusted zone and report all sharing with other organization members as external.
choices.explanation: This includes sharing within the organization and uses a different trust boundary from the one requested.

choices.text: Configure an analyzer that detects only permissions not used within the organization.
choices.explanation: Detecting unused identity permissions is different from detecting external access granted by resource policies.

choices.text: Call an account policy validation API once in only one Region.
choices.explanation: This does not continuously monitor resource sharing in both Regions.

learning.reason: It reports policy permissions on supported resources that cross the organization boundary.
learning.concept: The analyzer's trusted zone determines which entities it treats as external.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Check IAM policies before applying them
prompt: A CI pipeline receives IAM identity policy JSON in a pull request. Before deployment, it must report AWS policy grammar findings and practical recommendations, not just syntax errors. What should it run without granting permissions to real resources?

choices.text: Validate the policy as an identity policy with IAM Access Analyzer's ValidatePolicy.
choices.explanation: It returns findings based on AWS policy grammar and recommendations before the policy is applied.

choices.text: Evaluate a single API call with the Policy Simulator and use that as a check of the entire policy's grammar and recommendations.
choices.explanation: Testing an individual authorization decision has a different purpose from validating the full policy document.

choices.text: Apply the policy to a production role and wait for CloudTrail to record a denial.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to detect issues before granting the permissions.

choices.text: Use only a JSON parser and assume any readable policy contains valid IAM actions.
choices.explanation: A JSON parser can read a policy even when it contains an invalid IAM action name.

learning.reason: It returns findings based on AWS policy grammar and recommendations before the policy is applied.
learning.concept: JSON syntax, IAM policy grammar, and analysis of access in use are different checks.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Prevent deletion of audit log versions before their retention expires
prompt: You must retain S3 audit logs for 7 years. Neither bucket administrators nor the account root user may shorten the retention period for protected object versions. Each log must receive its retention period when it is stored. Which configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Enable versioning and S3 Object Lock, and configure 7-year retention in Compliance mode.
choices.explanation: Even ordinary AWS account administrative permissions cannot delete a protected version or shorten its retention period before it expires.

choices.text: Enable versioning only and allow administrators to delete objects by specifying the VersionId.
choices.explanation: This permits direct deletion of the versions that need protection.

choices.text: Use Governance mode and allow administrators with bypass permissions to shorten retention periods.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement that even privileged principals cannot shorten the retention period.

choices.text: Define only a bucket policy that denies deletion, while allowing root to update that policy freely.
choices.explanation: The denial can be removed by an overriding change, so this does not enforce the required retention period.

learning.reason: Even ordinary AWS account administrative permissions cannot delete a protected version or shorten its retention period before it expires.
learning.concept: Distinguish restricting deletion permissions from a retention mode that protects versions until their retention expires.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Verify whether audit logs were changed or deleted
prompt: You want to verify later that audit logs delivered from a CloudTrail trail to S3 have not been changed or deleted since delivery. Encryption and access controls are already in place. Which mechanisms should you use for verification? Select TWO.

choices.text: During the audit, run log file integrity validation against the delivered digests.
choices.explanation: This checks whether stored logs have changed or been deleted since delivery.

choices.text: Compare only the number of events ingested into CloudWatch with the number of files in S3.
choices.explanation: The counts can match even if file contents have changed.

choices.text: Enable log file integrity validation on the CloudTrail trail in question.
choices.explanation: Signed digests associated with the logs are delivered for the relevant period.

choices.text: Store a backup with the same name in S3 and do not issue a signature for value comparison.
choices.explanation: Matching names alone cannot verify the integrity of delivered logs.

choices.text: Store the logs with SSE-KMS and assume that any decryptable log is unchanged since delivery.
choices.explanation: Successful decryption does not establish that the content is the same as it was at delivery.

learning.reason: Signed digests associated with the logs are delivered for the relevant period. Validation checks whether stored logs have changed or been deleted since delivery.
learning.concept: Encryption at rest addresses confidentiality; log integrity validation provides evidence about post-delivery changes.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Observe Runtime Behavior Separately from EKS Configuration Audits
prompt: The EKS management API has been audited, but the operations team wants AWS threat detection to observe runtime behavior—such as processes and file operations—on the corresponding nodes. Which setting should they add?

choices.text: Enable ECR push-time scanning and use it to analyze processes in containers that are already running.
choices.explanation: Image scanning and monitoring behavior in a running environment are different tasks.

choices.text: Increase the existing CloudTrail management events and assume they will include every system operation in the containers.
choices.explanation: Management events do not record all runtime activity on a node.

choices.text: Use only VPC Flow Logs to obtain information about processes and local file operations.
choices.explanation: Network flows do not record the requested host-level activity.

choices.text: Enable GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring and deploy the agent for the applicable EKS nodes.
choices.explanation: This delivers runtime events from supported workloads to GuardDuty.

learning.reason: This delivers runtime events from supported workloads to GuardDuty.
learning.concept: Management API records and signals used to detect behavior on a running node are different.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Prevent Inconsistent Attribute Values Across an Organization
prompt: Teams use inconsistent values for the cost-center tag. For the supported resource types across multiple accounts, whenever this tag is set, accept only approved values. A separate mechanism already makes tagging mandatory. Which should you apply?

choices.text: Use AWS Config to send SNS notifications about tag violations, thereby rejecting invalid values when they are set.
choices.explanation: A notification after the fact does not control the value at the time it is entered.

choices.text: Apply a tag policy to the OU and define the approved values and enforcement for the supported resource types.
choices.explanation: This lets you enforce a consistent value standard when tags are applied.

choices.text: Enable cost allocation tags on the billing page and assume the configuration API will reject values that are not included in cost reports.
choices.explanation: Billing classification settings do not enforce allowed values when a tag is applied.

choices.text: Use Tag Editor to update only existing resources in bulk, without applying the standard to new tags.
choices.explanation: This can correct existing values, but it does not enforce the standard for future settings.

learning.reason: This lets you enforce a consistent value standard when tags are applied.
learning.concept: Distinguish whether a tag must exist from whether its value complies with the standard.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Allow Only Auditable Interactive Sessions
prompt: Use Session Manager for maintenance access to EC2 instances. For administrative purposes, the contents of interactive shells must be audited in CloudWatch Logs, and SSH tunneling or port-forwarding sessions that do not support recording cannot be allowed. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Use SSH through a tunnel and conclude that shell contents are saved because the start and end times are in CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: API auditing does not include the contents of interactive commands.

choices.text: Allow only port forwarding and assume that Session Manager logging can record the contents inside the tunnel.
choices.explanation: Session Manager logging does not capture the contents of forwarded traffic.

choices.text: Allow only recording-capable standard shell sessions and enable Session Manager logging output.
choices.explanation: This lets you retain the interactive contents of the permitted shells.

choices.text: Disable the CloudWatch Logs agent on the instances and audit all sessions by their start times only.
choices.explanation: The requested activity contents are not recorded.

learning.reason: This lets you retain the interactive contents of the permitted shells.
learning.concept: To determine whether a session is auditable, consider not just its authentication method, but also whether its contents can be recorded.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Measure False-Positive Impact Before Blocking
prompt: Add a new AWS Managed Rules inspection to the Web ACL for a public application. For production traffic, you want to measure matches for the selected new rule before switching to blocking, while continuing to evaluate other active protections. What should you configure?

choices.text: Set the new rule to Allow so matching requests continue to be evaluated by subsequent existing rules.
choices.explanation: Allow is a terminating action and stops evaluation of subsequent protections.

choices.text: Temporarily override the action for the target rule to Count, then restore the setting after validating the findings.
choices.explanation: This measures matches and lets subsequent evaluation continue without blocking traffic at the new rule.

choices.text: Do not add the target rule; treat the total number of ALB requests as the number of matches for the new rule.
choices.explanation: Without evaluating the rule, you cannot determine which requests matched it.

choices.text: Disable the entire Web ACL and first observe only the traffic the application accepts.
choices.explanation: This does not observe matches for the new rule and also disables existing protections.

learning.reason: This measures matches and lets subsequent evaluation continue without blocking traffic at the new rule.
learning.concept: A nonterminating action lets you observe matches while continuing to evaluate existing protections.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Use session attributes to scope a shared role’s access
prompt: Engineers assume a shared operations role through the company’s identity provider. How should access be designed so that adding a team does not require another role, and engineers can act only on resources whose Team tag matches a team attribute they cannot change?

choices.text: Allow anyone to assume the role by self-reporting any Team tag they choose.
choices.explanation: A user could change their claimed team and expand the scope of their access.

choices.text: Pass a Team session tag from the IdP and compare PrincipalTag with ResourceTag.
choices.explanation: A managed attribute can be matched to the tags on resources the user is allowed to access.

choices.text: Grant the shared role access to resources regardless of team, and check team membership in the operations menu.
choices.explanation: This does not limit which resources IAM allows the role to access.

choices.text: Create a unique role and policy for every team, and provision a new role whenever a team is added.
choices.explanation: This can separate permissions by team, but it does not meet the requirement to use a shared role and attributes.

learning.reason: A managed attribute can be matched to the tags on resources the user is allowed to access.
learning.concept: Control both which attributes are trusted in the token and the conditions under which the session can access resources.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Prevent unintended broad sharing of a secret
prompt: A deployment updates a Secrets Manager resource policy. Access for a specific partner execution role is required, but the policy must be rejected if it exposes the secret to a broad set of principals. Which safeguard should be used each time?

choices.text: Increase the rotation frequency of the secret.
choices.explanation: Rotating the value does not limit which principals can access it.

choices.text: Add CloudTrail notifications only, and have an operator review public access after the policy is applied.
choices.explanation: This does not block public access before the configuration is applied.

choices.text: Enable default encryption for the secret, without validating the resource policy’s access scope.
choices.explanation: Encryption does not check whether a broad resource policy update should be rejected.

choices.text: Enable BlockPublicPolicy when setting the resource policy.
choices.explanation: Secrets Manager rejects a policy that would allow broad public access.

learning.reason: Secrets Manager rejects a policy that would allow broad public access.
learning.concept: Validate the resource policy’s access scope before applying it while retaining the required individual sharing.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Deny only non-TLS traffic at the resource
prompt: Several legitimate clients connect to the same S3 bucket. How should the bucket be configured to reject requests over HTTP, including requests from clients that otherwise have permission, while preserving existing authorization?

choices.text: Add an allow statement for requests where aws:SecureTransport is true, but leave existing HTTP allows in place.
choices.explanation: An additional allow does not deny HTTP requests that are allowed elsewhere.

choices.text: Use S3 Object Lock and assume that TLS will be required for objects that cannot be changed.
choices.explanation: Enforcing retention does not restrict the connection method.

choices.text: Set SSE-KMS as the default and treat HTTP requests as encrypted in transit.
choices.explanation: Server-side encryption controls data at rest.

choices.text: Add a bucket policy that explicitly denies the applicable requests when aws:SecureTransport is false.
choices.explanation: This denies only that route, leaving existing allows over TLS to be evaluated.

learning.reason: This denies only that route, leaving existing allows over TLS to be evaluated.
learning.concept: Protecting the transport channel and authorizing principals to operate on objects are separate controls.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Restrict use of the same key by data purpose
prompt: An application uses the same symmetric KMS key for data keys from multiple departments and includes the department name as the Encryption Context during encryption. An audit role should be allowed to decrypt data for only one department. What should be configured while preserving the existing encryption method?

choices.text: Enable key rotation and distinguish data by department according to when the key was rotated.
choices.explanation: Key rotation does not configure department-specific decryption conditions.

choices.text: Add an Encryption Context condition for the target department to the kms:Decrypt permission.
choices.explanation: That decryption permission will not apply to requests with a different context.

choices.text: Allow the audit role to use kms:Decrypt without conditions, and check the department name in application logs.
choices.explanation: Checking logs afterward does not restrict access when it occurs.

choices.text: Create a different alias for each department that points to the same key, and use the alias name to separate decryption of ciphertext.
choices.explanation: Aliases are not authorization boundaries for ciphertext with different conditions.

learning.reason: That decryption permission will not apply to requests with a different context.
learning.concept: Authenticated encryption context can also be used as an authorization condition for decryption.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Enforce IMDSv2 after checking compatibility
prompt: You need to require IMDSv2 across a running EC2 fleet. First, observe whether any older agents use IMDSv1; after updating them, allow only token-based requests. Which two actions should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Change only HopLimit and use it to determine whether requests use IMDSv1 or IMDSv2.
choices.explanation: The network response hop limit and the token requirement are separate settings.

choices.text: Leave HttpTokens set to optional and conclude that IMDSv1 is blocked.
choices.explanation: optional allows requests without a token.

choices.text: Use only the CloudTrail management API history to fully verify metadata access from within instances.
choices.explanation: It does not show individual metadata requests made from within the operating system.

choices.text: Set HttpTokens to required in the instance metadata options, and apply the setting to future launch templates as well.
choices.explanation: This enforces token use for running instances and future instances.

choices.text: Monitor tokenless access with MetadataNoToken or a similar metric, then update the callers that need it.
choices.explanation: This helps identify existing callers that would fail once IMDSv2 is required.

learning.reason: You can identify existing callers that would fail once IMDSv2 is required, then enforce token use for running and future instances.
learning.concept: Measure compatibility separately from enforcing the setting on updated instances.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Stop later actions without interrupting an action in progress
prompt: A change freeze is declared while CodePipeline is updating a production stack. You need to collect the result of the action in progress and prevent the pipeline from moving on to the next action after it completes. Which stop operation should you use?

choices.text: Close the entrance to the production stage and assume that later actions in executions already inside the stage will also stop.
choices.explanation: Closing the entrance does not stop executions that have already entered the stage.

choices.text: Stop the execution using Stop and wait.
choices.explanation: It waits for the in-progress action to finish and does not start subsequent actions.

choices.text: Choose Stop and abandon, assuming the pipeline will still collect the update result from the integrated service.
choices.explanation: The pipeline abandons the execution without waiting.

choices.text: Delete and recreate the pipeline, then record the earlier stack update as successful.
choices.explanation: You would lose the ability to track the existing execution and the external action's result.

learning.reason: The operation waits for the in-progress action to finish and prevents subsequent actions from starting.
learning.concept: Treat stopping a pipeline execution separately from the state of an operation already started by an integrated service.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Pass artifacts to an action in another Region
prompt: In one AWS account, run a supported deployment action in Osaka from a Tokyo-based CodePipeline. Keep the source and the CodePipeline pipeline in Tokyo, and do not implement artifact copying in a script. What should you configure? Select two.

choices.text: Move only the Tokyo source to Osaka and leave the deployment action in Tokyo.
choices.explanation: This does not run the requested action in Osaka, and a source action cannot be a cross-Region action.

choices.text: Set the supported deployment action's Region to Osaka.
choices.explanation: You can specify the execution Region for an individual action.

choices.text: Create a bucket in Osaka but leave the action's Region unspecified, so it defaults to Tokyo.
choices.explanation: Configuring an artifact store alone does not change where the action runs.

choices.text: Create only a bucket in Osaka in another account and wait for the pipeline to detect the Region and owner automatically.
choices.explanation: You must specify an artifact store in the same account as the pipeline for the action's Region.

choices.text: Specify an S3 artifact store and a key in Osaka, in the same account.
choices.explanation: CodePipeline can handle copying the input to the target Region.

learning.reason: Specify the execution Region for the action, and let CodePipeline copy its input to that Region.
learning.concept: Provide an artifact handoff location in the Region where the action runs.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Check whether the previous production execution is eligible for rollback
prompt: You update the CodePipeline structure and then find a problem with the deployed application. The only successful execution you want to roll back to used the previous structure; there is no successful execution using the current structure. How should you assess a plan to use stage rollback?

choices.text: Retry the failed action and specify the previous successful version; the same execution will switch to the older version.
choices.explanation: A retry does not change the inputs of the execution being resumed to a different version.

choices.text: Choose stage rollback; it automatically restores the pipeline definition to its previous structure.
choices.explanation: A stage operation does not restore an earlier version of the pipeline configuration.

choices.text: If you have the execution ID, stage rollback can return to any successful execution from before the structure change.
choices.explanation: The execution ID does not change the eligibility requirements for a pipeline structure version.

choices.text: You cannot use an execution with the old structure as the rollback target. Redeploy a known-good version using the current structure.
choices.explanation: Rollback targets are limited to executions using the current pipeline structure version.

learning.reason: Rollback targets are limited to executions using the current pipeline structure version.
learning.concept: The existence of an artifact does not mean its execution is eligible as a rollback target.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Preventing One Change from Triggering Two Runs
prompt: A change to an existing CodeCommit branch starts CodePipeline twice. EventBridge was added, but polling is still enabled. How can you keep event-based triggering while reducing duplicate starts?

choices.text: Detect duplicates in the logs, then stop the test without changing the source change detection settings.
choices.explanation: Stopping the test afterward leaves the cause of the two starts in place.

choices.text: Delete the EventBridge rule and shorten the polling interval.
choices.explanation: This can leave only one trigger path, but it removes the required event detection.

choices.text: Keep EventBridge and set PollForSourceChanges to false.
choices.explanation: This stops the extra starts caused by polling.

choices.text: Use SUPERSEDED mode, leave both source events and polling enabled, and replace duplicate runs afterward.
choices.explanation: Runs might be replaced later, but both paths that start them remain enabled.

learning.reason: Stop the extra starts caused by polling.
learning.concept: When multiple paths detect the same source change, explicitly choose the path to use and disable the other one.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Applying an Image to a Container in an Existing Task Definition
prompt: Update an ECS service using the standard ECS deployment action in CodePipeline. The build produces a new image URI, but you want to retain the port and environment settings from the task definition used by the running service. What should you pass to the next action?

choices.text: Pass only imageDetail.json with ImageURI, using the blue/green format with the standard action.
choices.explanation: This format does not match the input contract for the standard action.

choices.text: Pass an imagedefinitions.json input containing the target container name and the new imageUri.
choices.explanation: The standard ECS action can replace the image for the target container.

choices.text: Output the test ALB listener ARN from the buildspec, and omit the image URI from the input.
choices.explanation: Listener information alone cannot update the image in the task definition.

choices.text: Push the new image to ECR with the same tag each time, but do not create an input for the deployment action.
choices.explanation: The standard ECS action will not receive the container and URI to replace.

learning.reason: The standard ECS action can replace the image for the target container.
learning.concept: Standard deployments and blue/green deployments use different image definition file contracts.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Identifying the Source of a Setting Visible During a Build
prompt: The buildspec sets DEPLOY_REGION to Tokyo, and the CodeBuild project sets it to Osaka. This StartBuild call passes a different region through environmentVariablesOverride. If no build command overrides it separately, which value is used?

choices.text: The buildspec takes precedence because it is source-controlled, overriding values specified later by the project or at runtime.
choices.explanation: Whether a value is version-controlled does not affect environment variable precedence.

choices.text: The override in this StartBuild call takes precedence.
choices.explanation: For a variable with the same name, the build-start override takes precedence over the project and buildspec settings.

choices.text: The project value always takes precedence, and the runtime override with the same name is ignored.
choices.explanation: Runtime variables take precedence over the project definition.

choices.text: The three values are concatenated and passed as an array.
choices.explanation: Values for a variable with the same name are not concatenated; precedence determines which one is used.

learning.reason: For a variable with the same name, the build-start override takes precedence over the project and buildspec settings.
learning.concept: When a setting is defined at several levels, identify which one applies to the individual run.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Requiring Approval for Integration Builds from External Pull Requests
prompt: Run CodeBuild for pull requests in a public GitHub repository. Internal contributions from trusted authors should start automatically. Even for a dedicated build that does not use elevated privileges, you do not want builds for external contributions to start until a maintainer approves them. What should you use?

choices.text: For builds triggered by external contributions, only shorten log retention without changing the start settings.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to trigger conditions or approval.

choices.text: Start every build, then wait for administrator approval at the final stage of the buildspec.
choices.explanation: The build starts before approval.

choices.text: Set only PULL_REQUEST_CREATED as the webhook event and use the same start conditions for external and internal contributions.
choices.explanation: The event type does not distinguish whether approval is required.

choices.text: Require approval for external contributions with the CodeBuild Pull request build policy.
choices.explanation: PR builds can require approval based on the contributor's relationship to the repository.

learning.reason: PR builds can require approval based on the contributor's relationship to the repository.
learning.concept: Validate external input before a build starts, and keep that safeguard separate from limiting the execution role's permissions.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Separate Shared Caches Only When Dependency Definitions Change
prompt: Multiple CodeBuild projects build with the same runtime. Their dependency directories use an S3 cache, and an old cache must not be reused only when package-lock.json changes. Which design meets this requirement?

choices.text: Create a cache key from the lock file hash, and use matching paths and a shared namespace.
choices.explanation: Projects can share a cache for the same inputs, while a change produces a different key.

choices.text: Generate a key containing the current time for each build, so even unchanged dependencies use a different cache.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to reuse the cache across builds.

choices.text: Use only the branch name as the key and keep using the same cache even if the lock file changes.
choices.explanation: The key does not detect a dependency change within the same branch.

choices.text: Use only the log group name as the cache key and use a different dependency path in each project.
choices.explanation: The key does not distinguish dependency contents or compatible restore targets.

learning.reason: Projects can share a cache for the same inputs, while a change produces a different key.
learning.concept: Build a cache key from inputs that affect the output being reused.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Pin Submodule Revisions Even When They Are Not Included in the Source
prompt: The GitHub source that CodeBuild fetches directly contains an internal Git submodule. The build must use the revision pinned in the main repository, and fetching the latest revision on every run with a custom script is not acceptable. What should be configured? Select two.

choices.text: Always fetch the latest revision from the submodule's main branch and record only the top-level commit.
choices.explanation: This cannot reproduce the revision pinned in the main source.

choices.text: List only the submodule path in the buildspec output file settings.
choices.explanation: Specifying an artifact does not retrieve a missing source input.

choices.text: Set a short cloneDepth for the main source and assume this automatically checks out submodules.
choices.explanation: History depth settings do not fetch submodules.

choices.text: Allow the source authentication principal to read the private submodule.
choices.explanation: This makes the pinned revision available from the private repository.

choices.text: Enable fetchSubmodules in the source configuration.
choices.explanation: The submodules referenced by the main source can then be fetched with it.
