learning.reason: The submodules referenced by the main source can be fetched with it. The pinned revision can be obtained from the private repository.
learning.concept: Reproduce both the top-level commit and the submodule commit it references.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Trigger Deployment When the Target Image Tag Is Updated
prompt: A release related to ECR must start only when an image is pushed to one managed tag. The information passed to deployment must be the image URI from that push, independent of a new Git commit. Which source should be used?

choices.text: Configure an S3 source and poll until CodeBuild logs indicate a push to ECR.
choices.explanation: This requires an extra path to inspect logs and is not tied to ECR source input.

choices.text: Define a connection trigger for Git tags and treat an ECR tag push as the same event.
choices.explanation: A Git reference and a container registry tag update are different events.

choices.text: Use an ECR source action with the repository and target tag, and use the generated imageDetail.json.
choices.explanation: This starts on publication of the specified image and passes image information downstream.

choices.text: Match the CodeDeploy target group name to the ECR tag and start when the name changes.
choices.explanation: A target group name is not an image publication event.

learning.reason: This starts on publication of the specified image and passes image information downstream.
learning.concept: Distinguish a workflow triggered by code changes from one triggered by publication of a distribution image.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Include Only the Intended On-Premises Hosts in the Same Deployment
prompt: Some business applications run on on-premises servers, and the CodeDeploy EC2/on-premises deployment type is available. Operators want to target only the on-premises hosts used for testing. The hosts can be configured for communication with the AWS network and CodeDeploy authentication. What should they do?

choices.text: Add the on-premises host IP addresses to an ALB target group and omit the CodeDeploy agent.
choices.explanation: Registering a destination alone does not let the host perform a deployment.

choices.text: Define only EC2 instance tags and do not register the on-premises hosts.
choices.explanation: A host that is not registered with AWS cannot be identified as a target.

choices.text: Register all on-premises hosts with the same tag and assume the application name will automatically distinguish test from production.
choices.explanation: With the same tag, the deployment group configuration cannot identify only the test hosts.

choices.text: Install the agent on the test hosts, register and tag them, then select that on-premises tag in the deployment group.
choices.explanation: This lets CodeDeploy identify the execution actors and target set.

learning.reason: This lets CodeDeploy identify the execution actors and target set.
learning.concept: Distinguish authentication to the deployment service from the hosts targeted by a deployment group.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Promote the package revision recorded during verification
prompt: There are verification and distribution repositories in the same CodeArtifact domain. If the revision of the version inspected by CI changes after inspection, the copy should fail. What should be specified in the publishing operation?

choices.text: Specify only the version name and expect to detect a revision change to that version between inspection and copying.
choices.explanation: The expected revision to compare against was not provided.

choices.text: Set allowOverwrite to true as a condition for allowing the copy, without specifying the source revision.
choices.explanation: Allowing an overwrite does not verify the source revision.

choices.text: Specify the inspected package version and its expected revision in versionRevisions for CopyPackageVersions.
choices.explanation: This verifies that the revision at copy time matches the recorded revision.

choices.text: Register the distribution repository as an upstream of the verification repository and assume that every copy associated with distribution will select only the inspected version.
choices.explanation: Adding an upstream does not pin a specific expected revision at copy time.

learning.reason: This verifies that the revision at copy time matches the recorded revision.
learning.concept: Record the revision that identifies the inspected content, separately from the package version number.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Unlist a faulty version while preserving retrieval by existing locks
prompt: An operational quality issue has been found in one version of an npm package. You do not want that version to appear in new resolutions, but during the migration period you want to allow retrieval of the version explicitly specified in existing lock files. How should you handle the version in CodeArtifact?

choices.text: Change the package version's status to Unlisted.
choices.explanation: It is removed from the normal version listing, but explicit retrieval remains possible.

choices.text: Change the version's status to Disposed, delete its assets, and retrieve it explicitly later.
choices.explanation: The assets that were deleted cannot be downloaded from that version.

choices.text: Change the version's status to Archived and assume existing locks can retrieve it in the same way.
choices.explanation: Archived assets cannot be downloaded.

choices.text: Leave the package version as Published and notify only existing users of its version number.
choices.explanation: The version remains a candidate for new dependency resolutions.

learning.reason: It is removed from the normal version listing, but explicit retrieval remains possible.
learning.concept: Removing a version from the candidate listing is different from preventing retrieval when that version is specified.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Reproduce a build locally without using the cloud queue
prompt: The cause of a failure in a CodeBuild Linux build is unclear. Developers use a Docker environment and want to iteratively check the failing step locally using a build image from the same family and the repository's buildspec. Which approach should they use?

choices.text: Add a VPC endpoint, then have the owner review only the logs in the console.
choices.explanation: This does not provide local iterative execution.

choices.text: Roll back a CodePipeline stage and assume local commands will also use the previous configuration.
choices.explanation: Changing the cloud state does not reproduce the local environment.

choices.text: Run CodeBuild Local Agent with a supported image and the buildspec.
choices.explanation: This lets you inspect the relevant commands in a similar environment without repeatedly queuing cloud builds.

choices.text: Paste the buildspec into a GitHub README and run some commands using only the development machine's global dependencies.
choices.explanation: This does not align the runtime and build environment.

learning.reason: This lets you inspect the relevant commands in a similar environment without repeatedly queuing cloud builds.
learning.concept: Distinguish reproducing an aligned environment from testing cloud-specific networking and authentication.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Inspect a build that cannot be reproduced at a breakpoint
prompt: You want to investigate a CodeBuild failure involving VPC reachability in the same environment. After preparing the appropriate role and session path, you want to pause immediately before a specific build command and inspect the state. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Only increase the project's timeout and always let execution continue through the command.
choices.explanation: This does not provide an arbitrary breakpoint or a debugging session.

choices.text: Connect to a temporary container over SSH after the buildspec finishes and inspect the discarded environment.
choices.explanation: A container that has finished and been discarded cannot be reused.

choices.text: Collect JUnit output in a CodeBuild report, then use the report details to connect to the container from the failed build and inspect its state.
choices.explanation: A test report does not provide access to the execution environment.

choices.text: Enable session connections and use codebuild-breakpoint in the buildspec.
choices.explanation: You can connect to the environment at the breakpoint through Session Manager.

learning.reason: You can connect to the environment at the breakpoint through Session Manager.
learning.concept: To investigate interactively in the same cloud execution environment, explicitly enable the session.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Record the approval decision and its rationale in the pipeline execution
prompt: A person decides whether to promote a release to production. The approval request must show a URL to the validation screen, and the approver must record an approval or rejection with an explanation in the relevant CodePipeline execution. Do not use periodic polling of another service's state. What should you configure?

choices.text: Add a Manual approval action with the review URL.
choices.explanation: The stage can wait until the decision is recorded.

choices.text: Send only the URL through SNS and advance to the next stage as soon as the message is sent.
choices.explanation: Successful delivery of a notification is not an approval from the assigned person.

choices.text: Put the validation screen URL in the CodeBuild test results and start the production promotion automatically when the tests pass, without input from an approver.
choices.explanation: No record of a person's approval or rejection is created.

choices.text: Have the approver comment on a ticket after deployment and treat the pipeline as always approved.
choices.explanation: This does not wait for a decision before promotion.

learning.reason: The stage can wait until the decision is recorded.
learning.concept: Tie approval to the execution, provide a reference URL, and record the decision.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Run a short validation command without a dedicated project
prompt: You want to add a shell operation to CodePipeline V2 to validate a small artifact manifest. The command finishes in seconds, and you do not want to manage a separate CodeBuild project. Which action is appropriate?

choices.text: Define the validation command in a V2 Commands action.
choices.explanation: It can run a command without creating a separate CodeBuild project.

choices.text: Enter a shell command as a comment in a Manual approval action and have the console run it automatically.
choices.explanation: An approval comment is not an executable command.

choices.text: Specify a CodeBuild action without creating the project it references.
choices.explanation: A standard CodeBuild action specifies an existing project.

choices.text: Use a path filter in the Source action to inspect artifact contents.
choices.explanation: A trigger condition does not validate an artifact after it has been retrieved.

learning.reason: It can run a command without creating a separate CodeBuild project.
learning.concept: Use pipeline-integrated commands for short, fixed operations and a dedicated build environment for work that needs one.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Change stack boundaries while retaining resources
prompt: A single CloudFormation stack manages a network and a shared queue. Operational responsibilities are being separated, so you need to move the corresponding existing queue to another stack. Preserve its physical ID and configuration, and do not change its properties at the same time. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Add the queue URL to the source stack's Outputs and only reference it from the destination stack.
choices.explanation: Referencing an output does not change which stack manages the resource.

choices.text: Use Stack refactoring to move the queue's logical resource while retaining the physical resource.
choices.explanation: A dedicated plan moves corresponding resources between stacks.

choices.text: First delete the queue from the source template, then create a new one in the destination with the same name.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to preserve the physical ID and existing data.

choices.text: Add a custom resource and change the queue configuration as part of the same operation as the move.
choices.explanation: There is no need to change resource configuration as part of the move.

learning.reason: A dedicated plan moves corresponding resources between stacks.
learning.concept: Separate changes to which stack manages a resource from updates to the resource's properties.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Reproduce a child-template change from the parent stack
prompt: A CloudFormation parent stack contains several child stacks. You want to release a change to one child's definition. Which configuration lets you track the version used for each child through the parent's update history, without manually operating on the child?

choices.text: Place the changed child template at a versioned location, update the parent's TemplateURL, and update the parent stack.
choices.explanation: The parent can manage the update to the target child stack.

choices.text: Change the child's resources in the console and leave the parent template at its original version.
choices.explanation: The changed child definition cannot be tracked through the parent's update history.

choices.text: Give each child the same stack name as the parent and assume CloudFormation will select the template automatically.
choices.explanation: The child definition is determined by the template referenced by the parent.

choices.text: Delete the child stack, then use the same logical ID in the parent to create new physical resources.
choices.explanation: This does not apply the version as an update to the existing stack.

learning.reason: The parent can manage the update to the target child stack.
learning.concept: When the parent references a version of the child template, you can reproduce the full configuration.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Retain diagnostic resources after a failed creation
prompt: Most of a new environment was created, but the final resource failed because of a temporary permissions configuration error. You need to inspect the resources already created in place and continue after fixing the cause, while avoiding the cost of recreating them. What should you specify in advance for the initial creation in the cloud?

choices.text: Exclude the failed resource from DependsOn in advance and ignore it.
choices.explanation: Changing resource dependencies does not configure resource retention when creation fails.

choices.text: Specify the normal rollback behavior so that all created resources are always deleted on failure.
choices.explanation: This loses the resources needed for diagnosis and incurs the cost of recreating them.

choices.text: Choose the setting that retains resources that were successfully provisioned when a failure occurs.
choices.explanation: You can fix the cause and retry from the failed state.

choices.text: Specify only stack termination protection and assume that resources will be retained regardless of the setting when creation fails.
choices.explanation: Termination protection does not retain successfully created resources after a failure.

learning.reason: You can fix the cause and retry from the failed state.
learning.concept: Choose between rolling everything back on failure and retaining created resources for diagnosis and retry.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Correct a manually changed value against the same template
prompt: A CloudFormation template explicitly declares the configuration value for a corresponding resource, but an operator changed the actual resource through the console. Without changing the template inputs, you want to compare the actual resource with the declaration before an update and review a change that restores the original value. What should you use?

choices.text: Specify a new stack name to create the same resource and automatically inherit the same physical ID.
choices.explanation: This does not correct a difference in an existing resource.

choices.text: Run drift detection alone and wait for the detected differences to be automatically reverted.
choices.explanation: Reporting a difference does not update the resource.

choices.text: Create a traditional change set and assume it will show all changes to the actual resource if the templates before and after are identical.
choices.explanation: Traditional comparisons focus on differences between update templates; they do not compare the template with the actual resource.

choices.text: Create a drift-aware change set, review the difference between the actual resource and its declaration, and execute it.
choices.explanation: Even with the same template, you can plan changes that correct drift in supported resources.

learning.reason: Even with the same template, you can plan changes that correct drift in supported resources.
learning.concept: Compare the previously deployed value, the new expected value, and the current actual value separately.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Deploy shared foundations without staying in the organization's management account
prompt: Use the service-managed model for StackSets to deploy common configuration to an OU from a dedicated foundation account. Use the AWS Organizations management account only during setup, and do not manually create individual roles in each member account. What should you configure? Select two.

choices.text: Register the dedicated foundation account as a delegated administrator for StackSets.
choices.explanation: You can operate without staying signed in to the organization's management account.

choices.text: Manually distribute self-managed execution roles to each member account.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the service-managed model or the operational requirements.

choices.text: Tag the OU name on a stack in the dedicated account.
choices.explanation: This does not register the account as a delegated administrator.

choices.text: Enable trusted access for Organizations and CloudFormation StackSets.
choices.explanation: This establishes the integration with the organization required for service-managed deployments.

choices.text: Store long-term credentials for the organization's management account in the dedicated account.
choices.explanation: This does not configure delegation through the organization service.

learning.reason: This establishes the integration with the organization required for service-managed deployments. You can operate without staying signed in to the organization's management account.
learning.concept: Define the organization's permission for service integration separately from the account delegated to operate centrally.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Find resource property errors before sending templates to AWS
prompt: An IaC team checks CloudFormation in pull requests. You want CI to report incorrect resource property names and types as well as YAML syntax errors, without providing AWS credentials. What should you use?

choices.text: Create a new stack in CloudFormation and report provisioning failures in the PR.
choices.explanation: This requires AWS credentials and creates real resources.

choices.text: Run drift detection only in the existing environment and treat that as validation of the new template in the PR.
choices.explanation: This does not validate the syntax or specification of a new template.

choices.text: Run cfn-lint in CI to check the template against resource specifications.
choices.explanation: It validates property names and types locally without deploying the template.

choices.text: Run only a YAML parser and assume that unknown property names will be reported as errors.
choices.explanation: A valid YAML document does not necessarily conform to CloudFormation resource specifications.

learning.reason: It validates property names and types locally without deploying the template.
learning.concept: Syntax checks cannot replace validation against the resource specifications of the target service.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Moving from fast development updates to standard configuration management
prompt: In the development environment, Lambda functions are updated quickly with CDK hotswap. In production, the CloudFormation template and deployed state must remain aligned, and changes must not be applied directly through service APIs. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Disable drift detection in production and use hotswap permanently.
choices.explanation: Disabling detection does not resolve differences between the deployed resources and the template.

choices.text: Run only CDK synth and treat the artifacts as deployed if no production resources change.
choices.explanation: The synthesized changes are never deployed to production.

choices.text: Use hotswap in production too, and treat changes made through the target resource's service API as CloudFormation updates.
choices.explanation: Direct changes bypass CloudFormation and can cause the deployed state to diverge from its managed state.

choices.text: Do not use hotswap in production; perform a standard CloudFormation deployment through CDK.
choices.explanation: Production changes go through a CloudFormation update.

learning.reason: Production changes go through a CloudFormation update.
learning.concept: Use fast iteration for development and a path that manages update history with IaC for production.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Updating a package on managed nodes without stopping the service
prompt: You distribute a custom agent with Systems Manager Distributor. Its update script supports applying changes incrementally, and you do not want to uninstall the entire agent during a routine update. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Specify Distributor's In-place update.
choices.explanation: The update script can modify the existing installation.

choices.text: Remove the nodes from Distributor targets, then manually apply the latest version to each node.
choices.explanation: This does not provide ongoing managed distribution during operations.

choices.text: Choose Uninstall and reinstall, and expect the service to keep running.
choices.explanation: The existing package is uninstalled first.

choices.text: Update SSM inventory and treat its report as evidence that the package files were updated.
choices.explanation: Inventory collects state; it does not update files.

learning.reason: The update script can modify the existing installation.
learning.concept: Choose between an incremental update and a reinstall based on how the package behaves.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Notifying the team about settings that have not been updated
prompt: Keep an Advanced parameter in Parameter Store active. If its value has not been updated for 90 days, notify the responsible team through EventBridge, but do not delete the parameter. Which policy should you use?

choices.text: Set only ExpirationNotification and assume it measures 90 days since the last update, regardless of whether an expiration date exists.
choices.explanation: This policy sends notifications based on expiration; it does not measure how long a value has gone without an update.

choices.text: Set the NoChangeNotification policy to 90 days.
choices.explanation: It generates an event when there has been no update and leaves the value in place.

choices.text: Set Expiration to 90 days and notify users after it expires.
choices.explanation: The parameter is deleted when it expires.

choices.text: Copy the parameter's current value into a tag and assume the tag sends an email after 90 days.
choices.explanation: Tags do not provide notifications based on the time since the last update.

learning.reason: It generates an event when there has been no update and leaves the value in place.
learning.concept: A notification that a parameter has not been updated is different from expiration of the parameter itself.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Avoiding data-plane pressure from frequent configuration checks
prompt: An ECS application reads a feature flag on every request. The configuration is distributed through AppConfig, and you do not want to call the service API for every request. You want changes to be picked up without redeploying the application. Which setup should you use?

choices.text: Start CodePipeline each time the configuration value is read, wait for the result artifact to be generated, and use it to make the decision.
choices.explanation: This triggers unnecessary executions for application configuration reads.

choices.text: Use the AppConfig Agent, and have the application read from its local cache.
choices.explanation: The agent manages periodic configuration retrieval, while request processing uses the cache.

choices.text: Access the AppConfig Data API directly from every application request.
choices.explanation: This does not avoid API calls that grow in proportion to request volume.

choices.text: Embed the value in environment variables at deployment startup and do not retrieve it again.
choices.explanation: Picking up changes would require another deployment.

learning.reason: The agent manages periodic configuration retrieval, while request processing uses the cache.
learning.concept: Separate how often the configuration service is called from how often the application reads its configuration locally.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Limit recording of global IAM resources to the required Regions
prompt: Enable AWS Config in two supported Regions. Record Region-specific resources in both, but avoid duplicate recording of legacy global IAM users and roles. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Limit global IAM recording to one Region while keeping Region-specific resource recording enabled in both.
choices.explanation: This avoids duplicate records for the same global IAM resources while covering resources that are specific to each Region.

choices.text: Use only one Config recorder across both Regions.
choices.explanation: This would leave Region-specific resources in the other Region unrecorded.

choices.text: Do not record global IAM resources anywhere, and replace Regions with organization names.
choices.explanation: This would not provide the requested IAM configuration history.

choices.text: Record global IAM resources in both Regions, but limit the displayed Region to one in the aggregator.
choices.explanation: Limiting the display does not prevent duplicate recording in each Region.

learning.reason: This avoids duplicate records for the same global IAM resources while covering resources that are specific to each Region.
learning.concept: Choose global-resource recording separately from resource recording in each Region.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Draft an IaC migration template from the current settings of manually managed resources
prompt: Create a draft template for migrating many supported resources that are outside IaC management into CloudFormation. You want to review the targets and properties before bringing them under management. What should you use?

choices.text: Delete the Config history and recreate existing resources one by one in CloudFormation.
choices.explanation: This does not read existing configuration values to produce a template.

choices.text: Create all existing resources in a new stack first, then infer their configuration from the stack.
choices.explanation: This creates new resources before producing a draft.

choices.text: Run a CloudFormation import without writing a definition, then review the configuration after management begins.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement not to bring resources under management during the review stage.

choices.text: Scan resources with IaC generator and generate a template for the resources you select.
choices.explanation: This produces a draft template from existing resources for review.

learning.reason: This produces a draft template from existing resources for review.
learning.concept: Reading existing resources to create a draft is separate from registering them as stack-managed resources.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Validate IaC against policy before deployment
prompt: Review CDK-synthesized CloudFormation in a PR. In addition to checking that the syntax is valid, you want code-defined rules to determine whether every S3 bucket has the settings required by your organization, without deploying to AWS. Which tool should you use?

choices.text: Use only AWS Config evaluations after deployment.
choices.explanation: This does not directly evaluate an undeployed template at the PR stage.

choices.text: Parse the synthesized template with a YAML parser and treat valid syntax as proof that every bucket has the required organizational settings.
choices.explanation: A syntax check does not determine whether organizational rules are satisfied.

choices.text: Display the changes with cdk diff without configuring automated rule checks.
choices.explanation: This shows changes but does not automatically determine whether the organizational settings are present.

choices.text: Compare the synthesized output with organizational rules using CloudFormation Guard.
choices.explanation: It can compare template properties with organizational rules.

learning.reason: It can compare template properties with organizational rules.
learning.concept: Template syntax and organization-specific constraints should be checked separately.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Avoid losing confirmed updates during a Region failure
prompt: Place a new DynamoDB table in a supported Region set. The application must continue writing after losing one Region, with an RPO of zero for committed records. Increased write latency between Regions is acceptable. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Create independent tables in each Region and have clients manually restore differences after a failure.
choices.explanation: There is no mechanism to confirm updates synchronously, so this does not ensure continued writes or an RPO of zero.

choices.text: Use MRSC in a supported Region set, configured with three replicas or with two replicas and a witness.
choices.explanation: Synchronous replication can provide an RPO of zero for committed updates.

choices.text: Use two MREC replicas and set ConsistentRead on every read to eliminate asynchronous write replication latency between Regions.
choices.explanation: The local read method does not make asynchronous cross-Region replication synchronous.

choices.text: Use a single-Region table, take hourly backups, and restore the latest backup in another Region.
choices.explanation: Committed updates made after the backup and before the failure may be lost.

learning.reason: Synchronous replication can provide an RPO of zero for committed updates.
learning.concept: Choose asynchronous or synchronous replication based on the recovery-point objective.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Recover only cacheable reads from origin failures
prompt: A CloudFront behavior sends static GET requests and order POST requests to the same primary origin. A proposed design creates a secondary origin so that errors from the selected primary origin automatically route both methods to the secondary origin. What should be reconsidered?

choices.text: Use an origin group for supported methods such as GET, and design separate failure routing in the application for POST.
choices.explanation: CloudFront origin failover cannot route POST requests.

choices.text: Configure error codes on the origin group so GET and POST are sent to the secondary origin under the same conditions.
choices.explanation: Supported methods are limited to GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS.

choices.text: Set the cache TTL for POST to 0 to enable failover to the secondary origin.
choices.explanation: The cache duration does not change the method limitation.

choices.text: Automatically convert POST requests to GET and send them to the secondary origin so order writes can also be safely reproduced.
choices.explanation: This changes the meaning of the request and does not preserve correct writes.

learning.reason: CloudFront origin failover cannot route POST requests.
learning.concept: Even within the same distribution, origin failover support depends on the HTTP method.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Ensure consistent first reads from restored volumes
prompt: Create many new volumes from the same EBS snapshot in a specific Availability Zone in the recovery Region. You want to avoid read latency on first access as soon as the volumes are created. Additional charges are acceptable, and you can prepare in advance. What should you configure in that Availability Zone?

choices.text: Increase the IOPS for gp3 and assume that this also eliminates the first retrieval of each restored block.
choices.explanation: Volume performance settings alone do not eliminate the initial retrieval of blocks from a snapshot.

choices.text: Create the volumes, but do nothing to initialize them before they receive their first production request.
choices.explanation: This cannot eliminate first-access latency in advance.

choices.text: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore for the snapshot in the target Availability Zone in the recovery Region ahead of time.
choices.explanation: Volumes created in an enabled Availability Zone receive initialized performance.

choices.text: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore only in another Availability Zone and assume it also applies to the target Availability Zone because the snapshot is the same.
choices.explanation: The setting applies to a specific snapshot and Availability Zone combination.

learning.reason: Volumes created in an enabled Availability Zone receive initialized performance.
learning.concept: Being able to copy a snapshot is different from having the new volume's blocks ready when the volume becomes available.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Achieve a short RPO without running full-size production-equivalent EC2 instances continuously
prompt: Recover a group of supported on-premises servers in AWS. During normal operations, you do not want to keep full-size recovery instances running continuously, and during a disaster you want to launch instances from continuously replicated disks. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Send only monitoring metrics to AWS and restore disks from those metrics when needed.
choices.explanation: Metrics do not contain disk contents.

choices.text: Run the same number and size of instances in AWS as in production at all times, and continuously replicate all data to them.
choices.explanation: This can be a viable alternative, but it violates the constraint against continuously running full-size instances.

choices.text: Manually create only a copy of an AMI each week and assume that it includes all updates made during that week when a disaster occurs.
choices.explanation: Changes made after the AMI was created are not included.

choices.text: Continuously replicate to an AWS DRS staging area, then launch recovery instances during a disaster.
choices.explanation: Staging resources are used during normal operations, and the servers can run on corresponding EC2 instances during recovery.

learning.reason: Staging resources are used during normal operations, and the servers can run on corresponding EC2 instances during recovery.
learning.concept: The replication area maintained continuously is separate from the production execution environment used during recovery.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Avoid overloading the database during write reconnections
prompt: A service uses many short-lived connections, and clients reconnect simultaneously immediately after an RDS failover. You need to pool connections for a supported engine and mediate switches between DB instances, while the application handles retries for transactions that were in progress. What should you introduce?

choices.text: Hard-code the RDS instance endpoint in every process and remove the connection limit.
choices.explanation: This neither pools individual connections nor mediates switching to a different promoted instance.

choices.text: Place RDS Proxy in front of the database and point the application to the proxy.
choices.explanation: It can use pooled database connections and mediate connection switching during a failover.

choices.text: Specify the CloudFront cache as the database connection endpoint.
choices.explanation: This does not pool database connections or provide a failover configuration.

choices.text: Switch all operations to read-only reader connections.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to continue writes.

learning.reason: RDS Proxy can use pooled database connections and mediate connection switching during a failover.
learning.concept: Sharing connections and retrying operations that failed mid-transaction are separate responsibilities.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Switch Regions Without Changing Clients’ Allow Lists
prompt: A TCP service runs on NLBs in two Regions. Customers can register only fixed public IPv4 addresses in their firewalls. How should you route traffic to a healthy endpoint during a service failure without waiting for customers to change DNS? Select TWO.

choices.text: Create a Standard Global Accelerator and give its static IPv4 addresses to customers.
choices.explanation: Customers can continue using the same allow list.

choices.text: Register the two regional NLBs in their corresponding endpoint groups.
choices.explanation: This provides destinations selected according to health and routing settings.

choices.text: Have each customer register the IP addresses of both NLBs separately, then email them which one to use during a failure.
choices.explanation: This does not switch the entry point without action by the customer.

choices.text: Use Route 53 records to switch between the NLB DNS names, without providing fixed IP addresses.
choices.explanation: This can select a DNS destination, but it does not meet the requirement for customers to allow fixed IP addresses.

choices.text: Associate the same Regional Elastic IP allocation with the NLB in each Region.
choices.explanation: A single regional IP allocation cannot be associated with NLBs in multiple Regions at the same time.

learning.reason: Customers can continue using the same allow list. The two regional NLBs provide destinations selected according to health and routing settings.
learning.concept: Separate the fixed entry point used by clients from the endpoints that can be switched behind it.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Fail Over to the Standby Region Through the Same S3 Access Point
prompt: S3 buckets in two Regions have already been replicated separately. Clients use a single S3 Multi-Region Access Point, and during an exercise, the operator wants to shift all traffic to the standby side. What should be changed without changing the application's name? Select TWO.

choices.text: Distribute new credentials to each client and continue using the primary bucket's name.
choices.explanation: Changing access keys does not replace regional routing settings.

choices.text: Manage the two Regions of the Multi-Region Access Point as active and passive, respectively.
choices.explanation: This restricts which Regions receive requests through the same access point.

choices.text: Keep both active and assume all requests will move to the designated Region.
choices.explanation: This does not limit the eligible destinations to one Region.

choices.text: Stop replication only and leave the access destination on the primary side.
choices.explanation: Stopping data exchange does not change where client requests are sent.

choices.text: Use failover controls during the exercise to make the standby side active.
choices.explanation: This switches the primary and standby routing states.

learning.reason: Active-passive management restricts which Regions receive requests through the same access point. Failover controls switch the primary and standby routing states.
learning.concept: Access routing and replication, which supplies the data needed at the destination, are separate settings.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Preserve Order Within Each Customer While Processing Customers in Parallel
prompt: Use SQS to process contract changes in order for each customer. Changes for different customers should be processed concurrently. A separate unique ID is already used for notification deduplication. How should you design the groups?

choices.text: Use a FIFO queue and set each customer's ID as the MessageGroupId.
choices.explanation: This preserves order for each customer while allowing other groups to be processed concurrently.

choices.text: Assign a new MessageGroupId to every notification for the same customer.
choices.explanation: Notifications for the same customer would be placed in different groups, so their order would not be preserved.

choices.text: Use the same MessageGroupId for all customers and use the deduplication ID to enable concurrent processing across customers.
choices.explanation: All messages would be in the same ordered group, eliminating customer-level concurrency.

choices.text: Use a standard queue, store the customer ID as an attribute, and assume SQS guarantees receive order within each attribute value.
choices.explanation: Standard queue delivery does not provide that group-order guarantee.

learning.reason: The same-customer order is preserved while other groups can be processed concurrently.
learning.concept: The ordering boundary in a FIFO queue and the deduplication identifier serve different purposes.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Launch Replacement Capacity Before an Interruption Notice
prompt: An EC2 Auto Scaling group uses Spot Instances. You want replacement capacity to launch when a rebalance recommendation indicates an increased risk of interruption. Multiple instance types and Availability Zones are available, and you do not want to maintain your own monitoring of replacement events. What should you enable?

choices.text: Manually create a new Spot Instance only after an EC2 instance terminates, then register it with the group.
choices.explanation: This conflicts with the requirement to attempt replacement automatically before an interruption.

choices.text: Adjust the target CPU utilization only, without making rebalance recommendations an additional launch trigger.
choices.explanation: CPU-based scaling does not respond to Spot interruption risk.

choices.text: Raise the maximum Spot price and assume every interruption will be resolved without notice.
choices.explanation: This does not configure replacement capacity to launch in response to interruption risk.

choices.text: Enable Capacity Rebalancing for the group.
choices.explanation: In response to a rebalance recommendation, it attempts to launch replacement Spot capacity early, subject to conditions.

learning.reason: In response to a rebalance recommendation, Capacity Rebalancing attempts to launch replacement Spot capacity early, subject to conditions.
learning.concept: Scaling toward a capacity target differs from replacing capacity because of Spot interruption risk.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Compare an application's recovery goals with its configuration
prompt: An application composed of multiple AWS stacks has RTO and RPO targets. Before injecting any faults, you want to compare its resource configuration with those targets and identify potential weaknesses that could prevent them from being met. What should you use?

choices.text: Configure GuardDuty severity filters and use the number of findings as a measure of recovery-goal attainment.
choices.explanation: The number of findings does not assess recovery capability.

choices.text: Immediately inject faults into production with AWS FIS and use that instead of a pre-deployment configuration assessment.
choices.explanation: This is different from the requested non-disruptive configuration assessment.

choices.text: Define the application and a resilience policy in AWS Resilience Hub, then run an assessment.
choices.explanation: It evaluates the configuration against recovery goals and identifies potential improvements.

choices.text: Set the CloudWatch log retention period to match the RPO and assume the RTO can also be met.
choices.explanation: Log retention does not assess the application's overall recovery time or acceptable data loss.

learning.reason: It evaluates the configuration against recovery goals and identifies potential improvements.
learning.concept: Distinguish configuration-based resilience assessment from validation using actual workloads or faults.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Allow time for startup without delaying health detection for existing tasks
prompt: New tasks in an ECS service can take up to 90 seconds to initialize. ALB health checks fail until a task responds successfully, and ECS replaces the task before initialization is complete. How can you allow new tasks to initialize without relaxing the failure-detection interval for existing tasks? Select two.

choices.text: Raise the ALB health check failure threshold for all targets, delaying detection for already running tasks as well.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid delaying failure detection for other tasks.

choices.text: Keep the existing ALB load balancer health check settings.
choices.explanation: This avoids changing the failure-detection interval for targets that are already running.

choices.text: Increase the ALB deregistration delay to allow time for startup initialization.
choices.explanation: This affects deregistration and does not affect health evaluation when a task starts.

choices.text: Set the ECS service's healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds to match the initialization time.
choices.explanation: The scheduler ignores unhealthy status for new tasks during this period.

choices.text: Disable the ECS deployment circuit breaker and expect the scheduler not to check the health of starting tasks.
choices.explanation: Changing how deployment failures are handled does not define a startup health grace period.

learning.reason: The scheduler ignores unhealthy status for new tasks during the grace period, while the failure-detection interval for running targets remains unchanged.
learning.concept: Distinguish the period during application initialization when the scheduler ignores health status from the load balancer's health check interval.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Identify hot keys that table-wide metrics cannot reveal
prompt: Some read requests to DynamoDB are being throttled, but table-wide capacity metrics do not identify the cause. You want to investigate future trends for throttled keys specifically, rather than rank keys by their total access counts. What should you enable?

choices.text: Use Contributor Insights in Throttled keys mode.
choices.explanation: This tracks trends for throttled keys.

choices.text: Compare the maximum and percentile values for table-wide latency, without separately measuring access skew by key.
choices.explanation: Latency alone does not identify which keys were throttled.

choices.text: Display only the total request count for DynamoDB over shorter intervals.
choices.explanation: Table-wide aggregates cannot identify individual keys.

choices.text: Monitor TTL deletion counts as a proxy for throttling by key.
choices.explanation: TTL deletions and rejected writes or reads are separate events.

learning.reason: This tracks trends for throttled keys.
learning.concept: Observe the distribution of keys causing rejections rather than overall consumption.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Investigate DB CPU usage at the OS process level
prompt: CloudWatch CPUUtilization for RDS for PostgreSQL has increased. You want to compare CPU consumption by OS process at intervals of a few seconds. Rankings of SQL wait events alone do not meet the requirement. What should you use?

choices.text: Zoom in on the standard CloudWatch CPUUtilization graph and assume it also includes a breakdown by OS process.
choices.explanation: The instance-wide CPU metric does not include a process breakdown.

choices.text: Subscribe to configuration-change notifications through a DB event subscription.
choices.explanation: This does not continuously measure CPU usage by process.

choices.text: Use Database Insights to view only SQL wait events as a substitute for CPU usage by individual OS process.
choices.explanation: SQL workload contributors and observations of the OS process list are different.

choices.text: Enable RDS Enhanced Monitoring and collect OS metrics at the required measurement interval.
choices.explanation: You can inspect relevant OS information, including the process list.

learning.reason: You can inspect relevant OS information, including the process list.
learning.concept: Choose between DB engine performance analysis and monitoring that inspects guest OS processes.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Compare Versions Within the Same Lambda Alias
prompt: A single Lambda alias routes traffic to an old and a new version using weighted routing. Because the invocation counts differ, you want to view the error rate for each version separately, even though both are invoked through the same alias. Which CloudWatch series should you use?

choices.text: Group by EventSourceMappingUUID and display invocations from the same mapping as two versions.
choices.explanation: A mapping ID is not a dimension that identifies the version of the function that ran.

choices.text: Aggregate Invocations and Errors across all versions and aliases by FunctionName, then split the totals according to the traffic weights.
choices.explanation: This does not provide the measured error counts for each version.

choices.text: Separate Invocations and Errors by the combination of alias and ExecutedVersion, then calculate the rate for each version.
choices.explanation: This gives you the series for each version actually invoked through the same weighted alias.

choices.text: Use only the alias-wide series for Resource and treat it as equivalent to the number of new-version invocations.
choices.explanation: Executions of the old version invoked through the same alias are included.

learning.reason: This gives you the series for each version actually invoked through the same weighted alias.
learning.concept: Use alias-wide aggregates for the alias as a whole, and version-specific aggregates for executions within that alias.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Monitor a Changing Fleet with One Aggregate Expression
prompt: The number of EC2 instances changes frequently. You want CloudWatch to find eligible fleet metrics dynamically within the same namespace, without listing instance IDs, and to use the fleet-wide average as a single time series for an alarm. What should you use?

choices.text: Return every series separately with GROUP BY InstanceId and treat them as a single fleet-wide average.
choices.explanation: The result is per instance, so it is not the requested fleet-wide average.

choices.text: Work backward from average EC2 CPU and create tags for the target instances.
choices.explanation: This does not configure monitoring that calculates the average dynamically.

choices.text: Select the targets in a Metrics Insights query and use the AVG result without GROUP BY for the alarm.
choices.explanation: This accounts for changes in the matching targets and returns the fleet-wide average as a single series.

choices.text: Statically list all IDs present at creation time and keep using the same expression after instances are replaced.
choices.explanation: New instance IDs will not be added to the monitoring target.

learning.reason: This accounts for changes in the matching targets and returns the fleet-wide average as a single series.
learning.concept: Manually registering individual series is different from selecting and aggregating monitoring targets with a query.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Standardize Different Log Field Names at Ingestion
prompt: Two teams emit the same information under the names requestId and request_id. You want to standardize the fields when logs are ingested into CloudWatch Logs so that standard-class logs can be queried the same way in the future, without changing either application. You want to retain the original logs. What should you use?

choices.text: Rename only the file and expect both services to use the same JSON key.
choices.explanation: Changing an outer name does not change fields in the event body.

choices.text: Create normalized fields with a log transformer.
choices.explanation: This provides transformed results for analysis while retaining the information in the ingested original logs.

choices.text: Use a data protection policy to mask both fields, then use the masked value as a common ID to find requests.
choices.explanation: The identifying values would no longer be available, and masking does not normalize the values while preserving them.

choices.text: Write both conditions in every individual Logs Insights query and leave the log fields unnormalized.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to standardize fields at ingestion.

learning.reason: This provides transformed results for analysis while retaining the information in the ingested original logs.
learning.concept: Separate the format used by log sources from the standardized format used for investigation and analysis.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Extract Numeric Values for Aggregation from Existing Logs
prompt: Existing plain-text logs contain a service name and latency=number in a consistent order. You cannot change the original logs. How can you query CloudWatch Logs Insights to get the p95 for each service? Select TWO.

choices.text: Use parse to extract the latency and service name according to the format.
choices.explanation: This creates fields for aggregation without rewriting the original logs.

choices.text: Use filter to select only lines containing latency, then use the event timestamp as the latency value.
choices.explanation: Filtering lines does not make the number in the text available for calculations.

choices.text: Change the retention period for historical logs and wait for aggregated p95 values to be generated automatically.
choices.explanation: Retention settings do not extract and aggregate log values.

choices.text: Treat the extracted latency as a number and aggregate it by service name using stats pct.
choices.explanation: This gives you the p95 for each service.

choices.text: Create a dedicated field index now and have it automatically convert unextracted latency values in historical logs into numbers for aggregation.
choices.explanation: An index does not convert unextracted values into numeric values for aggregation.

learning.reason: This creates fields for aggregation without rewriting the original logs. This gives you the p95 for each service.
learning.concept: Read-time extraction of fields from historical logs differs from ingestion-time transformation of future logs.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Suppress notifications during maintenance while continuing state evaluation
prompt: You operate a CloudWatch composite alarm. You want to silence paging while a separate alarm indicating maintenance is in ALARM, while keeping the composite alarm's own state evaluation active. Which setting should you configure?

choices.text: Set the maintenance alarm as the composite alarm's ActionsSuppressor.
choices.explanation: This preserves the composite alarm's state calculation and suppresses actions such as notifications only when the specified condition is met.

choices.text: Change the SNS target to an unrelated email address.
choices.explanation: This does not define alarm-based suppression, including for other actions.

choices.text: Delete all alarms for the duration of the maintenance window and recreate them afterward.
choices.explanation: This interrupts continuous evaluation of incidents.

choices.text: Add a negation of the maintenance alarm to the composite rule so that the composite alarm is always OK during maintenance.
choices.explanation: This may suppress notifications, but it does not preserve the composite alarm's state evaluation.

learning.reason: This preserves the composite alarm's state calculation and suppresses actions such as notifications only when the specified condition is met.
learning.concept: Separate evaluating the alarm's conditions from suppressing the actions associated with that evaluation.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Reduce sampling for a high-volume route while retaining traces for important requests
prompt: An application uses X-Ray sampling rules. The /health route generates a large volume of traces, while important transaction requests occur infrequently. You want to preserve the sampling policy for transactions and reduce collection only for health checks. What should you configure?

choices.text: Suppress delivery for /health with a monitoring alarm, without changing the sampling conditions.
choices.explanation: Controlling notifications does not change the trace acquisition rate.

choices.text: Lower the default sampling rate by the same proportion for every route.
choices.explanation: This also changes the sampling policy for transaction requests.

choices.text: Hide /health from the trace map while continuing to collect every trace.
choices.explanation: Changing what is displayed does not reduce the amount collected.

choices.text: Create a higher-priority custom sampling rule that matches /health and lowers its sampling rate.
choices.explanation: This reduces sampling only for the matching route and avoids affecting transactions that follow the default rule.

learning.reason: This reduces sampling only for the matching route and avoids affecting transactions that follow the default rule.
learning.concept: Change sampling before collection based on the type of request.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Isolate latency by processing interval
prompt: You are investigating ordinary GET requests on an ALB that does not use WAF. In the access logs, request_processing_time is short, while target_processing_time is long. Which interval should you investigate first?

choices.text: Investigate the time from when the ALB sends the request until the target begins returning response headers.
choices.explanation: This matches the interval represented by target_processing_time.

choices.text: Investigate only the processing after the ALB receives response headers from the target.
choices.explanation: That interval primarily corresponds to response_processing_time.

choices.text: Investigate only DNS resolution by the client.
choices.explanation: That DNS lookup is not included in the ALB's target processing time.

choices.text: Investigate delivery time for access logs from the ALB to S3, and classify long delivery as target processing latency.
choices.explanation: Log delivery wait time is not a measurement of the target's response.

learning.reason: This matches the interval represented by target_processing_time.
learning.concept: Each access log processing-time field refers to a different interval, so identify which boundary saw the increase.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Retain findings for long-term storage and cross-account analysis
prompt: You are not using Security Hub for this task. You want to continuously aggregate GuardDuty findings in encrypted S3 for custom long-term auditing. What should you configure to retain GuardDuty's finding details without trying to reconstruct findings from metrics?

choices.text: Disable GuardDuty, create an S3 bucket, and assume that findings will still be issued while it is disabled.
choices.explanation: This does not provide continuous export while keeping detection active.

choices.text: Configure GuardDuty findings export with an S3 bucket and a KMS key that has the appropriate permissions.
choices.explanation: This exports findings to an audit destination with encryption.

choices.text: Publish only the finding count to CloudWatch and reconstruct each finding's details from the total.
choices.explanation: The count cannot be used to reconstruct the attributes of individual findings.

choices.text: Extend VPC Flow Logs retention and store GuardDuty findings as if they were the same events.
choices.explanation: Some input data and detection results are distinct.

learning.reason: This exports findings to an audit destination with encryption.
learning.concept: Separate the detection service's current view from the storage destination used to retain long-term history.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Investigate Storage Growth by Prefix
prompt: An organization periodically reviews S3 growth. For one large bucket in particular, it wants to use S3 Storage Lens to track which prefixes are contributing to capacity growth. Daily data is sufficient, and individual request logs are not needed. What should be configured?

choices.text: Enable only CloudTrail data events for GetObject and treat the number of reads as the number of bytes stored.
choices.explanation: The number of reads is different from the amount of data stored.

choices.text: Configure the applicable detailed metrics in Storage Lens, including prefix aggregation.
choices.explanation: This makes capacity metrics available for each prefix in the target bucket.

choices.text: Move every prefix to a separate bucket and disregard the existing bucket structure.
choices.explanation: This would require application-side changes just to analyze storage.

choices.text: Collect only basic capacity metrics for the entire bucket, then assign the same growth rate to every key if the value increases.
choices.explanation: This does not identify which prefixes actually consumed capacity.

learning.reason: This makes capacity metrics available for each prefix in the target bucket.
learning.concept: Aggregated capacity analysis and auditing individual API calls are different needs.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Avoid Changing a Compliant Resource Based on a Stale Evaluation
prompt: Before Config automatic remediation starts, an operator brings the target bucket into compliance. The latest configuration evaluation is delayed, so the runbook may receive an earlier noncompliant status. What should the runbook do to avoid making a duplicate change?

choices.text: Retrieve the latest resource configuration and make a change only if remediation is needed.
choices.explanation: Even if a stale evaluation triggers the run, this avoids side effects when the resource is already compliant.

choices.text: Always treat the resource as noncompliant once Config starts remediation and overwrite its state every time.
choices.explanation: The trigger decision does not necessarily reflect the latest configuration.

choices.text: Check the latest configuration in the console only after remediation is complete.
choices.explanation: This cannot prevent an operation on a resource that was already compliant before the change.

choices.text: Stop all Config evaluations and continue remediation.
choices.explanation: This stops status tracking and still does not let an already-started remediation check the latest state.

learning.reason: Even if a stale evaluation triggers the run, this avoids side effects when the resource is already compliant.
learning.concept: Distinguish the observed state reported at invocation from the resource state immediately before a change.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Retain Input for Replay After It Expires from the Stream
prompt: A Lambda function reading Kinesis discards a batch after exceeding its configured number of attempts. By the time an operator investigates, the original records have passed their retention period. Which destination should be used to retain the body of a failed batch for recovery?

choices.text: Retain only the error count in metrics.
choices.explanation: The original input body cannot be recovered.

choices.text: Specify an applicable S3 bucket as the on-failure destination.
choices.explanation: An S3 destination can store the complete failed invocation record along with execution metadata.

choices.text: Enable only Kinesis scaling and assume that discarded batches can be recovered by adding capacity.
choices.explanation: Adjusting capacity does not recover input that has already been lost.

choices.text: Keep only an SNS notification on failure, then use its metadata to reread all original records after their retention period.
choices.explanation: There is no source from which to retrieve input that has expired from the stream.

learning.reason: An S3 destination can store the complete failed invocation record along with execution metadata.
learning.concept: Position information in a failure notification alone is not enough to replay input after it expires.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Choose How to Rerun After Fixing a Workflow Definition
prompt: A production Step Functions Standard workflow has failed. The incorrect state branching condition has been fixed, and the alias has been switched to the new version. The next run must process the same input using the corrected definition, while idempotency keys suppress side effects that have already succeeded. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: If the alias points to the latest version, Redrive the original execution so only the failed state is replaced with the new version.
choices.explanation: The definition and version associated with the original execution do not change.

choices.text: Resend only the input without saving the corrected version, so the original execution resumes under the same name.
choices.explanation: The corrected definition is not selected, so the branching condition remains unchanged.

choices.text: Start a new execution using the alias that points to the corrected version.
choices.explanation: Redrive reuses the original definition, so a new execution is needed to apply the new version.

choices.text: Overwrite only the failed event in the existing execution history to make it finish successfully.
choices.explanation: There is no way to edit the execution history to run a new version.

learning.reason: Redrive reuses the original definition, so a new execution is needed to apply the new version.
learning.concept: The definition used to resume an existing execution differs from the one selected for a new execution.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Capture why a task failed to start for the responder
prompt: A new ECS task becomes STOPPED before the application writes anything to Standard Output. The operations notification must include the failed task ARN, the stop reason, and the container exit status. Which event should you use?

choices.text: Collect ALB access logs and analyze client IP addresses and requests to infer the task startup failure and container exit status.
choices.explanation: The stop reason is not recorded for a task that stopped before serving HTTP traffic.

choices.text: Add only an application log filter for Standard Output and match it against the stop-reason string.
choices.explanation: A failure that produces no application logs has no notification source.

choices.text: Receive only CodeDeploy success and failure summaries and replace those values with the task ARN and stop reason.
choices.explanation: Deployment-level information alone cannot provide the reason for an individual task.

choices.text: Use the STOPPED ECS Task State Change event.
choices.explanation: You can process an event that includes the target task's stop reason and available container status.

learning.reason: You can process an event that includes the target task's stop reason and available container status.
learning.concept: When a failure occurs before application logging starts, use a state event recorded by the service.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Retry transient failures but fail on invalid input
prompt: An AWS Batch job returns an exit code based on the error. Retry known codes that indicate a temporary dependency outage and reasons that indicate host loss, but fail immediately for the exit code for invalid data. How can you avoid applying the maximum attempt count unconditionally?

choices.text: Use evaluateOnExit to set transient failures to RETRY and invalid input to EXIT.
choices.explanation: You can control whether to retry based on the exit code or failure reason.

choices.text: Set attempts to a high value and apply the same retry count to every exit code.
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish a temporary outage from invalid input.

choices.text: Convert the invalid-input exit code to success and treat job success as a record of the input error.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to record invalid input as an immediate failure in Batch.

choices.text: Shorten the job timeout and do not retry if the job completes before the timeout, regardless of its exit code.
choices.explanation: A timeout does not express retry conditions for each failure reason.

learning.reason: You can control whether to retry based on the exit code or failure reason.
learning.concept: Configure the maximum number of retries separately from which failures should be retried.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Use a validation step's result in the same remediation run
prompt: An initial step in Systems Manager Automation reads the current configuration through an API and determines which resource to remediate. A later step must use the ID and state from that check and must not call the same API again to read a different state. How should you connect the steps?

choices.text: Write the same value in a runbook comment and do not define an output for the execution.
choices.explanation: This cannot pass a value that changes with each execution to a later step.

choices.text: Define a selector and type in the initial step's Output, then reference the initial step name and output name from the later step's input.
choices.explanation: You can pass values retrieved by an earlier step to a later step in the same Automation execution.

choices.text: Call the same API again in the later step without checking whether the value matches the one observed at the start.
choices.explanation: A state change in between could produce a value different from the one retrieved in the initial step.

choices.text: Write the initial value only to CloudWatch Logs and do not name it in the later step's input.
choices.explanation: Saving a value in logs does not bind it as data for a later step.

learning.reason: You can pass values retrieved by an earlier step to a later step in the same Automation execution.
learning.concept: Explicitly define data used between steps as typed outputs.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Gather diagnostic details for a task rejected by the load balancer
prompt: A new task in an ECS service is RUNNING, but the ALB target reports an unhealthy status. Before restarting it, you want to distinguish a response-code mismatch from a timeout, as indicated by the target group's status. What should you check?

choices.text: Increase the CPU reservation for the running task and classify the result as a TLS error without checking it.
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish a health check's response code from a timeout.

choices.text: Compare only the Task Definition image tags and use that alone to determine whether the issue is a timeout or a response-code difference.
choices.explanation: A tag does not indicate the ALB's health check result or its cause.

choices.text: Stop all ALB access logs and consider the target healthy because the application is RUNNING.
choices.explanation: The task's runtime status does not establish whether the ALB health check succeeded.

choices.text: Check the target's health status and reason code.
choices.explanation: You can check why ALB marked the target unhealthy, such as ResponseCodeMismatch or Timeout.

learning.reason: You can check why ALB marked the target unhealthy, such as ResponseCodeMismatch or Timeout.
learning.concept: Distinguish a running container from one that the load balancer can reach and that responds successfully.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Find remediation targets from current configuration across Regions
prompt: A central Config aggregator has already aggregated the applicable resources from multiple accounts. During a post-incident inventory, you need to filter the current configuration by attribute conditions and produce a list of EC2 instances. You need a current-state list rather than a time-based change history. What should you use?

choices.text: Use only the noncompliant-resource count for each AWS Config rule and assume it also provides the current attributes of the affected resources.
choices.explanation: Aggregate counts do not provide a list of resources with matching attributes.

choices.text: Remove the aggregator's Region definitions and delete each account's snapshots.
choices.explanation: This removes the path for querying the current recorded configuration.

choices.text: Open each host's CloudTrail API history individually and estimate its current configuration manually.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a way to search the current configuration.

choices.text: Apply conditions on the required attributes with Config Advanced Query against the aggregator.
choices.explanation: You can query the latest recorded configurations of applicable resources across accounts.

learning.reason: You can query the latest recorded configurations of applicable resources across accounts.
learning.concept: Choose between following configuration changes over time and filtering resources by their current attributes.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Retrieve an application's logs as a bundle
prompt: An issue has occurred in an Elastic Beanstalk EC2-based environment. SSH is not permitted, and the investigation requires the relevant server logs as a set, not just the last 100 lines. How should you retrieve the existing logs across nodes?

choices.text: Use only CloudTrail records of Elastic Beanstalk configuration changes as the instances' server logs.
choices.explanation: Management operation records are not operating system or application logs.

choices.text: Delete the environment, immediately create a new one, and then retrieve the logs from the failure.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve evidence from the current environment while retrieving it.

choices.text: Request only Tail logs and assume the default trailing lines represent all the logs.
choices.explanation: Retrieving only the tail omits earlier log content needed for the investigation.

choices.text: Request Bundle logs for the environment and retrieve the bundle from each instance.
choices.explanation: This provides the relevant log files together, rather than only their trailing lines.

learning.reason: This provides the relevant log files together, rather than only their trailing lines.
learning.concept: Choose between a short tail of log output and a request that gathers the relevant logs in full.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Restore a temporary mitigation even when a change fails partway through
prompt: SSM Automation temporarily relaxes processing limits before performing a repair. If the repair fails, you want to restore the limits in the same execution and make the failure identifiable to operators. Which control should you use?

choices.text: Start every step individually without recording the preceding state or setting a value for restoration.
choices.explanation: This does not tie a failure to a compensating action within the same execution.

choices.text: Retry the limit-relaxation operation after every failure and provide no procedure to restore the limits.
choices.explanation: This does not ensure restoration if a problem occurs.

choices.text: Set the repair step's onFailure to the restoration step and set isCritical to true.
choices.explanation: This proceeds to restoration while also reflecting the repair failure in the overall execution result.

choices.text: Make restoration the success path after repair, and immediately abort on failure.
choices.explanation: If the repair fails, the restoration step does not run.

learning.reason: This proceeds to restoration while also reflecting the repair failure in the overall execution result.
learning.concept: Define both the normal path and a failure path that restores state after an operation has begun.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Separate permissions for startup and application execution
prompt: An ECS task definition for Fargate injects environment variables from Secrets Manager. The application updates DynamoDB while running, but does not call the Secrets Manager API itself. Where should you attach the minimum required permissions? Select two.

choices.text: Bake the secret, including its value, into the image.
choices.explanation: This bypasses the secure retrieval provided through the task definition and leaves the value in the artifact.

choices.text: Grant the task execution role permission to update DynamoDB.
choices.explanation: The application's API calls do not use the task execution role's credentials.

choices.text: Put all permissions in fixed access keys inside the container.
choices.explanation: This loses both permission separation and the use of short-term credentials.

choices.text: Grant the task execution role the permissions needed to retrieve the secret.
choices.explanation: ECS retrieves the value needed to start the container.

choices.text: Grant the task role narrowly scoped DynamoDB operations.
choices.explanation: This separates the AWS credentials the application uses inside the container.

learning.reason: ECS retrieves the value needed to start the container. The application can use separate AWS credentials inside the container.
learning.concept: Distinguish operations performed by the ECS agent at startup from those performed by the container's code after startup.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
