title: Keep Pods on the Same Node Within Separate Permission Boundaries
prompt: A single Pod in EKS needs read access to a specific S3 prefix. Do not add permissions to the node role, and the Pod Identity Agent can be installed. How should the permissions be associated with the Kubernetes service account?

choices.text: Distribute IAM access keys to all Pods through a ConfigMap.
choices.explanation: This widely distributes long-term credentials instead of limiting them to the target workload.

choices.text: Create only a Kubernetes RoleBinding and assume that it also grants IAM authorization for S3 API calls.
choices.explanation: Kubernetes RBAC within the cluster and permissions for AWS APIs are separate.

choices.text: Create a Pod Identity association for the target namespace and service account with a narrowly scoped IAM role.
choices.explanation: The corresponding Pods in the namespace can use the specified role.

choices.text: Add S3 permissions to the node role and rely on the convention that only the target Pod will use them.
choices.explanation: This does not isolate the permissions from other workloads on the same node.

learning.reason: The corresponding Pods in the namespace can use the specified role.
learning.concept: Associate IAM permissions with the workload's service account instead of granting them to the entire node.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Decrypt Application Ciphertext in the Recovery Region
prompt: An application encrypts small control data with a symmetric KMS key and replicates the ciphertext to another Region. The recovery application cannot connect to KMS in the original Region. How should this be designed in advance so the ciphertext does not need to be re-encrypted? Select two.

choices.text: Grant the recovery-side application permission to decrypt by using the related replica.
choices.explanation: Authorize use based on the key policy in each Region.

choices.text: Disable rotation of the original key and decrypt in the recovery Region with a different key.
choices.explanation: Disabling rotation does not allow a different key to decrypt the original ciphertext.

choices.text: Use a multi-Region key on the original side and place a related replica in the recovery Region.
choices.explanation: The two keys are related keys that can handle the same ciphertext.

choices.text: Add an IAM permission to use the original key and use the single-Region key from the original Region through the recovery-side endpoint.
choices.explanation: The keys do not have cross-Region compatibility.

choices.text: Create independent single-Region keys in both Regions and treat them as the same key by giving them the same alias.
choices.explanation: Matching alias names do not make the keys shared.

learning.reason: The two keys are related keys that can handle the same ciphertext. Authorize use based on the key policy in each Region.
learning.concept: Compatibility of key IDs and key material is separate from configuring which principals are authorized in each Region.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Reduce Key Request Costs While Keeping SSE-KMS
prompt: A large number of small objects are stored in an S3 bucket. SSE-KMS is required, but requests to KMS account for most of the cost. For objects covered by future requests, how can KMS calls be reduced while keeping the encryption method?

choices.text: Change the default encryption to SSE-S3 and treat it as using the same key as SSE-KMS.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to keep SSE-KMS.

choices.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and expect it to reduce the number of KMS requests as well.
choices.explanation: Optimizing the transfer path does not reduce the number of key calls made for SSE-KMS.

choices.text: Lengthen the KMS rotation interval to eliminate encryption requests for all objects.
choices.explanation: Changing the interval for key material updates does not reduce key use for each access.

choices.text: Enable S3 Bucket Key in the bucket's SSE-KMS configuration.
choices.explanation: This can reduce the number of requests required between KMS and S3.

learning.reason: This can reduce the number of requests required between KMS and S3.
learning.concept: Configure at-rest encryption for objects separately from the frequency of key retrieval calls.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Restore a Scheduled-for-Deletion Existing Secret
prompt: An operator scheduled a Secrets Manager secret for deletion. The recovery window is still open, and the application can no longer retrieve it using its existing ARN. How can the secret be restored so the same ARN and saved versions can be used again?

choices.text: Run RestoreSecret on the secret to cancel the deletion schedule.
choices.explanation: The original secret and its versions can be retrieved again.

choices.text: Wait until the recovery window ends, then manually restore the previous value to the existing ARN.
choices.explanation: After permanent deletion, the same secret cannot be restored.

choices.text: Create a new secret with the same name and assume that it will inherit the previous ARN and saved versions.
choices.explanation: Creating a new secret does not restore the original resource and its saved versions.

choices.text: Reschedule rotation only, without changing the deletion date.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the secret's scheduled-for-deletion state, in which it cannot be retrieved.

learning.reason: The original secret and its versions can be retrieved again.
learning.concept: A secret scheduled for deletion cannot be read, but the deletion schedule can be canceled while the recovery window remains open.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Centrally managing an organization-wide default standard and a limited exception
prompt: Use Security Hub CSPM central configuration. Apply the default settings to new accounts in the organization, but use a different approved standard for one validation OU. Do not allow individual accounts to manage their own settings. Which association should you use?

choices.text: Attach the default to the root and set the exception OU to self-managed so each department can configure it separately.
choices.explanation: This does not enforce the centrally approved exception standard.

choices.text: Associate the default policy with the root and directly associate a different policy with the exception OU.
choices.explanation: Regular child accounts inherit the default, while the direct association takes precedence for the exception OU.

choices.text: Change only the EventBridge notification conditions for the exception OU.
choices.explanation: Changing the notification path does not change the standard or control settings.

choices.text: Apply both the default and exception configuration policies to one account at the same time.
choices.explanation: Only one configuration policy can be applied to an account or OU at a time.

learning.reason: Regular child accounts inherit the default, while the direct association takes precedence for the exception OU.
learning.concept: Use inheritance in the organizational hierarchy and the precedence of an association attached directly to a child.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Applying an organization-wide WAF policy to new ALBs
prompt: Apply common AWS WAF rules to ALBs in multiple member accounts. You want them automatically associated, including ALBs created in the future in the target OU, without requiring each team to configure them individually. What should you choose?

choices.text: Apply a Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy to the target OU and ALBs, and enable automatic remediation.
choices.explanation: This deploys common settings to resources in scope and can address noncompliance.

choices.text: Have each team select the same managed rule names manually each month, then associate them with newly created resources later.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to include new resources automatically.

choices.text: Create a Config aggregator and assume that WAF is automatically configured on the ALBs it displays.
choices.explanation: A configuration aggregation path does not deploy web ACLs.

choices.text: Create one web ACL in the management account and assume it will be automatically associated with ALBs throughout the organization by name alone.
choices.explanation: This does not specify a central policy or deployment to the target resources.

learning.reason: This deploys common settings to resources in scope and can address noncompliance.
learning.concept: Distinguish organization-wide rule deployment from rule evaluation within an individual web ACL.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Checking a specified data range for sensitive information
prompt: Determine whether objects migrated to a specified S3 prefix contain personal information. Limit the scope to those objects, and classify their contents rather than evaluating only permissions or access logs. What should you use?

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer to evaluate external sharing only.
choices.explanation: Analyzing sharing policies does not reveal the types of data stored.

choices.text: Run an Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job scoped to the target S3 bucket and prefix.
choices.explanation: It can inspect supported data and return sensitive information discovery findings.

choices.text: Use S3 Inventory to check only for SSE-KMS, and treat encrypted objects as containing no personal information.
choices.explanation: Encryption status is separate from whether data is sensitive.

choices.text: Collect only CloudTrail GetObject records and use the identities of readers as the sensitive information discovery results.
choices.explanation: The records can identify who performed the operation, but they do not classify object contents.

learning.reason: It can inspect supported data and return sensitive information discovery findings.
learning.concept: Distinguish checking access settings from data discovery that examines object contents.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Assessing supported EC2 instances that are not managed by SSM
prompt: Some EC2 instances cannot have SSM Agent installed for operational reasons. They run a supported OS, use EBS for the root volume, and meet the required conditions. What should you choose to assess OS packages with Amazon Inspector without installing an agent?

choices.text: Choose agent-based scanning only and expect to get results while the instances remain unmanaged by SSM.
choices.explanation: The instances do not meet the SSM management requirement for the agent-based approach.

choices.text: Configure ECR basic scanning and also assess the EC2 OS packages.
choices.explanation: ECR images and running EC2 instances are different scan targets.

choices.text: Use Inspector hybrid scanning to assess eligible unmanaged EC2 instances without an agent.
choices.explanation: It can inspect packages on supported EBS-based EC2 instances from snapshots.

choices.text: Enable GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring as a substitute for an inventory of package vulnerabilities.
choices.explanation: Runtime findings and an assessment of installed packages are different.

learning.reason: It can inspect packages on supported EBS-based EC2 instances from snapshots.
learning.concept: Distinguish in-instance inventory collection from assessment performed on a volume.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Check usage before narrowing a policy
prompt: An operational role’s IAM policy has grown over many years, and you want to remove permissions for services that are not being used. Before removing them, you want to see the latest time each service was accessed during a recent period. What should you review?

choices.text: Check resource tags and treat any permission without a tag as unused.
choices.explanation: Resource attributes do not provide a role’s usage history.

choices.text: Use only an external access analyzer to assess which services in the organization’s roles are unused.
choices.explanation: Findings about external sharing of resource policies do not show access times.

choices.text: Review IAM service last accessed information.
choices.explanation: Service-level access times can inform decisions about narrowing permissions.

choices.text: Look only at the year in the policy’s Version field and remove every permission that has not changed for a long time.
choices.explanation: The policy language version does not indicate whether a permission is used.

learning.reason: Service-level access times can inform decisions about narrowing permissions.
learning.concept: Distinguish permissions that have been granted from a history of actual access attempts.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Decrypt existing data after rotation
prompt: You enable automatic rotation for a customer managed symmetric KMS key with AWS generated key material. You are told that existing ciphertext will become undecryptable unless it is immediately re-encrypted. How should you assess this claim?

choices.text: Assign the same alias to a different KMS key so that it can automatically decrypt the old ciphertext.
choices.explanation: Changing the logical key is different from updating key material within the same key.

choices.text: Existing ciphertext can normally be decrypted as is. KMS manages the key material from before rotation.
choices.explanation: The same logical key is used, and the material corresponding to the existing ciphertext is selected.

choices.text: All previous key material is deleted immediately after rotation, so decrypt and store all ciphertext first.
choices.explanation: Standard rotation does not immediately invalidate old key material.

choices.text: Enabling automatic rotation causes AWS to rewrite all ciphertext in storage.
choices.explanation: Rotation does not automatically update data stored by an application.

learning.reason: The same logical key is used, and the material corresponding to the existing ciphertext is selected.
learning.concept: Distinguish updating key material within one logical KMS key from migrating to a new key.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Allow only CloudFront requests to a private S3 bucket
prompt: An existing site points CloudFront to an S3 website endpoint, and users can retrieve content directly from the S3 URL. After the change, you want to store content using SSE-KMS, block public access, and allow reads only from a specified distribution. Which two measures should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Check the origin only by its URL Referer and continue allowing anonymous S3 reads.
choices.explanation: This does not block public access or scope IAM authorization to the specified distribution.

choices.text: Only redirect viewer HTTP requests to HTTPS, and assume that this also blocks public access to the S3 URL.
choices.explanation: The viewer communication policy does not change direct-access permissions to S3.

choices.text: Switch to a regular S3 bucket endpoint and configure a signing OAC for CloudFront.
choices.explanation: OAC cannot be used with an S3 website endpoint.

choices.text: Scope S3 read and KMS permissions for the CloudFront service principal to the specified distribution’s SourceArn.
choices.explanation: This can tie the permissions required to access SSE-KMS origin data to the specified distribution.

choices.text: Keep the website endpoint as a custom origin and add only OAC.
choices.explanation: OAC does not support website endpoints.

learning.reason: OAC cannot be used with an S3 website endpoint. The permissions required to access SSE-KMS origin data can be tied to the specified distribution.
learning.concept: When signed access from CloudFront is required, align the origin type with the bucket’s authorization.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Separate encryption defaults for new volumes from migration of existing volumes
prompt: An AWS account has two Regions in use, and some existing unencrypted EBS volumes remain. You want future new volumes to be encrypted and existing data to be migrated to encrypted volumes. What scope does the default setting affect?

choices.text: Add Encrypted to each existing volume’s tags; data protection is applied whenever a tag with that name exists.
choices.explanation: Tags do not change a volume’s encryption state.

choices.text: Change application traffic to HTTPS to encrypt data already stored in EBS.
choices.explanation: Encryption in transit and block storage encryption are separate.

choices.text: Enable encryption by default in each Region in use, and separately migrate existing unencrypted volumes to encrypted volumes.
choices.explanation: Encryption by default must be enabled per Region and does not automatically change existing volumes.

choices.text: Enable it in one Region, and the existing and new volumes in the other Region will also be encrypted automatically.
choices.explanation: The setting is regional and does not apply retroactively to existing volumes.

learning.reason: Encryption by default must be enabled per Region and does not automatically change existing volumes.
learning.concept: Enabling a default for newly created resources does not migrate resources created in the past.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Avoid updating existing instances during a faulty release
prompt: You are deploying a new version to the same Elastic Beanstalk environment. You must keep the old version's capacity unchanged while the new version is launched in a temporary, separate Auto Scaling group and checked for health. You want to avoid having to recreate the old instances if the deployment fails. Which deployment policy should you use?

choices.text: Choose an Immutable deployment.
choices.explanation: The new version starts in a separate group and replaces the existing instances only after passing health checks.

choices.text: Do not set a deployment policy; only extend the retention period for saved application versions.
choices.explanation: This does not change how instances are replaced or checked for health during deployment.

choices.text: Choose a Rolling deployment and handle the capacity reduction for each temporary batch within the existing group.
choices.explanation: This updates existing instances in sequence and does not preserve the old version's capacity.

choices.text: Choose All at once and redeploy the old application to every instance after an error.
choices.explanation: This policy updates all running resources at once.

learning.reason: The new version starts in a separate group and is checked for health before it replaces the existing instances.
learning.concept: Choose between updating existing instances in sequence and replacing them with additional healthy instances.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Retain the version in use while cleaning up the registry
prompt: The number of Elastic Beanstalk application versions is growing and nearing the registration limit. You want to automatically clean up old versions beyond a specified count, but you cannot delete a version that an environment is using. Which setting should you configure?

choices.text: Set a short deletion period for the source bundle's S3 key and leave Elastic Beanstalk's registration state unmanaged.
choices.explanation: Deleting the physical files in S3 does not manage the application's registration limit.

choices.text: Disable all automatic deletion of old versions until the environments are terminated.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to clean up unused versions while keeping environments running.

choices.text: Reduce the deployment batch size so the number of retained versions adjusts automatically.
choices.explanation: The startup batch setting does not affect cleanup of registered application versions.

choices.text: Set a maximum count in the application version lifecycle policy.
choices.explanation: This cleans up old, unused versions while retaining versions that are in use by an environment.

learning.reason: This cleans up old, unused versions while retaining versions that are in use by an environment.
learning.concept: Distinguish registered application versions from the versions referenced by running environments.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Create a test environment from a running environment's configuration
prompt: A tester needs to create a new Elastic Beanstalk environment and reuse the option settings from an existing environment. The running environment must remain unchanged, and the tester needs to choose the application version to evaluate. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Replace the application version in the running environment with the test version, without copying its configuration.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to create a new environment without changing the existing one.

choices.text: Create a Saved configuration from the existing environment and use it to configure the new environment.
choices.explanation: You can reuse the settings and choose a different application version.

choices.text: Copy the source bundle under a different name and assume that this also copies all of the existing environment's option values.
choices.explanation: The application version alone does not carry over the complete set of current environment settings.

choices.text: Copy only the DNS CNAME and use it as the new environment's option settings.
choices.explanation: A name-resolution setting is not an environment configuration template.

learning.reason: You can reuse the settings and choose a different application version.
learning.concept: The environment's option settings and the version of the code deployed to it can be specified separately.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Swap the public name after validating a separate environment
prompt: During a Beanstalk platform migration, you run two environments in parallel and manage their shared database outside the environments. After validation, you want the existing environment URL to direct traffic to the new version, while retaining the old environment so you can roll back. Which operation should you perform?

choices.text: Swap the CNAMEs of the old and new environments, and keep the old environment until DNS propagation and validation are complete.
choices.explanation: This points the same public name to the new environment while preserving the option to switch back.

choices.text: Move the new environment's instances into the old environment's Auto Scaling group without changing the environment URL mapping.
choices.explanation: This only mixes the managed resources and does not switch traffic to the target environment.

choices.text: Rename the shared database and expect the Beanstalk public URL to point to the new environment automatically.
choices.explanation: The database name and the environment CNAME are separate.

choices.text: Delete the old environment, then recreate an environment with the same name, assuming the public name will be available for immediate reuse.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirements for parallel operation and rollback.

learning.reason: This points the same public name to the new environment while preserving the option to switch back.
learning.concept: Manage the lifetime of each independent runtime environment separately from the environment that a public name points to.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Integrating an Unsupported Internal Deployment System
prompt: A company wants to add its internal deployment system to CodePipeline. No existing action provider supports it, and an internal worker performs the operation. The pipeline must receive the result and have the final outcome reported back. Which integration should be used?

choices.text: Poll the source frequently and match completion of internal jobs to source changes.
choices.explanation: Changes to source detection do not define how to report the exact result of an external job.

choices.text: Register a custom action, and have the job worker retrieve and acknowledge the job, then report success or failure.
choices.explanation: This lets the external execution result be reflected in the pipeline.

choices.text: Run the worker asynchronously and always report success as the final result to CodePipeline.
choices.explanation: A failed release could proceed to the next stage.

choices.text: Use Manual approval and consider the job complete when an operator reads the notification, without returning the external system's result.
choices.explanation: Whether the deployment succeeded is not tied to the pipeline job.

learning.reason: This lets the external execution result be reflected in the pipeline.
learning.concept: Associate the receipt and completion of external processing with the same job in the pipeline.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Choosing Whether to Store an Artifact as a ZIP or Extract It
prompt: A CodePipeline build artifact is a ZIP containing files for a website. After deployment, the individual files must be in S3 rather than the archive. No separate extraction job will be added. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Set Extract to false and specify only the ZIP filename for distribution as ObjectKey.
choices.explanation: This places a single archive in S3 rather than individual files.

choices.text: Enable S3 versioning and treat the uploaded ZIP version as if it were extracted.
choices.explanation: Versioning does not extract an archive.

choices.text: Enable Extract in the S3 deploy action.
choices.explanation: This deploys the artifact's contents as individual files.

choices.text: Add a lifecycle rule to the destination bucket and configure extraction on the first read.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle rules control retention and storage classes.

learning.reason: This deploys the artifact's contents as individual files.
learning.concept: Even for the same artifact, choose the object granularity required by the destination.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Expiring Only Old Development Images
prompt: An ECR lifecycle policy is being introduced. A single image may have both a release tag to retain and a dev tag to clean up. How should the team verify what will expire before applying the policy, including the priority order of multiple rules?

choices.text: First delete every image matching the dev tag, then check whether any targeted images also had a release tag.
choices.explanation: This makes an irreversible change instead of checking beforehand.

choices.text: Set rule priorities and use Lifecycle policy preview to inspect the candidates.
choices.explanation: This shows the actual candidate selection for images with multiple tags.

choices.text: Enable tag immutability and assume it automatically previews which images will expire.
choices.explanation: Immutability controls tag reuse; it does not evaluate the lifecycle policy.

choices.text: Specify rules in the order they were added and do not check priorities or the actual candidates.
choices.explanation: This does not verify evaluation order or the effect of multiple tags.

learning.reason: This shows the actual candidate selection for images with multiple tags.
learning.concept: Set priorities according to the policy examples, then inspect the actual candidates for combinations of tags.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Checking the Network Requirements for the First Pull
prompt: A workload uses ECR pull through cache and runs in a private subnet with an ECR VPC endpoint. It is pulling an uncached image from an external registry for the first time. Which prerequisite should be verified?

choices.text: Assume that the ECR endpoint alone is sufficient for every first pull, even when the cache is empty.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the documented internet connectivity requirement for the initial pull.

choices.text: Add an S3 gateway endpoint and route the upstream access required for the first pull through it.
choices.explanation: An S3 route does not provide a path to the external registry.

choices.text: Extend ECR image retention and treat images that have not been pulled as already cached.
choices.explanation: Extending retention does not cache an image that has not been pulled.

choices.text: Provide an internet route for the initial pull.
choices.explanation: This meets the initial-pull requirement for pull through cache with PrivateLink.

learning.reason: This meets the initial-pull requirement for pull through cache with PrivateLink.
learning.concept: Distinguish the path for reading an artifact that is already cached from the path for retrieving it from upstream for the first time.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Automate signing for selected new container images
prompt: In the organization’s ECR, only images under the production prefix should be signed with AWS Signer when pushed. How should this be configured without maintaining signing logic in each pipeline, given that signature verification is enforced through a separate process? Select two.

choices.text: Configure tag immutability only and treat tags that cannot be reused as proof that the images are signed.
choices.explanation: Tag immutability does not create a cryptographic signature for an image.

choices.text: Enable ECR enhanced scanning and convert vulnerability findings into signatures.
choices.explanation: Scanning produces findings about images; it does not attach signatures.

choices.text: Configure an ECR managed signing rule with a filter for the target repositories and a Signer profile.
choices.explanation: The rule determines which signing configuration is used when a target image is pushed.

choices.text: Add a separate signing step to every pipeline and maintain the same configuration for each team.
choices.explanation: This still requires maintaining signing logic in each pipeline.

choices.text: Grant the principal that pushes the target images the permissions required to sign with that profile.
choices.explanation: Managed signing can use the identity of the principal that pushed the image.

learning.reason: The rule determines which signing configuration is used when a target image is pushed, and managed signing can use the identity of the principal that pushed it.
learning.concept: The path that creates a signature is separate from the path that verifies a signature before execution.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Collect all diagnostics even when an early test fails
prompt: A CodeBuild batch runs several independent tests in parallel. If any test fails, the remaining tests must continue so that all results are collected. The batch failure itself must still be recorded. What should you do?

choices.text: Set fast-fail to false and do not use a setting that ignores failures for individual tests.
choices.explanation: This preserves failure results while allowing the other builds to continue.

choices.text: Set fast-fail to true and assume the batch will wait for all other results after the first failure.
choices.explanation: The batch stops the remaining builds.

choices.text: Set ignore-failure on every test so the batch does not record a failure.
choices.explanation: The tests can continue, but the batch will not record the failure as required.

choices.text: Disable parallel execution and terminate the shell as soon as the first test fails.
choices.explanation: The remaining results cannot be collected.

learning.reason: The other builds can continue while the failure result is retained.
learning.concept: Distinguish whether the batch exits early from whether each build’s failure is included in the final result.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Retain raw data after a build report expires
prompt: Test reports from CodeBuild must be available for audit reference for six months, longer than the service’s report-retention period. Auditors need the original XML files. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Set the batch timeout to six months and assume each report will be retained for the same period.
choices.explanation: Execution time and report-retention periods are unrelated.

choices.text: Export raw files from the report group to S3 and configure S3 retention for the audit period.
choices.explanation: The XML remains available after the CodeBuild report expires.

choices.text: Copy test names to CodeBuild tags and reconstruct all results from the tags if an issue occurs.
choices.explanation: Tags do not store report contents.

choices.text: Extend the CloudWatch Logs retention period to six months and assume all XML files are copied to the logs automatically.
choices.explanation: The retention setting for console logs does not store test files.

learning.reason: The XML remains available after the CodeBuild report expires.
learning.concept: Keep the retention period for source files needed for audit separate from that of summary results shown in the console.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Read a custom build image from another account
prompt: A CodeBuild project in one account must use an ECR image from the organization’s image account as its environment image. Limit sharing to the role for this dedicated project. Which configuration should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Make the ECR image anonymously public and expect only projects within the organization to retrieve it.
choices.explanation: Authorization does not restrict image retrieval to the dedicated role.

choices.text: Grant the role the required ECR retrieval permissions and also allow that principal in the repository on the providing account’s side.
choices.explanation: This satisfies both authorization requirements for cross-account ECR access.

choices.text: Grant permission to pull the environment image only in the final phase of the buildspec.
choices.explanation: The environment image is needed before build commands start.

choices.text: Select CodeBuild’s default credentials for image pulls to restrict access to the dedicated role.
choices.explanation: This does not select the service role that should be allowed to retrieve the image.

choices.text: Set the build project’s image-pull credentials to SERVICE_ROLE.
choices.explanation: The specified service role’s permissions are used to retrieve the custom image.

learning.reason: The specified service role’s permissions are used to retrieve the custom image, and both authorization requirements for cross-account ECR access must be met.
learning.concept: Choose the identity used to pull the build environment image and authorize that identity to retrieve it.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Preserve pre-existing host-specific configuration
prompt: A host-specific configuration file exists on EC2 deployment targets. It was not included in the previous successful deployment. The new version instructs CodeDeploy to place a default configuration file at the same location. You want to preserve the host-specific file on existing hosts and place the default on new hosts. What should you do?

choices.text: Deploy the new version as a rollback and use the healthy-host threshold in DeployConfig to decide whether to preserve the conflicting file.
choices.explanation: The minimum number of healthy hosts does not determine the file handling policy.

choices.text: Set file_exists_behavior to OVERWRITE and assume the host-specific file will remain if its mtime is newer.
choices.explanation: The existing contents are replaced by the file in the revision.

choices.text: Keep the default DISALLOW setting and expect only the conflicting file to be ignored while the deployment succeeds.
choices.explanation: The deployment fails when a conflict occurs.

choices.text: Set file_exists_behavior to RETAIN in the AppSpec file.
choices.explanation: An existing file at the target location is retained, while the version's file can be copied where no file exists.

learning.reason: An existing file at the target location is retained, while the version's file can be copied where no file exists.
learning.concept: Choose how to handle a conflict with a pre-existing file that did not come from the previous deployment.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Declare post-copy permissions without adding scripts
prompt: You are copying a configuration file to Linux on EC2 with CodeDeploy. You want to specify the file's owner and mode in the target directory on every deployment. Where should you declare these settings in AppSpec without adding a shell hook?

choices.text: Set the deployment group's tag to the same value as the owner and assume the tag is converted into a Linux user.
choices.explanation: Tags are used to select targets; they do not become file owners.

choices.text: Specify only destination in the files section of AppSpec, include the owner in the path name, and use the path to set permissions.
choices.explanation: A path name alone does not change the owner or access mode.

choices.text: Write the Linux file mode in the IAM policy for the CodeDeploy service role and have it applied automatically after the copy.
choices.explanation: IAM permissions do not define file modes on the operating system.

choices.text: Specify the target path, owner, and mode in the permissions section of AppSpec.
choices.explanation: You can declaratively apply the required settings to copied files.

learning.reason: You can declaratively apply the required settings to copied files.
learning.concept: Separate the definition of where a file is placed from the definition of permissions applied after placement.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Determine whether rollback reverses side effects beyond the application
prompt: CodeDeploy for EC2 automatically rolled back a bad version to the last known good version. An external configuration change appended by a hook remained in place. For safe recovery in the future, which explanation and response are correct?

choices.text: The last known good version is deployed as a new deployment. Design hook side effects so they can be explicitly reversed.
choices.explanation: CodeDeploy does not automatically undo changes made by arbitrary scripts.

choices.text: Rollback restores a full backup of the instance, so the remaining external configuration should be considered a temporary display shown before success.
choices.explanation: Redeploying an application version does not restore a full snapshot of the operating system or external services.

choices.text: Reduce only the deployment group's concurrency; this restores the previous external state.
choices.explanation: Deployment concurrency does not compensate for hook side effects.

choices.text: Delete the previous successful version's revision information and let CodeDeploy infer the external configuration from before the change.
choices.explanation: Deleting a revision does not restore the previous value of an external setting.

learning.reason: CodeDeploy does not automatically undo changes made by arbitrary scripts.
learning.concept: Distinguish redeploying a version from restoring consistency after external changes made by hooks or the application.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Build native dependencies for a different runtime environment
prompt: A SAM Lambda function uses a native library. The development machine's OS differs from the Lambda runtime, and an extension packaged locally cannot be loaded in production. How should you build it with SAM?

choices.text: Build all native dependencies on the development machine, then distribute that ZIP to multiple Lambda runtimes without specifying the OS or architecture.
choices.explanation: The host-targeted binary remains incompatible with Lambda.

choices.text: Increase the Lambda memory and expect the memory setting to transform the unavailable native library.
choices.explanation: Changing memory does not transform a binary's format.

choices.text: Change only the deployment account name to the architecture name.
choices.explanation: Neither the runtime environment nor the native dependencies built for it change.

choices.text: Run sam build in a container using a compatible build image.
choices.explanation: Dependencies can be built in an environment similar to Lambda.

learning.reason: Dependencies can be built in an environment similar to Lambda.
learning.concept: Even with the same source, native dependencies must match the target OS and architecture.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Define build commands that share state
prompt: An older CodeBuild project uses buildspec version 0.1. At the start of `commands`, it changes to a subdirectory and prepares the environment, but the next command fails because that state is not carried over. How can you run multiple commands in the same shell without combining them into one long line?

choices.text: Enable log output and record the working directory so later commands automatically start there.
choices.explanation: Saving logs does not change the shell's working directory.

choices.text: Specify an S3 cache location and assume the shell process state is saved there too.
choices.explanation: A file cache does not save process environment variables or the working directory.

choices.text: Change the buildspec to version 0.2 and list the commands individually.
choices.explanation: The commands can run in the same shell, so changes such as changing directories affect subsequent commands.

choices.text: Keep version 0.1 and add only `export` at the end of each command to pass values to the next independent shell.
choices.explanation: Shell state created by one command is not carried over to the next command.

learning.reason: Commands can run in the same shell, so changes such as changing directories affect subsequent commands.
learning.concept: Distinguish a specification where each command runs in a separate shell from one where shell state carries over.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Omit a property based on an environment condition
prompt: Use the same template to deploy to multiple environments. Set the identifier of existing storage only in production; in other environments, omit the property itself instead of setting it to an empty string. Which expression should you use?

choices.text: Return AWS::NoValue in the false branch of Fn::If.
choices.explanation: In the false branch, this removes the target property from the template.

choices.text: Set only a Condition on a stack Output and leave the resource property unchanged in every environment.
choices.explanation: A condition on an output does not remove the target property.

choices.text: Set a literal empty string in the false branch of Fn::If and treat the property as unspecified for every resource.
choices.explanation: The value is still specified, and there is no guarantee this has the same meaning as omitting it.

choices.text: Put the production parameter name in DependsOn and change the order in development.
choices.explanation: This attribute specifies dependency order; it does not conditionally omit a property.

learning.reason: In the false branch, this removes the target property from the template.
learning.concept: Distinguish treating a property as unspecified from assigning it an empty value.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Read the centralized AMI setting again on stack update
prompt: The latest AMI ID is managed in Parameter Store, and a CloudFormation stack uses an SSM parameter key as an input. When the AMI value changes, you want the next normal stack update to read the latest value while passing the same key. What should you define?

choices.text: Pass the parameter key to an AWS::SSM::Parameter::Value type and update the stack.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation uses the parameter's current value in the resource configuration.

choices.text: Write the AMI shown in Systems Manager Inventory to the Outputs section.
choices.explanation: This does not reference the centralized parameter from the deployment configuration.

choices.text: Assume that using the same key automatically replaces the EC2 AMI even without updating the stack.
choices.explanation: Changing an external parameter does not automatically update existing resources.

choices.text: Use the String type, copy the AMI ID directly into the stack parameter's default value, and update without changing it.
choices.explanation: This does not read a new value from the centralized key.

learning.reason: CloudFormation uses the parameter's current value in the resource configuration.
learning.concept: Distinguish the key referenced by a stack input from the value read during an update.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Read an output from another Region during creation or update
prompt: An application CloudFormation stack in Tokyo needs an output value from an infrastructure stack in Osaka. They are in the same account, and the application does not need to update automatically whenever the infrastructure stack changes. Which method lets the application refer to the output during creation or update without copying the output elsewhere?

choices.text: Use Fn::GetAtt to specify a resource name in Osaka and request an arbitrary output from another stack.
choices.explanation: The usual Fn::GetAtt does not reference an arbitrary output from an independent stack in another Region.

choices.text: Export the output in Osaka and refer to it directly from Tokyo with Fn::ImportValue.
choices.explanation: Fn::ImportValue references are limited to the same Region.

choices.text: Use Fn::GetStackOutput and specify the Osaka Region.
choices.explanation: It can resolve an output value from another Region during creation or update.

choices.text: Use CodeBuild to read the Osaka output, copy it into the Tokyo configuration, and maintain a scheduled script that updates the Tokyo side.
choices.explanation: This adds unnecessary copying and scheduled updates for a value that can be resolved at deployment time.

learning.reason: It can resolve an output value from another Region during creation or update.
learning.concept: Distinguish resolving a value during creation or update from a strong reference that also controls changes to or deletion of the referenced stack.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Apply updated stack metadata to a running EC2 instance
prompt: At launch, an EC2 instance applies CloudFormation metadata with cfn-init. After launch, you want to rerun configuration whenever the corresponding stack metadata changes, without replacing the instance. What should you install?

choices.text: Move the metadata content to Outputs and keep the existing instance unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a way for EC2 to detect changes and apply the configuration.

choices.text: Configure cfn-hup and register a hook that runs cfn-init when the target metadata changes.
choices.explanation: It can detect changes while the instance is running and apply the specified configuration.

choices.text: Send cfn-signal when startup completes and assume it also monitors metadata changes.
choices.explanation: Notifying CloudFormation of initialization results does not continuously monitor for changes.

choices.text: Rely on UserData running automatically again for every update, without installing any post-launch configuration.
choices.explanation: This does not define post-launch monitoring or application of metadata changes.

learning.reason: It can detect changes while the instance is running and apply the specified configuration.
learning.concept: Separate a process that runs once at launch from one that periodically detects metadata changes.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Avoid unintended replacement during a custom resource update
prompt: A CloudFormation Lambda custom resource updates an entry in an existing DNS management service. The same entry was updated, but replacement occurred because the provider generated a new response ID each time. How should this be fixed?

choices.text: Return a changed PhysicalResourceId from the previous one and expect no replacement as long as the logical ID is unchanged.
choices.explanation: For a custom resource, a change to the physical ID indicates replacement.

choices.text: Omit the physical ID entirely from the update response and expect the previous value to be supplied.
choices.explanation: This fails to return a value required by the response contract.

choices.text: Return the same PhysicalResourceId in the response for an in-place update.
choices.explanation: This avoids replacement caused by returning a different physical ID.

choices.text: Return the CloudFormation RequestId instead of the PhysicalResourceId for each update.
choices.explanation: The ID changes with each request, so it does not identify the same resource.

learning.reason: This avoids replacement caused by returning a different physical ID.
learning.concept: For a custom resource, the provider's physical ID identifies the same resource.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Safely handle multiple change requests
prompt: Several operators manage the same StackSet, and some deployment operations overlap while others do not. Which feature runs nonconflicting operations in parallel and queues conflicting requests so they run one at a time?

choices.text: Enable StackSet ManagedExecution.
choices.explanation: It runs nonconflicting operations and queues conflicting operations.

choices.text: Change the Region order and leave the waiting order between operations undefined.
choices.explanation: Region ordering does not manage conflicts between separate deployment requests.

choices.text: Increase the maximum number of concurrent accounts for each operation and assume this also eliminates conflicts between operations.
choices.explanation: This changes only the concurrency within a single deployment.

choices.text: Enable automatic deployments and stop all manual updates without managing conflicts.
choices.explanation: This is not a way to safely process multiple requests.

learning.reason: It runs nonconflicting operations and queues conflicting operations.
learning.concept: Distinguish the number of accounts that can be deployed to in parallel within one operation from conflict management across multiple StackSet deployments.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Avoid rebuilding an asset because of unrelated files
prompt: The CDK packages a directory as a file asset. Test logs that change on every run are not needed in the deployment package, but they cause the asset to be recreated. Which configuration excludes those logs while continuing to detect changes to the actual source?

choices.text: Keep the generated logs in the asset unchanged and shorten only the retention period using the S3 destination's lifecycle policy to suppress hash changes.
choices.explanation: Logs included in the input contents affect the hash even if the retention setting changes.

choices.text: Exclude the logs so that only the deployment contents are included in the asset input.
choices.explanation: Asset recreation can then be determined solely by the contents intended for deployment.

choices.text: Set the asset hash to a fixed value and keep using that hash after the source changes.
choices.explanation: This would prevent changes to the actual source from being detected.

choices.text: Enable stack termination protection and expect it to automatically reduce the frequency of asset creation.
choices.explanation: Stack deletion controls do not affect the input hash.

learning.reason: Asset recreation can then be determined solely by the contents intended for deployment.
learning.concept: Distinguish the files whose changes should affect the hash from build artifacts.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Wait for the scheduled association interval before starting work
prompt: You have change approval and are preparing a State Manager cron schedule. You create the association during the day, but the first change must wait until the weekend cron interval; it must not run immediately after creation. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Run Run Command immediately, then delete the association over the weekend.
choices.explanation: This makes the change before the specified weekend.

choices.text: Set only the cron schedule and assume the association's default behavior will also delay its first run.
choices.explanation: By default, a new association might run immediately.

choices.text: Set a large MinDuration value to suppress the run immediately after creation.
choices.explanation: This is not the API setting for the desired initial cron behavior.

choices.text: Enable ApplyOnlyAtCronInterval and specify the cron schedule.
choices.explanation: This avoids a run immediately after creation and waits for the specified cron interval.

learning.reason: Avoid an immediate run and wait for the specified cron interval.
learning.concept: Separate the time an association is registered from the time its operation first runs.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Analyze instance software inventories centrally
prompt: Systems Manager Inventory has already been collected from managed nodes in multiple Regions. You want to sync package lists to a central S3 bucket and analyze them across Regions with SQL. Do not add commands that change the configuration. What should you use?

choices.text: Create OpsItems one at a time and use their completion times as package versions.
choices.explanation: Work records do not sync a node's software inventory.

choices.text: Start patching only and assume that details about all updated packages will automatically appear in central S3.
choices.explanation: This does not define a destination for synchronizing inventory data.

choices.text: Create an Inventory Resource Data Sync and sync it to a supported S3 destination.
choices.explanation: This aggregates configuration inventory for analysis.

choices.text: Create a Config aggregator and assume all OS packages are included as standard configuration items.
choices.explanation: This provides no path to sync and analyze the target SSM Inventory data.

learning.reason: This aggregates configuration inventory for analysis.
learning.concept: Separate collecting information from nodes from syncing that information to analytical storage.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Identify missing patches before installing them
prompt: Before change approval is granted for Windows managed nodes, you need to list the patches missing relative to a baseline. How can you update compliance information without updating the OS or rebooting?

choices.text: Set an automatic-patching maintenance window to the current time and run its default installation operation.
choices.explanation: This does not specify an inspection-only operation.

choices.text: Run AWS-RunPatchBaseline with Operation set to Scan.
choices.explanation: This scans for missing patches without installing them.

choices.text: Set Operation to Install and set only NoReboot.
choices.explanation: This can suppress a reboot, but it still installs patches.

choices.text: Exclude all patches from the baseline and make the node report itself as always compliant.
choices.explanation: This prevents you from identifying patches that are actually missing.

learning.reason: This scans for missing patches without installing them.
learning.concept: Separate checking compliance from installing a fix.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Apply an organization patch plan across Regions
prompt: You want to apply a common patch policy to your organization's managed nodes. You need to target specified OUs and supported Regions, with different schedules for scanning and installation. Which option avoids manually configuring settings in each account?

choices.text: Specify the scope, baselines, and times in a Quick Setup patch policy.
choices.explanation: You can manage the selected accounts and Regions with one policy.

choices.text: Create different tag names for patch targets in each account, and have an operator configure the policy and schedule.
choices.explanation: This does not provide centralized policy management and automatic application.

choices.text: Set all times in one maintenance window in the management account and expect it to apply unchanged to every node in the organization.
choices.explanation: This does not define the target scope or cross-account configuration.

choices.text: Set only the evaluation frequency of a Config rule and use it as the patch installation date.
choices.explanation: A compliance evaluation does not configure a patch application schedule.

learning.reason: You can manage the selected accounts and Regions with one policy.
learning.concept: Specify patch approval rules, target accounts, and scan and installation times separately.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Evaluate time limits even when resources do not change
prompt: You need an AWS Config custom rule that marks a resource noncompliant when a certain number of days have passed since its last change. You must detect the passage of time even if the resource does not change. Which evaluation mode should you use?

choices.text: Use a Config aggregator to display stale evaluations without performing new evaluations.
choices.explanation: This cannot determine when a resource became noncompliant.

choices.text: Trigger evaluations only on configuration changes, and assume unchanged resources will still be evaluated on their deadlines.
choices.explanation: If the resource is not updated, that reason will not trigger an evaluation.

choices.text: Stop the recorder until the deadline, then run a single manual inventory.
choices.explanation: This does not provide ongoing deadline-based evaluation.

choices.text: Set the rule to periodic evaluation so it also evaluates resources with no configuration updates.
choices.explanation: It can evaluate based on time even when no change event arrives.

learning.reason: The rule can evaluate based on time even when no change event arrives.
learning.concept: Rules whose results can change as time passes require evaluation that does not depend on configuration changes.

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Return the Same Configuration Variant to the Same Customer
prompt: Use AWS AppConfig multi-variant feature flags. Only users on the target plan should receive a different configuration, and the application can pass the same user attributes with each request. Which configuration should you use without distributing multiple application versions?

choices.text: Overwrite a single environment variable for each connection and do not isolate configuration for concurrent requests.
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate rules for each attribute, and values from concurrent executions can get mixed.

choices.text: Redistribute each plan as a separate application executable and have the feature flag return the same value.
choices.explanation: This does not handle the configuration as a variant in a shared application.

choices.text: Configure a variant rule that matches the plan attribute, and pass the matching context when retrieving the configuration.
choices.explanation: The same rule can evaluate requests consistently based on the attribute.

choices.text: Adjust the overall deployment percentage and assume that only users on the target plan will be identified, without passing an attribute from the application.
choices.explanation: A deployment percentage alone does not distinguish the plan of the requester.

learning.reason: The same rule can evaluate requests consistently based on the attribute.
learning.concept: Separate the configuration being deployed from the value selected based on each request's context.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Detect cross-Region replication delays against a deadline
prompt: Most new S3 objects must be replicated to another Region within 15 minutes. You also need notifications that identify objects delayed under the applicable rule. Which two features should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Disable versioning at the destination to reduce processing volume.
choices.explanation: This breaks a prerequisite for S3 replication.

choices.text: Set a seven-day lifecycle for all objects and make replication run at the same speed.
choices.explanation: A retention condition does not set a replication-time target.

choices.text: Subscribe to the replication event OperationMissedThreshold.
choices.explanation: The notification can identify objects whose replication exceeded the threshold.

choices.text: Run S3 Batch Operations once at month-end instead of replicating new objects as they arrive.
choices.explanation: This does not manage replication of new objects against a 15-minute target.

choices.text: Enable S3 Replication Time Control on the applicable replication rule.
choices.explanation: This applies a 15-minute replication target and SLA to new objects.

learning.reason: S3 Replication Time Control applies a 15-minute replication target and SLA to new objects, and notifications can identify objects whose replication exceeded the threshold.
learning.concept: Combine the feature that sets an operational replication target with the feature that notifies you about delayed objects.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Separate capacity for standby and analytics readers
prompt: With Aurora Serverless, one reader must maintain enough capacity to handle the writer's load before a failover. Another reader is dedicated to analytics and should be able to scale down independently when its read workload is low, even while the writer is under heavy load. How should you configure them?

choices.text: Set both to promotion tier 0 and assume only the analytics reader will scale down before the writer.
choices.explanation: Both high-priority readers follow the writer's capacity.

choices.text: Change only the reader monitoring frequency without configuring the relationship between promotion tier and capacity.
choices.explanation: Monitoring frequency does not change the required capacity-following behavior.

choices.text: Set the standby reader to promotion tier 0 or 1, and the analytics reader to tier 2 or higher.
choices.explanation: The first follows the writer's capacity, while the second can scale independently.

choices.text: Set both to tier 2 or higher and assume the standby reader will always maintain the same capacity as the writer.
choices.explanation: Lower-priority readers scale independently of the writer.

learning.reason: The standby reader follows the writer's capacity, while the analytics reader can scale independently.
learning.concept: Promotion tiers also affect how Aurora Serverless readers follow capacity.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Prepare instances with lengthy initialization before demand rises
prompt: An EC2 Auto Scaling application takes 10 minutes to initialize its dependencies. When demand increases, the application should not have to perform all of that work from scratch, and spare instances can remain stopped during normal operation. On-Demand Capacity Reservations alone are insufficient. What should be added?

choices.text: Configure a warm pool containing initialized instances.
choices.explanation: This lets the time-consuming preparation finish before demand increases.

choices.text: Enable only scale-in protection for EC2 instances.
choices.explanation: This does not initialize spare instances.

choices.text: Create only Capacity Reservations and initialize every instance from scratch when scaling out.
choices.explanation: This does not reduce application initialization time after launch.

choices.text: Only increase the health check grace period.
choices.explanation: This changes how instances are treated while they are becoming ready, but it does not move the preparation work earlier.

learning.reason: This lets the time-consuming preparation finish before demand increases.
learning.concept: Distinguish reserving compute capacity from keeping the application initialized and ready.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Adjust worker capacity to meet a backlog target
prompt: Auto Scaling workers process SQS messages. The current queue length rises and falls regardless of the number of workers, so the time messages spend waiting can vary even when the queue has the same length. Which metric should be used as the target to keep the processing backlog per worker steady?

choices.text: Use the cumulative number of instance launches without referring to the number of messages waiting in the queue.
choices.explanation: A cumulative count does not represent current load or the backlog per worker.

choices.text: Use the backlog per worker: the number of messages waiting to be processed divided by the number of in-service workers.
choices.explanation: This provides a target based on the backlog per worker relative to processing capacity.

choices.text: Use the queue's maximum retention period as the target metric.
choices.explanation: A retention setting is not an observed value that changes with current demand.

choices.text: Use only the total number of messages in the queue and treat it as the same load on one worker even when the minimum capacity increases.
choices.explanation: This metric does not account for changes in the number of workers and their processing capacity.

learning.reason: This provides a target based on the backlog per worker relative to processing capacity.
learning.concept: Choose a scaling metric whose value moves toward its target as capacity is added.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Prevent scale-in from terminating tasks only while they are working
prompt: Workers in an ECS service must redo their work if they are stopped during a long-running job. The service must remain able to scale in, and only tasks whose work is complete should become eligible for scale-in. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Set the placement strategy to spread and assume that all tasks in progress are automatically protected.
choices.explanation: This setting affects placement across AZs or instances; it does not protect tasks from scale-in.

choices.text: Permanently raise the service's minimum task count to its maximum.
choices.explanation: This prevents scale-in regardless of the status of individual jobs.

choices.text: Only increase the ALB response timeout for all tasks.
choices.explanation: Health check and HTTP connection settings do not provide scale-in protection.

choices.text: Enable task scale-in protection for tasks while they are working, and disable it when their work is complete.
choices.explanation: This prevents normal scale-in during work while allowing completed tasks to be removed.

learning.reason: This prevents normal scale-in during work while allowing completed tasks to be removed.
learning.concept: Keep scaling enabled while protecting individual tasks that should not be terminated before their work is complete.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Isolate a critical consumer from contention with other readers
prompt: Several standard consumers read shards from Kinesis. Write throughput is sufficient, but the monitoring consumer falls behind when reads by other consumers increase. How can the monitoring consumer be given independent, shard-level read throughput?

choices.text: Only increase the batch size on the writer to reserve read capacity for monitoring.
choices.explanation: Changing how writes are batched does not provide a separate read allocation for each consumer.

choices.text: Have the monitoring consumer call GetRecords more frequently and ignore the effect on other reads.
choices.explanation: This does not change the shared read capacity used by standard consumers.

choices.text: Reset the monitoring consumer's checkpoint to the oldest position each time and retrieve the same records repeatedly when shared reads are delayed.
choices.explanation: This does not provide independent read throughput.

choices.text: Register the monitoring consumer for enhanced fan-out and read with SubscribeToShard.
choices.explanation: This uses read throughput that is independent of the shared capacity used by other consumers.

learning.reason: This uses read throughput that is independent of the shared capacity used by other consumers.
learning.concept: Distinguish increasing overall system capacity from designing a consumer so it does not use shared read capacity.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Gradually increasing traffic to a new Region under the same name
prompt: Two healthy ALBs are published through Route 53 under the same domain name. During testing, the new Region should receive a small share of traffic, and that share should be increased gradually. Routing must not depend on users’ geographic locations. What should you configure?

choices.text: Shorten only the DNS TTL without specifying traffic proportions.
choices.explanation: This controls how long responses are cached, but does not specify a traffic proportion.

choices.text: Use failover routing with one ALB as primary and the other as secondary, and send a small amount of traffic to the secondary while the primary is healthy.
choices.explanation: This does not distribute traffic to the secondary by a chosen proportion while the primary is healthy.

choices.text: Use latency-based routing alone and expect it to produce the configured gradual proportions.
choices.explanation: This routes according to latency between Regions and does not apply explicitly configured weights.

choices.text: Create weighted records with the same name and adjust the weights of both records.
choices.explanation: DNS responses can be selected according to the desired relative proportions.

learning.reason: Weighted routing selects DNS responses according to the desired relative proportions.
learning.concept: DNS routing proportions control response selection, while caching causes actual traffic distribution to fluctuate.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Avoid discarding distinct business requests with identical bodies
prompt: Separate payment requests with identical bodies arrive in an SQS FIFO queue. Content-based deduplication discarded the second request. How can you ensure that only retries of the same business request are treated as duplicates during the five-minute deduplication interval?

choices.text: Pass the business request identifier as an explicit MessageDeduplicationId.
choices.explanation: Distinct requests remain distinguishable even when their bodies are identical, while retries of the same request can use the same ID.

choices.text: Change only the message attributes and assume content-based deduplication hashes the attributes too.
choices.explanation: Content-based deduplication does not include attributes in its identification.

choices.text: Generate a random deduplication ID for every retry.
choices.explanation: Retries of the same request are then treated as separate messages.

choices.text: Set only MessageGroupId to the customer ID and leave content-based deduplication unchanged.
choices.explanation: The deduplication identifier calculated from the identical body remains unchanged.

learning.reason: Distinct requests remain distinguishable even when their bodies are identical, while retries of the same request can use the same ID.
learning.concept: Choose the deduplication ID passed to the queue to represent whether the business request is the same, rather than whether its body is identical.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Launch equivalent nodes even when a specific type is unavailable
prompt: You are using Karpenter to provision Spot nodes for EKS. Pods require the same architecture and a minimum amount of memory, but the current NodePool is restricted to a single instance type that is unavailable, preventing the nodes from launching. What should you review?

choices.text: Keep the single instance type and increase only its maximum number of nodes.
choices.explanation: There is still only one candidate type, and it is unavailable.

choices.text: Remove all architecture constraints and select nodes on which the images cannot run.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the conditions required to run the Pods.

choices.text: Remove the PodDisruptionBudget to increase the number of Spot candidates.
choices.explanation: A PDB does not control the available instance type candidates for nodes.

choices.text: Retain the required architecture and capacity constraints, and include multiple compatible instance types and Availability Zones as candidates.
choices.explanation: This increases the chances of launching nodes without depending on one unavailable type.

learning.reason: This increases the chances of launching nodes without depending on one unavailable type.
learning.concept: Specify the resources an application requires separately from the alternative instance types that can provide them.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Support unpredictable I/O spikes relative to stored data
prompt: EFS burst credits have been exhausted, slowing processing on a shared file system. The amount of stored data is small, and peak throughput requirements are difficult to predict. How can you eliminate reliance on credits without provision­ing excessive fixed capacity?

choices.text: Switch EFS to Elastic throughput.
choices.explanation: Throughput adjusts to demand without relying on burst credits.

choices.text: Set Provisioned throughput to the forecast maximum and reserve the same capacity even when there is no peak.
choices.explanation: This can be used when performance limits can be estimated, but it does not meet the requirement to avoid excessive fixed capacity.

choices.text: Keep Bursting and shorten file retention, assuming that less stored data will increase throughput.
choices.explanation: Bursting baseline throughput is related to stored data, and this does not remove the dependency described in the requirement.

choices.text: Add mount targets within the Region and assume that this alone assigns separate credits to each client.
choices.explanation: The number of mount targets does not change the file system's throughput mode.

learning.reason: Throughput adjusts to demand without relying on burst credits.
learning.concept: Distinguish performance based on stored data and credits from a setting that adjusts throughput to demand.

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Avoiding dependency on another AZ’s NAT for outbound access
prompt: Several private subnets across multiple AZs share a single zonal NAT Gateway. When the AZ containing the NAT goes down, workers in healthy AZs also lose access to public dependencies. If you want to keep using zonal NAT Gateways, what should you change?

choices.text: Add a zonal NAT Gateway in another AZ, but keep the default routes of all private subnets pointing to the original NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: Traffic would still depend on the same AZ.

choices.text: Pin the destination IP addresses for each subnet and continue using a single NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: Pinning destination addresses does not avoid an AZ failure along the outbound path.

choices.text: Place a NAT Gateway in each AZ and route each subnet through the NAT Gateway in the same AZ.
choices.explanation: This isolates workers in other AZs from a NAT failure in one AZ.

choices.text: Only add a security group rule to the EC2 instance in the AZ containing the NAT Gateway.
choices.explanation: This does not remove the single-AZ dependency in the route.

learning.reason: This isolates workers in other AZs from a NAT failure in one AZ.
learning.concept: Network redundancy depends on the routes each subnet selects, as well as on the number of resources.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Catching brief congestion that a one-minute average could miss
prompt: A high-frequency job experiences congestion for only a few dozen seconds. The baseline monitoring interval is unlikely to capture the peak. You want to send custom metrics from the application at short intervals and create an alarm that can evaluate them in 10-second increments. Which two settings should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Configure a high-resolution alarm with a supported 10-second Period.
choices.explanation: The alarm can evaluate its condition over a shorter observation window.

choices.text: Set StorageResolution to 1 for each custom data point.
choices.explanation: This stores the metric at high resolution, with second-level granularity.

choices.text: Set the log retention period to 10 seconds and assume that all metrics will then have a 10-second period.
choices.explanation: Log retention and metric granularity are independent.

choices.text: Increase the number of evaluation periods for an existing one-minute alarm and make the measurements 10 seconds long.
choices.explanation: The number of evaluation points does not change the time resolution of the data points.

choices.text: Send standard-resolution, one-minute data and reconstruct it at a 10-second granularity.
choices.explanation: You cannot recover the breakdown of short intervals that were not measured.

learning.reason: This stores the metric at high resolution, with second-level granularity. The alarm can evaluate its condition over a shorter observation window.
learning.concept: Match the data storage resolution to the period over which the alarm aggregates data.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Analyzing older metrics at an available granularity
prompt: You tried to download six-month-old standard-resolution CloudWatch metrics at one-minute granularity, but the result was empty. You did not save the original history separately. How should you retrieve the available data?

choices.text: Repeat the one-minute retrieval with the same settings and wait for CloudWatch to decompose the aggregated data.
choices.explanation: Aggregated values cannot be converted back to the original one-minute data.

choices.text: Set metric log retention now and assume the one-minute data from several months ago will become available retroactively.
choices.explanation: Current log settings do not restore the granularity of historical metrics.

choices.text: Retrieve the data at one-hour granularity, which is supported for the retention period in question.
choices.explanation: Older data points are available in aggregated form at a coarser period.

choices.text: Assume that deleting the alarm for the metric will make the older detailed history available.
choices.explanation: Deleting an alarm does not affect metric retention granularity.

learning.reason: Older data points are available in aggregated form at a coarser period.
learning.concept: Metrics are aggregated to a coarser granularity as they age, and the original finer-grained data points cannot be recreated.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
