title: Keeping the same evaluation window across graphs with different time ranges
prompt: A CloudWatch Dashboard has monitoring graphs with a one-minute period. When you extend the displayed time range to several days, the aggregation period changes automatically, making sudden spikes harder to compare. How can you preserve each widget’s explicit period, as long as one-minute data is available?

choices.text: Set periodOverride to auto and assume the period will always remain the same regardless of the displayed time range.
choices.explanation: auto adjusts the period according to the time range.

choices.text: Set the dashboard’s periodOverride to inherit.
choices.explanation: This preserves the aggregation period specified for each widget.

choices.text: Change the alarm’s DatapointsToAlarm and apply the same setting to the dashboard’s displayed period.
choices.explanation: Alarm state evaluation and graph period settings are separate.

choices.text: Change only the dashboard’s default start time while keeping the aggregation-period rule.
choices.explanation: Changing the start of the displayed time range does not stop automatic period adjustment.

learning.reason: This preserves the aggregation period specified for each widget.
learning.concept: The displayed time range and the aggregation period used for graph data points are different settings.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Detecting Delivery Backlog Caused by Destination Throttling
prompt: Logs are continuously sent to Kinesis from a CloudWatch Logs subscription. Log ingestion continues, but the consumer stops receiving events intermittently. Which metric should you check first to determine whether the destination is throttling delivery?

choices.text: Check only the retention period in AWS/Usage to determine throttling at individual destinations.
choices.explanation: This does not measure why CloudWatch Logs delivery failed.

choices.text: Compare only IncomingLogEvents for the log group on a dashboard; if the value has not decreased, conclude that delivery succeeded.
choices.explanation: Log ingestion and subscription delivery are separate paths.

choices.text: Check DeliveryThrottling on the delivery side.
choices.explanation: This shows events that could not be forwarded because the destination throttled delivery.

choices.text: Search only the consumer's application logs and treat logs that never arrived as processed.
choices.explanation: This does not show the delivery status of events that did not reach the consumer.

learning.reason: This metric shows events that could not be forwarded because the destination throttled delivery.
learning.concept: Monitor whether input is arriving separately from whether the destination accepts it.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Detecting New, Unregistered Log Patterns
prompt: A frequent new error pattern appears in standard-class application logs, but existing filters do not catch it. You want to detect changes in the logs based on historical patterns without adding string thresholds one at a time. What should you use?

choices.text: Configure CloudWatch Logs anomaly detection for the target log group.
choices.explanation: It can learn patterns from event history and detect unusual occurrences.

choices.text: Configure anomaly detection only for the CloudWatch EC2 CPUUtilization metric.
choices.explanation: This does not learn new patterns in log messages.

choices.text: Create a filter that counts the fixed string ERROR.
choices.explanation: This can count a known string but cannot detect changes in unregistered patterns.

choices.text: Delete the log group frequently and create a new one each day to compare it with historical patterns.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the continuous data or detector needed for comparison.

learning.reason: It can learn patterns from event history and detect unusual occurrences.
learning.concept: Distinguish anomaly detection for numeric time series from detection of the occurrence and variation of log patterns.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Logging Slow Shard Queries
prompt: You are analyzing slow shard operations in a specific OpenSearch Service index. You enabled shard search slow-log publishing to CloudWatch Logs, but have not configured a threshold for the target index. What additional configuration is required?

choices.text: Extend only the CloudWatch retention period and assume that historical logs will be generated if the publishing path is enabled.
choices.explanation: The retention period does not configure a threshold in OpenSearch.

choices.text: Treat the domain-wide request slow-log settings as shard-level settings.
choices.explanation: The duration of an overall request differs from the duration of each shard operation.

choices.text: Configure the search slow-log threshold for the target index.
choices.explanation: A log is generated when shard processing exceeds the threshold.

choices.text: Increase the number of index replicas and assume slow-log generation is enabled automatically.
choices.explanation: An availability setting does not configure the condition that generates logs.

learning.reason: A log is generated when shard processing exceeds the threshold.
learning.concept: Configure the log delivery path separately from the conditions that cause a process to generate a log.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Finding Slow Spans by Attributes Other Than Transaction ID
prompt: More services have been instrumented with OpenTelemetry. When investigating latency affecting only certain customers, you need to filter and aggregate related spans by attributes such as customer tier or processing stage. Which CloudWatch feature should you use?

choices.text: Store all span attributes as the state value of a single composite alarm.
choices.explanation: A composite alarm does not provide a search interface for span data.

choices.text: Display only average response time on a CloudWatch Dashboard and reconstruct customer attributes from it.
choices.explanation: Span-specific attributes cannot be reconstructed from an average.

choices.text: Only narrow the log display range without ingesting OpenTelemetry spans.
choices.explanation: There is no span data available to analyze.

choices.text: Ingest spans into Transaction Search and query by attribute.
choices.explanation: You can use ingested spans to find specific operations and trends.

learning.reason: You can use ingested spans to find specific operations and trends.
learning.concept: Use service-wide time series metrics separately from attribute analysis of individual spans within a transaction.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Do Not Treat a Missing Observation Period as No Traffic
prompt: While investigating VPC Flow Logs during an incident, you find a record for the target interface with log-status set to SKIPDATA. Can you conclude that there were no rejected packets during that time period?

choices.text: SKIPDATA means there was no traffic, so all traffic during that time period was normal.
choices.explanation: This confuses SKIPDATA with a different status that indicates no traffic.

choices.text: No. SKIPDATA indicates that some records may have been omitted.
choices.explanation: Unobserved traffic is not evidence that the traffic did not exist.

choices.text: It means all packets moved to another AZ, so exclude the target interface from the investigation.
choices.explanation: This value does not indicate that traffic moved to another route.

choices.text: SKIPDATA means all traffic was rejected, so the results for each IP are conclusive.
choices.explanation: The record collection status does not indicate ACCEPT or REJECT.

learning.reason: Unobserved traffic is not evidence that the traffic did not exist.
learning.concept: Treat a period with omitted records differently from a period with no traffic.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Monitor Scenario Success and Response Time Separately
prompt: A scheduled Synthetics canary completes successfully, but its response time is increasing. You want to detect both a decline in success and an increase in duration even when an execution succeeds. What should you monitor?

choices.text: Use only Duration and treat the result as successful whenever the duration is normal.
choices.explanation: An execution can fail even if it completes quickly.

choices.text: Monitor SuccessPercent and Duration using separate conditions.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes an increase in failures from an increase in duration, including for successful executions.

choices.text: Use only SuccessPercent and assume that success will decrease when processing takes longer.
choices.explanation: The success rate may remain steady if the longer executions still succeed.

choices.text: Only increase the canary's schedule frequency, without evaluating success and duration separately.
choices.explanation: Increasing the number of observations does not assess the two measures individually.

learning.reason: This distinguishes an increase in failures from an increase in duration, including for successful executions.
learning.concept: The success rate does not directly indicate worsening duration, so monitor separate metrics.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Distinguish Function Duration from Processing Backlog
prompt: The time it takes for processed data to reach consumers is increasing for a Lambda function that reads from Kinesis. The function's Duration is nearly unchanged. Which metric should you use to investigate the backlog of stream input waiting to be processed by the function?

choices.text: Conclude that all input was processed immediately if the number of errors is steady.
choices.explanation: A backlog can build up on the stream side even when processing succeeds.

choices.text: Continue tracking only the maximum Duration, and conclude that the input backlog has not increased if it remains steady.
choices.explanation: The function's execution duration does not include time spent waiting before processing.

choices.text: Check the function's IteratorAge and, if it is increasing, investigate whether the consumer is keeping up with the stream.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch lets you track the age of records being processed.

choices.text: Use the SQS standard queue metric ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage as the age for this Kinesis stream alone.
choices.explanation: An SQS queue metric does not represent a backlog in a Kinesis stream.

learning.reason: CloudWatch lets you track the age of records being processed.
learning.concept: The handler's execution duration differs from the time elapsed since a processed record was added to the stream.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Run a Scheduled Historical Query and Deliver Its Results
prompt: You use an existing CloudWatch Logs Insights query to produce an hourly audit summary. You want to run the same summary automatically every day and place the results in an analytics S3 bucket. You do not want to add external polling code. What should you do? Select TWO.

choices.text: Save the query in the console and assume that it will run automatically.
choices.explanation: Saving a query is different from scheduling its execution.

choices.text: Delete the existing query and save only CloudWatch aggregate metrics.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the hourly audit summary requirements or the query results.

choices.text: Configure a Logs Insights scheduled query to run daily and specify an S3 destination.
choices.explanation: Scheduled delivery can send the query's aggregate results to the specified destination.

choices.text: Forward individual events with a subscription and assume that it will produce the same aggregated query results.
choices.explanation: Forwarding individual raw log events does not perform the existing aggregation.

choices.text: Grant the execution role the permissions needed to run the query and deliver the results to S3.
choices.explanation: The same role can be authorized to process the query and write to the destination.

learning.reason: Scheduled delivery can send the query's aggregate results to the specified destination. The same role can be authorized to process the query and write to the destination.
learning.concept: Distinguish continuous forwarding of log messages from delivery of query results aggregated over a time window.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Protect nodes not yet run when failures increase
prompt: You need to distribute an agent configuration to hundreds of nodes using SSM Run Command. Run the command on no more than 5 nodes at a time, and stop sending it to nodes that have not yet run if the permitted number of failures is exceeded. Commands already running may continue. Which settings should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Use only target tags to specify the node limit and stop-on-error behavior.
choices.explanation: Defining the target set does not control rollout speed or failure handling.

choices.text: Set MaxConcurrency to 5.
choices.explanation: This sets the maximum number of targets that can run the command concurrently.

choices.text: Set MaxErrors to the permitted value.
choices.explanation: This can stop command dispatch after the threshold is exceeded.

choices.text: Set the command delivery timeout to 5 seconds and set the number of nodes to receive the command to 5.
choices.explanation: A time value does not determine the number of nodes running concurrently.

choices.text: Set the number of permitted failures in the command's log retention period.
choices.explanation: The retention period does not determine whether commands are dispatched.

learning.reason: Set the maximum number of targets that can run concurrently. Stop command dispatch after the error threshold is exceeded.
learning.concept: Specify concurrency and whether to dispatch new executions after errors as separate settings.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Receive read-only API records through a rule
prompt: The CloudTrail trail records the relevant read-only management events. You have also added a matching pattern to the EventBridge default event bus, but processing of read-only management events does not start while the rule is in its normal Enabled state. What should you review?

choices.text: Set the rule to DISABLED and expect event processing to continue as long as the trail is enabled.
choices.explanation: The rule itself will no longer evaluate events.

choices.text: Change the pattern to data events for object operations.
choices.explanation: The required read-only management APIs are a different event category.

choices.text: Extend the CloudTrail log retention period, while keeping the event pattern and normal Enabled state unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the trail's retention period does not affect the EventBridge rule state.

choices.text: Set the rule to ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS.
choices.explanation: This includes read-only management events among the events the rule can match.

learning.reason: This includes read-only management events among the events the rule can match.
learning.concept: An event's presence in an audit record and whether a rule evaluates that event category are separate matters.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Authorize both sides when forwarding events centrally
prompt: Send only critical operational events from multiple accounts to a central EventBridge bus. When creating a new cross-account bus target, restrict incoming events to specified senders and use a dedicated role for the sending rule. Which two configurations should you combine? Select two.

choices.text: Make the central bus public and use only the source string in each event to authenticate the sender.
choices.explanation: A string in event data does not replace authorization of the sending principal.

choices.text: Use the central bus policy to restrict senders and allow PutEvents.
choices.explanation: The receiving bus can limit which accounts and other principals it permits.

choices.text: Allow PutEvents to the central bus in the IAM role used by the sending rule's target.
choices.explanation: This configures the sending side's execution permission to deliver events to the specified bus.

choices.text: Add arbitrary tags to all events and leave the bus policy unspecified.
choices.explanation: Tags do not grant permission to send events to the bus.

choices.text: Give the receiving side administrator permissions in all accounts instead of using a role from the sending account.
choices.explanation: This does not provide authorization limited to the specified sending role and target bus.

learning.reason: The receiving bus can restrict which accounts and other principals it permits. The sending side's execution permission can authorize delivery to the specified bus.
learning.concept: Cross-account event delivery requires authorization for the intended operation on both the sender and receiver sides.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Check OS startup when the network is unreachable
prompt: On a supported Nitro EC2 instance, the OS firewall was changed incorrectly, cutting off SSH and SSM Agent communication. Access to the Serial Console was approved in advance. Which path lets you investigate the cause from the OS without stopping the instance?

choices.text: Reassign the instance's public IP and expect the OS firewall to change as well.
choices.explanation: Changing the address does not change OS rules.

choices.text: Connect to the EC2 Serial Console and investigate.
choices.explanation: It provides access to the OS independently of the instance's VPC network connectivity.

choices.text: Retry Session Manager through the same SSM Agent.
choices.explanation: The required agent communication is cut off under these conditions.

choices.text: Add another bastion host in the same subnet and investigate using only SSH through the existing OS firewall.
choices.explanation: This uses a path that the OS firewall is blocking.

learning.reason: It provides access to the OS independently of the instance's VPC network connectivity.
learning.concept: When the instance's data-plane network is unavailable, use an independent management path.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Drain the service, then isolate the affected host
prompt: In an EC2 launch type ECS cluster, a container instance is scheduled for retirement. You want the scheduler to move tasks from existing ECS services, but a standalone RunTask workload may not be replaced automatically. What should you do?

choices.text: Force-terminate the instance and assume every task will always resume from the same state.
choices.explanation: A standalone task's state and progress are not carried over.

choices.text: Lower the CPU threshold and wait for scale-in without specifying the target instance.
choices.explanation: This does not manage which instance is retired or what happens to its existing tasks.

choices.text: Set the target to DRAINING and separately plan to stop or migrate standalone tasks.
choices.explanation: This allows service task replacement to proceed while making the handling of standalone tasks explicit.

choices.text: Change the task definition for the service but leave the affected instance ACTIVE.
choices.explanation: New tasks could still be placed on the same host.

learning.reason: This allows service task replacement to proceed while making the handling of standalone tasks explicit.
learning.concept: Tasks belonging to a service and tasks launched independently are handled differently during instance retirement.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Separate concurrency throttling from function errors
prompt: Some Lambda requests are rejected. The function's error count is unchanged, and the issue occurs only during periods when other workloads in the account increase. How should you first check for request admission limits rather than processing time?

choices.text: Inspect Throttles and concurrency, then compare them with the function and account limits.
choices.explanation: This can identify requests throttled before the function began executing.

choices.text: Look only for function configuration changes in CloudTrail, without comparing throttling metrics.
choices.explanation: This does not show the number of rejections during that period or their relationship to capacity.

choices.text: Infer the account's concurrency limit from the average Duration alone.
choices.explanation: This does not show requests that did not execute or the current limit value.

choices.text: Conclude that no requests were rejected because the function's Errors did not increase.
choices.explanation: Throttled requests are not included in Errors.

learning.reason: This can identify requests throttled before the function began executing.
learning.concept: Track separately requests that ran and failed and requests that could not begin execution.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Distinguish TTL deletions from operator deletions
prompt: An item disappeared from an MREC global table with TTL enabled. You want to determine whether it was deleted by the TTL service or explicitly by the application. By default, analyzing only the Streams in a replica did not reveal the service identity. What should you check?

choices.text: If a REMOVE event in any replica has no service principal, conclude that every deletion was performed by the application.
choices.explanation: A TTL deletion cannot be identified by principal information in a replica.

choices.text: Use only the REMOVE event type in the replica's Streams to classify TTL deletions versus other deletions.
choices.explanation: REMOVE indicates a deletion but does not identify its cause through principal information.

choices.text: Classify every historical deletion as a TTL operation based only on the current TTL setting.
choices.explanation: Whether the feature is enabled does not reveal the cause of an individual deletion.

choices.text: Check userIdentity on the deletion record in the Streams in the Region where TTL processing occurred.
choices.explanation: A TTL deletion in the source Region includes principal information identifying the DynamoDB service.

learning.reason: A TTL deletion in the source Region includes principal information identifying the DynamoDB service.
learning.concept: A replicated deletion does not necessarily have the same principal information as the deletion record in the source Region.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Don't mistake empty receives for an empty queue
prompt: The visibility timeout for a standard SQS queue is long, and the number of in-flight messages increased during an incident. A diagnostic using short polling returns OverLimit, while long polling returns no new messages. What should you check?

choices.text: Purge all messages and assume the original input can still be retained.
choices.explanation: This does not address what needs to be isolated and also loses the queue's business data.

choices.text: Check the number of received but undeleted in-flight messages, and fix the path that deletes messages once processing is definitely complete.
choices.explanation: When the limit is reached, the result can appear differently depending on the polling method.

choices.text: Conclude that the queue was empty because long polling did not return OverLimit.
choices.explanation: With long polling, no new messages may be returned when the limit is reached.

choices.text: Increase the message retention period and expect the in-flight limit to increase automatically every time.
choices.explanation: The retention period does not change the limit on messages already received.

learning.reason: When the limit is reached, the result can appear differently depending on the polling method.
learning.concept: Check the limit on messages already received but not yet deleted, not just the total number of unprocessed messages.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Set conditions for an individual subscription without changing the publisher
prompt: JSON-formatted events are published to SNS. The existing publisher cannot add attributes. You want to deliver only events whose body has stage set to production to one subscription. Where should you configure this?

choices.text: Restrict the topic permissions using the word production so that the same condition applies to all subscriptions.
choices.explanation: Topic permissions do not define delivery conditions based on the message body for a particular subscription.

choices.text: Set FilterPolicyScope to MessageBody on the target subscription and define the body condition.
choices.explanation: This evaluates the existing message body and filters delivery for that subscription alone.

choices.text: Change the publisher to send everything to a separate topic, then add a subscription.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to leave the existing publisher unchanged.

choices.text: Keep the default MessageAttributes and write the body’s stage condition in the policy.
choices.explanation: This checks attributes rather than the body, so it does not reference the required value.

learning.reason: This evaluates the existing message body and filters delivery for that subscription alone.
learning.concept: Separate the events that reach a topic from the conditions for forwarding them to each subscription.

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Retrieve execution input missing from a terminal event only when needed
prompt: You receive a failure event for a Step Functions Standard execution. The execution ARN is included, but some large inputs are omitted from the body when inputDetails.included is false. How can you retrieve the missing input after receiving the event without adding continuous polling?

choices.text: Assume that a successful CloudTrail record for StartExecution provides all execution data from the state machine.
choices.explanation: Checking the response to the start operation does not provide input omitted from the terminal event.

choices.text: Add InputPath to the EventBridge rule and expect it to automatically fill in input that is absent from the original event.
choices.explanation: Specifying an input path cannot retrieve data that was not included in the event.

choices.text: Treat an event with no input as proof that the execution itself had no input, and skip failure handling.
choices.explanation: Input not being delivered in the event is different from the execution having no input.

choices.text: Use the execution ARN from the event to retrieve the input with DescribeExecution when needed.
choices.explanation: You can inspect input associated with a Standard execution that was not included in the delivered event.

learning.reason: You can inspect input associated with a Standard execution that was not included in the delivered event.
learning.concept: Separate delivery of a failure notification from retrieval of detailed data associated with the execution.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Diagnose a denial that an account administrator cannot remove
prompt: A member account’s administrative role has IAM administrative permissions. An SCP on the parent OU explicitly denies an operation for a service, while a child OU has an SCP that allows the operation. What must be changed before the operation can be performed?

choices.text: Give the Allow in the child OU’s SCP higher priority so it overrides the explicit denial.
choices.explanation: SCPs have no such priority setting that cancels a denial.

choices.text: Remove the IAM permissions in the account so that the operation can be performed based on the SCP’s Allow alone.
choices.explanation: An SCP sets the maximum permissions available; it does not grant permission to perform an operation by itself.

choices.text: Review the explicit denial in the parent OU’s SCP within the approved scope.
choices.explanation: An Allow in a child OU or an administrative role’s permissions cannot override a denial from a parent.

choices.text: Assign the same administrative permissions to another role in the member account and use that role.
choices.explanation: The organization’s denial for the operation applies under the same OU.

learning.reason: An Allow in a child OU or an administrative role’s permissions cannot override a denial from a parent.
learning.concept: Check how a lower-level Allow and an inherited explicit Deny are evaluated in the hierarchy.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Restrict access to organizational resources by external principals
prompt: A target S3 resource in your organization also allows access from another account. Under your policy, you want the resource to enforce an organization-wide denial of access that does not meet specified conditions, including for external principals. The external principals’ accounts are outside the scope of your organization’s SCPs. Which policy should you use?

choices.text: Apply a Resource Control Policy to the account that contains the supported resource.
choices.explanation: It can set a permissions boundary for access to supported resources, including access by external principals.

choices.text: Use an organization tag policy to identify external principals and add a Deny to each S3 API.
choices.explanation: A tag policy does not define access permissions for resources.

choices.text: Only narrow the permissions boundary of your organization’s workload role.
choices.explanation: That boundary does not control external principals accessing the resource.

choices.text: Set an SCP on the external account in your organization and control only that account’s roles.
choices.explanation: You cannot apply your organization’s SCPs to accounts outside your organization.

learning.reason: It can set a permissions boundary for access to supported resources, including access by external principals.
learning.concept: Distinguish the organization boundary of the principal performing an operation from the organization boundary of the resource being acted on.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Use the Grant Token for the First Operation Without Waiting for Propagation
prompt: You created a grant to delegate limited permissions to a single principal for an AWS KMS operation. You want to use it in the same workflow immediately after creation, without waiting for eventual consistency to propagate. What should you pass to the corresponding API?

choices.text: Pass the GrantToken returned by CreateGrant to the corresponding KMS request.
choices.explanation: This lets the new grant be evaluated before propagation is complete.

choices.text: Set the application to retry indefinitely and assume the grant is available from the first request.
choices.explanation: This does not use a mechanism that makes the grant recognizable on the first request.

choices.text: Always allow every principal in the account through the key policy.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the limited scope of the delegation.

choices.text: Use the GrantId as an arbitrary encryption context value and treat it as equivalent to an authorization token.
choices.explanation: A grant ID is not a pre-propagation token for the request.

learning.reason: This lets the new grant be evaluated before propagation is complete.
learning.concept: Use a mechanism that lets the newly created grant be referenced before propagation, without broadening the long-term authorization configuration.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Keep Application Decrypt Permissions Away from Key Administrators
prompt: You use a customer managed KMS key. Allow the key administrators to describe the key and configure rotation, while allowing only the application role to decrypt. You also want to prevent administrators from adding decrypt permissions for themselves. Which policy should you use?

choices.text: Set the key tag name to DecryptionDisabled and leave the existing key policy and IAM permissions for cryptographic operations unchanged.
choices.explanation: This has no effect unless an IAM condition or key policy restricts key use.

choices.text: Allow both administrators and the application to use kms:* and rely on procedures to govern whether they use decryption.
choices.explanation: Authorization does not separate the two parties.

choices.text: Allow administrators only configuration operations; do not grant policy changes, grant creation, or decryption.
choices.explanation: This also prevents adding decrypt permissions through key policy changes or grants.

choices.text: Change the automatic rotation period and assume administrators will no longer be able to decrypt ciphertext created before the change.
choices.explanation: Rotation does not separate decryption permissions.

learning.reason: This also prevents adding decrypt permissions through key policy changes or grants.
learning.concept: Explicitly separate, by principal, permissions to change configuration from permissions to perform encryption and decryption.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Validate a Pinned WAF Rules Version Before It Expires
prompt: You have pinned an AWS Managed Rules version. You want to validate the next version before the current one expires and prepare for an unintended automatic switch. How can you obtain the number of days until expiry and information about new versions? Select two.

choices.text: Subscribe to the SNS topic for update notifications for the applicable managed rule group.
choices.explanation: You receive notifications about new versions and changes so you can begin validation in advance.

choices.text: Monitor DaysToExpiry in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This tracks the days remaining until the pinned version expires.

choices.text: Infer the version's expiry from the number of WAF requests.
choices.explanation: Request counts do not indicate a version's expiry date.

choices.text: Assume that enabling Count in WAF makes the version last indefinitely.
choices.explanation: A runtime rule action does not prevent expiry.

choices.text: Change the Web ACL's CloudWatch log retention period to set the rule version's expiry.
choices.explanation: Log retention and rule version lifetime are independent.

learning.reason: This tracks the days remaining until the pinned version expires. Notifications about new versions and changes let you begin validation in advance.
learning.concept: Plan rule changes using version expiry information and update notifications.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Avoid Duplicate Findings for the Same Control Across Standards
prompt: In a long-running Security Hub CSPM environment, the same control belongs to multiple enabled standards, and a finding is created for each standard. How can you treat the control's check result as a single finding without disabling any standards?

choices.text: Only lower the severity of duplicate findings and expect this to change how findings are created.
choices.explanation: Changing severity does not combine findings created for separate standards.

choices.text: Enable Consolidated control findings.
choices.explanation: This can generate one finding for a control shared by multiple standards.

choices.text: Deploy all the same standards to another member account and average the counts across the organization.
choices.explanation: This is not a setting that makes findings for the same control into one finding.

choices.text: Keep only one standard and disable all checks belonging to the others.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve all the requested standards.

learning.reason: This can generate one finding for a control shared by multiple standards.
learning.concept: The set of enabled standards and the finding unit for a shared control are separate concerns.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Detect unusual management API error rates with CloudTrail Insights
prompt: The CloudTrail trail already records write management events. You want to investigate an unusual increase in management API error rates instead of setting a fixed threshold for every API. Which feature should you add?

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail Insights ApiErrorRateInsight on the trail.
choices.explanation: It can detect unusual increases in error rates from the configured management events.

choices.text: Expand the S3 data event key scope and assume write-management error rates will be detected automatically in the same logs.
choices.explanation: Adding data events does not enable Insights analysis.

choices.text: Retain the log files in S3 for a set number of years, without creating anomaly notifications.
choices.explanation: Retention alone does not detect changes in error rates.

choices.text: Validate the trail's integrity digest and use it to determine whether error rates are anomalous.
choices.explanation: Integrity validation does not analyze event rates or normal baselines.

learning.reason: It can detect unusual increases in error rates from the configured management events.
learning.concept: Distinguish recording individual API operations from detecting changes that deviate from the usual rate.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Obtain AWS-wide third-party audit documentation
prompt: For a vendor assessment, you need the publicly available SOC report for AWS's service scope from the authorized source, rather than a configuration inventory of your active accounts. Where should you obtain it?

choices.text: Retrieve all IAM Access Analyzer findings and treat them as the provider's audit scope.
choices.explanation: Access assessments for your environment do not provide third-party audit documentation.

choices.text: Export the resource inventory from an AWS Config aggregator as the SOC report.
choices.explanation: Your configuration data is not AWS's third-party audit report.

choices.text: Retrieve the relevant SOC report from AWS Artifact Reports.
choices.explanation: It provides access to available AWS compliance documents.

choices.text: Verify CloudTrail event files' signatures and present them as an audit report for AWS services as a whole.
choices.explanation: This verifies record integrity; it is not the issuer of SOC reports.

learning.reason: It provides access to available AWS compliance documents.
learning.concept: Distinguish a cloud provider's third-party audit documentation from evidence of whether your own environment is compliant.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Choose the supported path to resolve landing zone drift
prompt: Drift has been detected in an AWS Control Tower landing zone because someone manually changed the managed baseline configuration. You want to identify the target, correct the relevant condition, and restore the original managed state. Which path should you use?

choices.text: Remove the resources from Control Tower management and maintain the baseline manually in each account.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to resolve drift while retaining managed baseline configuration.

choices.text: Change the guardrail notification destination and consider the existing drift resolved.
choices.explanation: Changing the notification destination does not correct the actual configuration.

choices.text: Manually edit the landing zone version shown in the inventory.
choices.explanation: This does not repair the actual managed state or expected configuration.

choices.text: Identify the type of drift and, when applicable, reset the landing zone to restore its managed state.
choices.explanation: Control Tower can reapply management of the active landing zone configuration.

learning.reason: Control Tower can reapply management of the active landing zone configuration.
learning.concept: For a baseline tracked by a management service, correct the cause and restore consistency through the supported remediation path.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Place CDN and load balancer certificates in the correct regions
prompt: Both the CloudFront alternate domain name and its origin, an ALB in Tokyo, use HTTPS. In which regions should you provision the ACM certificates for their respective associations?

choices.text: Create one certificate in Tokyo; the ACM ARN will be the same in other regions and can be associated with CloudFront.
choices.explanation: ACM certificates used by CloudFront for viewers have a regional requirement.

choices.text: Provision the certificate for CloudFront in US East (N. Virginia) and the certificate for the ALB in Tokyo, where the ALB is located.
choices.explanation: Each service can use a certificate provisioned in the region it can reference.

choices.text: Export the ACM certificate to S3 and specify its S3 URL from each listener.
choices.explanation: Association requires a registered certificate that the service can reference.

choices.text: Create one certificate in the region CloudFront references and assign that ARN directly to the Tokyo ALB listener as well.
choices.explanation: An ACM certificate for an ALB must be in the same region as the load balancer.

learning.reason: Each service can use a certificate provisioned in the region it can reference.
learning.concept: Separate the client-facing CDN from the regional origin where TLS terminates.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Connect management agents without creating a public path
prompt: You use SSM Agent on private EC2 instances. You do not use the internet or a NAT path, and you do not open SSH for inbound access. How should the instances connect to the services required for management operations and sessions? Select two.

choices.text: Allow an HTTPS path from the agent to the endpoints.
choices.explanation: The agent can initiate communication without inbound SSH access to the instance.

choices.text: Open only inbound SSH to the EC2 instance, without providing destinations for outbound service traffic.
choices.explanation: The agent has no required outbound path.

choices.text: Enable only CloudTrail management events in place of the Agent, and use the events as sessions.
choices.explanation: API audit records cannot establish an interactive session.

choices.text: Create the Systems Manager interface endpoints required by the Region and the agent.
choices.explanation: The required services for APIs and management sessions are reachable from within the VPC.

choices.text: Create only an S3 gateway endpoint and assume S3 relays management session messages.
choices.explanation: S3 alone does not provide the paths for Systems Manager APIs and sessions.

learning.reason: The required services for APIs and management sessions can be reached from within the VPC, and the agent can initiate communication without inbound SSH access to the instance.
learning.concept: Distinguish the outbound path used by the agent from inbound management ports on the instance.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Deliver configuration records to a central encrypted destination
prompt: AWS Config is already recording configuration changes. Separately from a CSPM, you need to deliver configuration history to an S3 bucket in a central account using SSE-KMS. You want to grant only the permissions required from the recording account to the central destination. Which combination should you use? Select two.

choices.text: Create only an AWS Config aggregator and assume the results will be stored in central S3.
choices.explanation: Viewing aggregated data and delivering configuration history to S3 are separate functions.

choices.text: Allow anyone to write to the central S3 bucket and omit KMS key authorization.
choices.explanation: This violates both the least-privilege and SSE-KMS requirements.

choices.text: Specify the KMS key to use and authorize the required delivery principal to use it in the key policy.
choices.explanation: In addition to bucket permissions, the principal must be able to perform the required SSE-KMS operations.

choices.text: Specify the central S3 bucket in the delivery channel and allow writes in the bucket policy, scoped to the Config delivery principal and source.
choices.explanation: This allows delivery to the specified S3 bucket in another account.

choices.text: Increase the recording frequency for each recorder and assume this automatically grants access to the central key.
choices.explanation: Recording frequency does not authorize use of a key in another account.

learning.reason: This allows delivery to the specified S3 bucket in another account. In addition to bucket permissions, the principal must be able to perform the required SSE-KMS operations.
learning.concept: Authorization to retrieve recorded data is separate from authorization to access the destination and encryption key.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Continuously evaluate backup retention policies
prompt: You need to continuously audit whether backups for multiple protected resources are created with the specified retention periods. You want to evaluate the conditions in an AWS Backup environment as a control, without changing how backups are created. Which feature should you use?

choices.text: Evaluate the retention conditions in an AWS Backup Audit Manager framework.
choices.explanation: It supports continuous compliance evaluation for backup operations.

choices.text: Increase only the number of copies in backup vaults, without evaluating the retention conditions.
choices.explanation: Copies are a protection measure, but adding copies does not assess whether the requirements are met.

choices.text: Define the retention conditions only in S3 audit logs and rely on account owners to report the retention periods for AWS Backup recovery points.
choices.explanation: A setting for a different storage layer does not evaluate backup retention.

choices.text: Run restores every day and assume success means the retention period is met for every recovery point.
choices.explanation: A successful restore does not prove compliance with each retention period.

learning.reason: It supports continuous compliance evaluation for backup operations.
learning.concept: Separate the settings that run backups from those that evaluate the settings or recovery points for compliance.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Pass a runtime queue URL to a downstream stack
prompt: In CodePipeline, you create a queue for each environment and then update a worker stack in a downstream CloudFormation action. The queue URL is in the Outputs of the upstream stack. Because the template is reused elsewhere, you cannot hardcode an export name or a pipeline variable reference. How can you pass the runtime URL to a downstream parameter?

choices.text: Provide the Outputs JSON in TemplateConfiguration and use the same name for an output and a worker stack parameter.
choices.explanation: TemplateConfiguration requires a prescribed structure, such as Parameters; matching an output key to a parameter name does not map the values.

choices.text: Set Fn::GetArtifactAtt's ObjectKey in the downstream ParameterOverrides to reference the same output artifact.
choices.explanation: ObjectKey returns the key of the artifact in S3, not a value from within the JSON.

choices.text: Make the upstream stack's Outputs a JSON artifact, then use Fn::GetParam in the downstream ParameterOverrides.
choices.explanation: This retrieves the queue URL created in that pipeline execution from the JSON included in the downstream input.

choices.text: Set Fn::ImportValue in the default value of the QueueUrl parameter to reference the upstream action's output artifact name.
choices.explanation: An artifact name is not a CloudFormation export, and a parameter default cannot use that intrinsic function.

learning.reason: This retrieves the queue URL created in that pipeline execution from the JSON included in the downstream input.
learning.concept: Parameter override functions for a CloudFormation deployment action.

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Find the first failing commit in a long change history
prompt: A contract test fails immediately after a release. There are many changes, including merges, between the last known-good commit and the current failing commit. A deterministic test can be run at each commit. Which approach should you choose to locate the point of failure while minimizing the number of test runs and without changing the shared branch?

choices.text: In a temporary clone, specify the good and bad endpoints and run the contract test with git bisect run.
choices.explanation: This narrows down the candidates in the history and locates the point of failure without updating the shared branch.

choices.text: Run git blame on the deployment configuration file and inspect every commit that last changed each current line.
choices.explanation: The history of current lines alone does not cover dependency files or past test failures on lines that were later changed.

choices.text: Compare the good and bad endpoints with git diff and treat the commit that most recently changed a file as the point of failure.
choices.explanation: A file diff between the endpoints cannot identify the first commit at which the test failed.

choices.text: In a temporary clone, inspect commits one by one from newest to oldest and run the contract test at each commit.
choices.explanation: This does not change the history, but it does not use a search method that reduces the number of test runs.

learning.reason: This narrows down the candidates in the history and locates the point of failure without updating the shared branch.
learning.concept: Binary search between known-good and known-bad endpoints

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: A build that exceeds the project limit fails immediately
prompt: The database used for contract tests accepts at most two builds at a time. After setting the CodeBuild project’s concurrent build limit to 2, a third start request returns an immediate error while two builds are running. Which design preserves the limit without losing start requests?

choices.text: Keep the limit at 2, increase the CodeBuild reserved fleet capacity to 3, and let the fleet start the excess build.
choices.explanation: Increasing compute capacity does not override the limit for the same project.

choices.text: Raise the limit to 3 and shorten each build’s execution timeout to reduce database connections.
choices.explanation: A shorter execution timeout does not prevent three builds from connecting concurrently.

choices.text: Keep the limit and increase the project’s queuedTimeoutInMinutes so the third build remains in the queue longer.
choices.explanation: A queue waiting time does not apply to a request whose start was rejected.

choices.text: Keep the limit, persist start requests, and retry them when capacity becomes available.
choices.explanation: A start request that exceeds the project’s concurrent limit fails, so the request must be retained.

learning.reason: A start request that exceeds the project’s concurrent limit fails, so the request must be retained.
learning.concept: Project concurrency limits and retrying start requests

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Include both output files with the same name
prompt: CodeBuild generates billing/dist/config.json and ledger/dist/config.json. Which buildspec setting meets the requirement to preserve the distinction between the source-root directories billing and ledger and include only these two files in one ZIP archive?

choices.text: Set the artifact base-directory to an asterisk and specify dist/config.json under files, preserving the base-directory names.
choices.explanation: The matched base-directory names themselves are not included in the artifact paths.

choices.text: Set the artifact base-directory to billing and list dist/config.json and ledger/dist/config.json under files.
choices.explanation: ledger is not under billing, so the latter path does not refer to the expected file.

choices.text: Specify both paths individually under files and set discard-paths to no.
choices.explanation: This selects both files relative to the source root and preserves their relative directories in the ZIP.

choices.text: Specify both paths individually under files and set discard-paths to yes.
choices.explanation: The directories would be removed, so the two files could not be distinguished by their paths.

learning.reason: This selects both files relative to the source root and preserves their relative directories in the ZIP.
learning.concept: Artifact path hierarchy and discard-paths

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Target production instances in one of two rings
prompt: In a CodeDeploy EC2 deployment group, you want to select instances whose Environment is prod and whose Ring is either canary or early. The same Ring tags also exist in test environments. Which conditions should you specify to select the instances without changing the existing tags?

choices.text: Put each condition in a separate tag group and require a match in all three groups.
choices.explanation: The same Ring key cannot have both values, so both Ring conditions cannot be satisfied at the same time.

choices.text: Put Environment=prod and a Ring condition with the value canary,early in one tag group.
choices.explanation: A comma in the value does not split the condition; moreover, the environment condition alone would select instances in the same group.

choices.text: Put the environment condition in one tag group and both Ring conditions in another.
choices.explanation: At least one condition must match in each group, which limits the selection to production instances in either ring.

choices.text: Put Environment=prod, Ring=canary, and Ring=early in one tag group.
choices.explanation: Conditions within one group are ORed, so test instances that match only a Ring condition would also be included.

learning.reason: At least one condition must match in each group, which limits the selection to production instances in either ring.
learning.concept: AND between tag groups and OR within a group

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Lambda Deployment Stalls After a Successful Validation Log
prompt: In a CodeDeploy Lambda deployment, the BeforeAllowTraffic hook passes its synthetic check and exits without an exception. The deployment waits for the hook result and eventually fails. How should the check result be reported to CodeDeploy?

choices.text: Increase the Lambda timeout, log the successful check to CloudWatch Logs, and wait for CodeDeploy to process the log.
choices.explanation: CodeDeploy does not determine hook success from log text.

choices.text: Call PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus with the two IDs included in the hook event.
choices.explanation: CodeDeploy determines the result from an explicit status report for the lifecycle event.

choices.text: Have the hook return HTTP 200 and use a deployment alarm to confirm that the Lambda Errors metric is zero.
choices.explanation: An alarm is a separate stop condition and does not replace the hook callback.

choices.text: Add permission to invoke the hook to the CodeDeploy service role, then return the DeploymentId from the function when the check succeeds.
choices.explanation: The hook has already been invoked, and an ordinary return value cannot resolve the pending result.

learning.reason: CodeDeploy determines the result from an explicit status report for the lifecycle event.
learning.concept: Explicit callbacks for CodeDeploy validation hooks

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Restrict ZIP Deployments to an Approved Signing Profile
prompt: A financial Lambda function is deployed as a ZIP. Lambda must reject unsigned ZIPs and ZIPs signed with a test profile when the function code is replaced. The deployment role is already restricted. Which two additional settings are needed? Select two.

choices.text: Associate the function with a code signing configuration that allows the version ARN of the approved signing profile.
choices.explanation: This specifies which signing source the function trusts and distinguishes it from test and other profiles.

choices.text: Set the signing configuration to Warn, then use a CloudWatch alarm on SignatureValidationErrors to detect failures.
choices.explanation: Warn can make violations visible, but still allows the code to be deployed.

choices.text: Set the AWS Signer profile name as a Lambda environment variable and have the function check the code deployment at startup.
choices.explanation: By startup, the code has already been deployed; an environment variable does not replace deployment-time signature settings.

choices.text: Set the deployment policy for untrusted artifacts to Enforce and sign deployment ZIPs with the approved profile.
choices.explanation: Enforce requires signature validation and rejects noncompliant new ZIPs.

choices.text: Tag deployment ZIPs as S3 objects with SignerApproved=yes and configure the signing settings to check the tag value.
choices.explanation: An S3 tag is not a basis for trust in Lambda code signing validation.

learning.reason: Specify the signing source the function trusts to distinguish it from test profiles. Enforce signature validation to reject noncompliant new ZIPs.
learning.concept: AWS Signer allowed profiles and Enforce

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Convert Local Build Artifact Paths for Deployment
prompt: The build of a SAM application is complete. Its artifacts consist of ZIP-based function code and a template that references local paths. A job without deployment permissions must put the code in S3 and pass a template with rewritten references to the deployment job. Which procedure should be used?

choices.text: Run sam build again and have a CloudFormation action reference the build output directory directly.
choices.explanation: A local path in the build environment does not let CloudFormation in a later job retrieve the code.

choices.text: Use sam validate and confirm that the validated template contains converted S3 references.
choices.explanation: Template validation does not upload artifacts or rewrite references.

choices.text: Run sam package on the built template and pass the output template containing S3 references.
choices.explanation: This places the artifacts in S3 and rewrites their references without applying a CloudFormation stack.

choices.text: Run sam deploy as usual and pass the stack update result to the next job.
choices.explanation: A standard deployment applies the stack, so it does not fit the separation of duties where code placement happens first.

learning.reason: Place the artifacts in S3 and rewrite their references without applying a CloudFormation stack.
learning.concept: SAM packaging and stack deployment

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Deployment Succeeds, but the Initialization Script Does Not Run
prompt: An Elastic Beanstalk environment is being migrated to Amazon Linux 2023. The source ZIP contains a parent directory named release, with application code, .platform, and .ebextensions beneath it. How should the ZIP be created so that the platform hooks and extension configuration are loaded?

choices.text: Place the contents of release at the ZIP root, including .platform and .ebextensions.
choices.explanation: The hooks and extension configuration are then in their required locations relative to the root.

choices.text: Keep the parent directory and use a CodeDeploy AppSpec to copy the hidden directories to the ZIP root.
choices.explanation: CodeDeploy AppSpec is not used to reassemble an Elastic Beanstalk source bundle.

choices.text: Keep the ZIP with its parent directory and have the application startup command run cd release before detecting the hooks.
choices.explanation: The platform processes hooks relative to the extracted source root before application startup.

choices.text: Put only .ebextensions at the ZIP root and keep .platform in the application's public directory.
choices.explanation: The extension configuration is found, but the platform hooks are no longer in their required location.

learning.reason: The hooks and extension configuration are then in their required locations relative to the root.
learning.concept: Root directory structure of an Elastic Beanstalk source bundle

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Managed Platform Updates for a Production Environment
prompt: You need to apply patch and minor platform updates to an Elastic Beanstalk environment on a regular schedule. You want to keep the current application version and have AWS validate and replace instances during a fixed maintenance window. The application deployment policy cannot be changed. What should you configure?

choices.text: Change the application deployment policy to Immutable and redeploy the current application version every week.
choices.explanation: Redeploying the application alone does not update the platform, and this would not preserve the existing deployment policy.

choices.text: Enable managed platform updates and set a maintenance window and the update level to minor.
choices.explanation: This applies minor and patch updates within the platform branch during the scheduled window and validates new instances using an immutable approach.

choices.text: Set the managed platform update level to patch and apply minor versions by regularly deploying the current application version.
choices.explanation: Minor versions are not included in automatic updates when you select patch.

choices.text: Schedule an EC2 Auto Scaling instance refresh and use the current launch configuration.
choices.explanation: Replacing instances with the current launch configuration does not select an Elastic Beanstalk platform version.

learning.reason: This applies minor and patch updates within the platform branch during the scheduled window and validates new instances using an immutable approach.
learning.concept: Separating platform updates from application deployments

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Reverting a Change on a Shared Release Branch
prompt: An incorrect launch configuration was introduced in a single commit, G, on a protected shared release branch. A later monitoring fix is also needed, and the reversal must be recorded through the normal review and deployment process. Which operation should you choose if there are no diff conflicts?

choices.text: Reset the branch to G's parent commit and force-push, then reapply the monitoring fix later.
choices.explanation: This rewrites published history and does not follow the normal change process for a protected branch.

choices.text: Cherry-pick the monitoring fix after G onto another branch and merge that branch into the release branch.
choices.explanation: Bringing in the monitoring fix does not undo the changes introduced by G.

choices.text: Run git revert G to create a commit with the inverse changes, then submit it for review as a normal change.
choices.explanation: This undoes G's changes while preserving the shared history and the later monitoring fix.

choices.text: Restore the configuration file from the tree of G itself to a working branch, then submit it for review.
choices.explanation: This restores the state that includes G, so the configuration change introduced by G remains.

learning.reason: This undoes G's changes while preserving the shared history and the later monitoring fix.
learning.concept: An inverse-change commit that preserves published history

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Verifying Published Package Assets
prompt: A specified version of a library exists in CodeArtifact. Release verification must check both the dependency sheet and the binary distributed with it, along with their known SHA-256 hashes, before proceeding. How can you verify these without installing the package?

choices.text: Check the Published status returned by list-package-versions to determine the corresponding filenames and hashes.
choices.explanation: The publication status of a version does not provide filenames or hashes for its individual assets.

choices.text: Compare the revision returned by describe-package-version directly with the known SHA-256 hash of the binary.
choices.explanation: A revision identifies the state of the package version; it is not the SHA-256 hash of the binary.

choices.text: Compare the filenames and hashes returned by list-package-version-assets for the specified version with the release manifest.
choices.explanation: The identifiers and checksums of each asset in the version let you verify their presence and integrity.

choices.text: Get dependency names from list-package-version-dependencies and use them to check whether both the dependency sheet and binary are present.
choices.explanation: A package's dependencies do not identify individual assets included in that same package version.

learning.reason: The identifiers and checksums of each asset in the version let you verify their presence and integrity.
learning.concept: Assets and hashes associated with a package version

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Passing a Validation Result JSON to the Next Action
prompt: Start an existing Step Functions Standard workflow from CodePipeline, then have a downstream CodeBuild validation read the completed result JSON as an input file. You cannot change the workflow's output format or create a separate persistence process. Which configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: In the downstream action, use the output variable ExecutionArn as the input filename and read the execution metadata as JSON.
choices.explanation: ExecutionArn is a variable that identifies the execution; it is not a file that contains the workflow output.

choices.text: Change the workflow to Express, set ExecutionOutput on the same invocation action, and retrieve the completed output quickly.
choices.explanation: A CodePipeline Express invocation is treated as complete after it starts and does not support output artifacts.

choices.text: Set OutputType to ExecutionInput on the Step Functions invocation action and pass the output artifact to the next input.
choices.explanation: The invocation action has no OutputType setting, and the input to an execution is different from the execution result the validation needs.

choices.text: Declare an output artifact on the Step Functions invocation action and set it as the input to the downstream CodeBuild action.
choices.explanation: The output available when a Standard execution completes can be passed as JSON.

learning.reason: The output available when a Standard execution completes can be passed as JSON.
learning.concept: Configuring Step Functions Standard execution results as pipeline artifacts

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Safely applying an ECS replacement and an independent monitoring change
prompt: A CloudFormation stack uses the AWS::CodeDeployBlueGreen transform. A single update includes an image change to an ECS task definition and a threshold change to an independent CloudWatch alarm in the same stack. How should you apply the update while preserving the ECS phased deployment?

choices.text: Use a CloudFormation change set to display the task definition update first, then execute that same change set.
choices.explanation: The display and review order does not change which changes are included in the same execution.

choices.text: Add a DependsOn relationship from the alarm to the ECS service and apply both in the same stack update.
choices.explanation: Adding a dependency order still leaves a change unrelated to the green deployment in the same update.

choices.text: Change the linear traffic shift to an all-at-once shift and apply both changes in the same stack update.
choices.explanation: Changing how traffic is shifted does not change the restriction on stack updates that trigger a green deployment.

choices.text: Put the task definition replacement and the alarm configuration change in separate stack updates, and confirm each one completes.
choices.explanation: An update that starts a green deployment must not include changes to unrelated resources.

learning.reason: An update that starts a green deployment must not include changes to unrelated resources.
learning.concept: The permitted scope of updates for CloudFormation-managed ECS blue/green deployments

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Choosing compute for a job that builds Docker images
prompt: After moving to Lambda compute with a standard CodeBuild image, a short unit test succeeds, but another job cannot start the Docker daemon that requires privileged mode. You must keep the short test in the Lambda environment and continue using the current Docker build procedure. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Keep both jobs on Lambda compute and increase the memory only for the project that runs the Docker build.
choices.explanation: Lambda memory settings cannot enable privileged mode.

choices.text: Combine both jobs on EC2 compute and create the container immediately after the unit test in the same build.
choices.explanation: The Docker build can run, but this does not preserve the configuration in which the short test finishes first in a Lambda environment.

choices.text: Keep both jobs on Lambda compute and add ECR upload permissions to the execution role for the Docker build.
choices.explanation: Write permissions to a registry and privileged mode for the Docker daemon are separate constraints.

choices.text: Move only the Docker build to an EC2 environment that supports privileged mode.
choices.explanation: Only the job that depends on privileged mode, which Lambda does not support, needs to be moved to a compatible environment.

learning.reason: Only the job that depends on privileged mode, which Lambda does not support, needs to be moved to a compatible environment.
learning.concept: Privileged mode limitations of CodeBuild Lambda compute

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Changing the priority of the source for the same package version
prompt: In a downstream CodeArtifact repository, the same package version is available from two direct upstream repositories with different verified identifiers. The downstream has retained the version from the previously higher-priority upstream because it was fetched earlier. After swapping their priority, how can you verify that the version can be fetched from the new upstream without affecting all users?

choices.text: Keep the upstream configuration of the downstream repository in use, clear the local caches for all builds, and then request the version.
choices.explanation: Clearing local caches does not remove a version already retained by the CodeArtifact downstream repository and would affect users.

choices.text: Swap the priorities in the downstream repository in use and simply request the same version from it to confirm that the new upstream's content is returned.
choices.explanation: Once a version has been retained, changing the upstream order does not overwrite it.

choices.text: Change the package version in the new upstream to Unlisted and check where the version resolves without changing the existing downstream's priorities.
choices.explanation: Unlisted changes whether a version appears in listings; it does not redirect a retained version to a new upstream.

choices.text: Create a test downstream with the new priority order that has not yet retained the version, then request the version through that repository.
choices.explanation: If the version has not been retained, the direct upstreams are searched in priority order, so you can verify the behavior without affecting the downstream in use.

learning.reason: If the version has not been retained, the direct upstreams are searched in priority order, so you can verify the behavior without affecting the downstream in use.
learning.concept: A version retained by a downstream and upstream search priority when it has not been fetched

category: SDLCの自動化
examDomain: SDLCの自動化
title: Reporting two required GitHub checks for the same commit
prompt: Two CodeBuild projects that use GitHub directly as their source start for the same commit. You want the results of a test and a license review to appear as separate required statuses in GitHub's protection rules, using an authorized connection. Which project settings should you use?

choices.text: Enable reportBuildStatus and use the same context in both projects, changing only targetUrl.
choices.explanation: Changing the link does not give the statuses different identifying contexts, so the two required checks cannot be distinguished.

choices.text: Use different build tags for the two projects, leave reportBuildStatus disabled, and make the tag names required checks in GitHub.
choices.explanation: AWS resource tags are not reported as commit statuses in GitHub.

choices.text: Enable reportBuildStatus in both projects and set distinct names for the test and license review in buildStatusConfig.context.
choices.explanation: The results can be reported to the source provider and distinguished by their context names.

choices.text: Disable reportBuildStatus in both projects and set only buildStatusConfig.context.
choices.explanation: Setting a name alone does not report build results to GitHub.

learning.reason: The results can be reported to the source provider and distinguished by their context names.
learning.concept: Reporting separate statuses to a source provider with CodeBuild

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Enforcing VPC creation order beyond references
prompt: A CloudFormation template creates a VPC, an internet gateway, an attachment between them, and a default route for a public subnet. The route references the gateway ID with Ref, but intermittent errors say the gateway is not yet attached to the VPC. How should you fix the template?

choices.text: Set the VPCGatewayAttachment logical ID as a dependency of the default route with DependsOn.
choices.explanation: Referencing the ID can make CloudFormation wait for the gateway to be created, but you must explicitly specify that the gateway attachment has completed.

choices.text: Pass the gateway's physical ID to GatewayId as a parameter to remove the implicit dependency between resources.
choices.explanation: Using a literal ID does not make CloudFormation wait for the connection defined in the template to be established before creating the default route.

choices.text: Add the VPC and InternetGateway as dependencies of the default route with DependsOn, and wait for both to be created.
choices.explanation: Waiting for only the VPC and gateway to be created does not wait for the attachment, which is defined as a separate resource, to complete.

choices.text: Set the default route as a dependency of VPCGatewayAttachment with DependsOn, while keeping the route reference.
choices.explanation: This makes the attachment wait for the route to complete, so it does not prevent the route from being created before the gateway is attached.

learning.reason: Referencing the ID can make CloudFormation wait for the gateway to be created, but you must explicitly specify that the gateway attachment has completed.
learning.concept: Implicit dependencies in CloudFormation and DependsOn for an attachment

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Validating a prohibited combination of environment and connectivity mode
prompt: A shared CloudFormation template accepts dev or prod for Environment and private or public for EndpointMode. Each value is valid, but the prod and public combination must be rejected with an explanation before any resources are changed. No external validation can be added. What should you use?

choices.text: Use a RuleCondition in Rules to select prod, then use Assertions to check that EndpointMode is private.
choices.explanation: This checks the relationship between the two inputs only in production and can return an explanation if the combination is invalid.

choices.text: Set AllowedValues for EndpointMode to private only, while keeping both values in AllowedValues for Environment.
choices.explanation: This also prohibits the dev and public combination, imposing a broader constraint than the single prohibited combination.

choices.text: Set an environment-specific pattern for EndpointMode's AllowedPattern and use the template's Environment parameter to choose it.
choices.explanation: AllowedPattern constrains a single input string and cannot express a choice based on another parameter.

choices.text: Use Conditions to detect prod and public, then set the Condition of the related resources to false so their creation is skipped.
choices.explanation: This controls whether resources exist; it does not reject invalid input with an explanation.

learning.reason: This checks the relationship between the two inputs only in production and can return an explanation if the combination is invalid.
learning.concept: Rules and Assertions for constraints across multiple parameters

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: The stack keeps waiting after initialization completes in a private network
prompt: In a VPC without external connectivity, initialization on an EC2 instance completes and sends a success response to the URL of an AWS::CloudFormation::WaitConditionHandle. The CloudFormation interface endpoint and IAM permissions have been verified, but the PUT to the URL times out. What should you change without creating an internet route?

choices.text: Connect EC2 to an STS interface endpoint and retrieve new temporary credentials for the instance role.
choices.explanation: The network connection to the presigned URL is failing; retrieving credentials again through STS does not change the route.

choices.text: Connect the target subnet to an S3 VPC endpoint and allow the CloudFormation response bucket in the endpoint policy.
choices.explanation: The wait condition response is sent to S3, so the instance needs to reach the target in S3 as well as have a route to the CloudFormation API.

choices.text: Add cloudformation:SignalResource to the CloudFormation endpoint policy and leave the PUT to the presigned URL unchanged.
choices.explanation: A direct PUT to the wait condition handle URL is not a CloudFormation SignalResource API call.

choices.text: Allow only HTTPS from the EC2 security group to the CloudFormation endpoint and keep using the handle URL.
choices.explanation: The response host is S3; allowing HTTPS only to the CloudFormation endpoint does not provide connectivity to it.

learning.reason: The wait condition response is sent to S3, so the instance needs to reach the target in S3 as well as have a route to the CloudFormation API.
learning.concept: The presigned S3 response destination for a wait condition and PrivateLink

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Balancing root stack deletion protection with updates
