prompt: An operations team uses an AWS CloudFormation root stack to manage shared resources and several nested stacks. They want to prevent accidental deletion while retaining the ability to intentionally remove a child stack through a reviewed template update. Which setting should they use?

choices.text: Enable termination protection on the root stack and handle stack deletion and template updates in separate operational procedures.
choices.explanation: Termination protection also applies to child stacks. It protects against deletion operations, but does not prevent a child stack from being removed in a root stack update.

choices.text: Enable termination protection separately on each child stack and disable it on the root stack.
choices.explanation: Termination protection for nested stacks is managed through the root stack, rather than enabled individually.

choices.text: Use a stack policy on the root stack to prohibit Update:Delete across the board, in place of termination protection.
choices.explanation: A stack policy constrains stack updates; it does not directly prevent deletion of the root stack.

choices.text: Set DeletionPolicy=Retain on every child stack resource in the root template to prohibit deletion of the root stack.
choices.explanation: Retain preserves the targeted resources; it does not prohibit deletion of the root stack as a whole.

learning.reason: Termination protection also applies to child stacks. It protects against deletion operations, but does not prevent a child stack from being removed in a root stack update.
learning.concept: How root termination protection differs for stack deletion and updates

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: A masked input remains visible in stack outputs
prompt: A password entered when creating a CloudFormation stack has NoEcho=true in Parameters. However, another team's automation can read an Outputs value that references the password. The consuming team must be allowed to view the stack, while the application must continue to receive the credentials only through an authorized path. How should this be fixed?

choices.text: Move the password from Outputs to Metadata and share only the output name with template users.
choices.explanation: Metadata is also outside NoEcho's protection, so this would leave the credentials in the stack metadata.

choices.text: Move the password to an Export in Outputs and use a different CloudFormation export name for each environment.
choices.explanation: Naming the export does not make its value private and adds another way to retrieve it.

choices.text: Keep Outputs and pass the same value to the template again as a separate parameter with NoEcho set to true.
choices.explanation: Adding another parameter with NoEcho does not mask plaintext recorded in an output.

choices.text: Remove the password from Outputs, pass only a reference to the secret, and have the application's execution role retrieve it from Secrets Manager.
choices.explanation: NoEcho does not mask Outputs. Removing the value from the output lets the application's permissions control access to the secret itself.

learning.reason: NoEcho does not mask Outputs. Removing the value from the output lets the application's permissions control access to the secret itself.
learning.concept: Outputs and secret references that NoEcho cannot protect

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Reference an approved template fragment in multiple stacks
prompt: The CloudFormation stacks for different environments must embed the same approved resource fragment. The fragment is stored in a dedicated S3 bucket under a different key for each release, and each template must pin the version it uses. Separate child stacks and registry registration are not needed. What should you specify?

choices.text: Set AWS::CloudFormation::Stack's TemplateURL to a release-specific value and avoid importing the fragment as a separate stack.
choices.explanation: That resource type creates a nested stack, so the fragment is not embedded as the same resource definitions in the parent template.

choices.text: Specify AWS::Include with Fn::Transform and set Location to the S3 URI for the chosen release.
choices.explanation: This embeds the S3 configuration fragment in the same template, and a release-specific key makes the input reproducible.

choices.text: Specify the S3 URI in Fn::ForEach under AWS::LanguageExtensions and expand each key in the fragment one by one.
choices.explanation: Fn::ForEach iterates over a supplied collection; it does not read S3 objects.

choices.text: Pass the release-specific S3 URI to Fn::ImportValue and expand the returned value into multiple resource definitions in the template.
choices.explanation: ImportValue references an export from another stack; it does not expand a template stored in S3.

learning.reason: This embeds the S3 configuration fragment in the same template, and a release-specific key makes the input reproducible.
learning.concept: Using the S3 location with AWS::Include and embedding a fragment pinned to a version

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Import individually managed stacks into a StackSet
prompt: CloudFormation stacks were created individually in multiple accounts from the same template. You want to retain the existing stack IDs and resources while controlling future updates from one place. You have the list of stack IDs to manage and the required IAM configuration for the accounts. What should you do?

choices.text: Add Outputs to the existing stacks in each account, then deploy a new StackSet that uses those exports.
choices.explanation: Referencing exports does not provide bulk updates to the existing stacks or import their stack IDs.

choices.text: Run CreateStackInstances in the target accounts and specify the same names as the existing stacks to associate them.
choices.explanation: Creating new stack instances alone does not bring each account's existing stack ID under management.

choices.text: Create a StackSet with a template that matches the existing stacks, then pass the stack IDs to import to ImportStacksToStackSet.
choices.explanation: This operation adds existing stacks to StackSet management, so there is no need to recreate resources with the same template.

choices.text: Use CloudFormation resource import to move the resources from each stack into a single stack in the management account.
choices.explanation: This would not preserve the existing stacks across accounts and is not the operation for importing stacks into a StackSet.

learning.reason: This operation adds existing stacks to StackSet management, so there is no need to recreate resources with the same template.
learning.concept: The difference between resource import and importing existing stacks into a StackSet

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Review permission broadening separately from ordinary configuration changes
prompt: The AWS CDK CI pipeline saves the usual resource diff. Security reviewers also need a report, for the same deployment target stack, comparing the existing state with the candidate and limited to changes that broaden permissions such as IAM permissions. Do not make changes to the stack. Which command should be added?

choices.text: Use cdk deploy --require-approval broadening and generate a report without granting approval.
choices.explanation: This command can proceed with a deployment when there are no changes requiring approval, so it does not meet the CI requirement for a report only.

choices.text: Extract only resources whose names contain AWS::IAM from the output of cdk synth.
choices.explanation: The candidate template alone does not compare permissions with existing permissions or determine whether they have broadened.

choices.text: Run cdk diff --security-only for the target stack.
choices.explanation: This compares the candidate with the existing environment without deploying and isolates changes that broaden security permissions.

choices.text: Run cdk diff --strict for the target stack and decide from that output alone whether a public security group exists.
choices.explanation: Strict changes how filtered diffs are handled; it does not limit the output to permission-broadening changes.

learning.reason: This compares the candidate with the existing environment without deploying and isolates changes that broaden security permissions.
learning.concept: Permission broadening in CDK diffs

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Run only the approved runbook on a schedule
prompt: A scheduled maintenance pipeline starts a shared Systems Manager Automation runbook with StartAutomationExecution. The owning team creates revised versions of the same document and also changes the default version. The caller must use only revision 7, which has been reviewed until additional approval is granted. How should the start request be configured?

choices.text: Set DocumentVersion to $LATEST and record the reviewed revision number in the execution output.
choices.explanation: Selecting the latest version is not pinned by recording the number in the output.

choices.text: Specify the shared document in DocumentName and pin DocumentVersion to the numeric version 7.
choices.explanation: Even if the default or latest version changes, each call continues to select the approved revision.

choices.text: Omit DocumentVersion and add revision=7 as a session tag on AutomationExecutionRole.
choices.explanation: A role session tag does not select a runbook version.

choices.text: Set DocumentVersion to $DEFAULT and check in the execution history that the document version was 7.
choices.explanation: If the default version changes, a later call will start a different version; checking afterward cannot prevent that execution.

learning.reason: Even if the default or latest version changes, each call continues to select the approved revision.
learning.concept: The document revision specified when starting an Automation execution

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Record security group changes even when they are reverted
prompt: A customer-managed AWS Config recorder records security groups daily. A rule is changed for only 15 minutes during maintenance and then reverted. The audit must be able to retrieve the configuration history for both states, while keeping daily recording for other resource types wherever possible. What should be changed?

choices.text: Configure a periodic AWS Config rule for security groups and keep the configuration recorder's daily frequency.
choices.explanation: A rule's evaluation frequency is separate from the frequency at which the recorder captures configuration items.

choices.text: Add security groups to the recording frequency override and specify continuous recording, leaving other resource types at the default daily frequency.
choices.explanation: For the selected type, detected configuration changes are recorded so that a short-lived configuration is not lost in daily aggregation.

choices.text: Increase the frequency at which the AWS Config delivery channel delivers data and keep the configuration recorder's daily frequency.
choices.explanation: Changing the delivery interval does not add an intermediate state that the daily recorder did not capture.

choices.text: Add more data sources to the AWS Config aggregator and aggregate the security groups from each Region while keeping daily recording.
choices.explanation: An aggregator collects recorded data; it does not change the recorder's recording interval.

learning.reason: For the selected type, detected configuration changes are recorded so that a short-lived configuration is not lost in daily aggregation.
learning.concept: Continuous recording and daily recording, which aggregates changes over a 24-hour period

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Roll back a configuration version without overwriting a parameter
prompt: At startup, a service reads a configuration release version from Systems Manager Parameter Store. After promoting version 18 to production, an operator wants to return to the tested version 17 without copying its value. Promotion and rollback must switch only the reference, without redeploying the application. What should be used?

choices.text: Have the application always retrieve the latest version without a label, and add the label prod to version 17 during rollback.
choices.explanation: A retrieval without a label does not follow the label's target; it continues to read the latest version.

choices.text: Have the application retrieve the parameter by its label, and move that same label to version 17 during rollback.
choices.explanation: A label can be moved as a pointer to an existing version, so there is no need to copy the value.

choices.text: If version 18 has a problem, delete and recreate the parameter with the same name, then enter the value from version 17.
choices.explanation: This replaces the parameter's history instead of pointing to an existing version, and requires entering the value again.

choices.text: Have the application retrieve the parameter with version 18 in its name, then overwrite version 18 with the same value as version 17.
choices.explanation: Updating a parameter creates a new version in its history; it does not rewrite an existing version 18.

learning.reason: A label can be moved as a pointer to an existing version, so there is no need to copy the value.
learning.concept: Using a Parameter Store label to reference a specific existing version

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Control configuration generation order during host initialization
prompt: With CloudFormation AWS::CloudFormation::Init, an installer must run first, and then configuration files must be written to a directory created by the installer's output. Within the same config, files are processed before commands, causing an error. How can this be fixed while preserving the configuration declarations and existing scripts?

choices.text: Split the work into separate configs and have cfn-init select a configSet that lists the installation config first.
choices.explanation: A configSet runs multiple configurations in the specified order, avoiding reliance on the fixed processing order within a single configuration.

choices.text: Add a CreationPolicy to the same EC2 resource and wait for cfn-signal to report success.
choices.explanation: A resource creation policy can wait for completion, but it does not change the order of files and commands within cfn-init.

choices.text: Set waitAfterCompletion on every command so the installation completes before files are reached.
choices.explanation: Waiting after command execution does not change the fact that files run first within that config.

choices.text: Write the commands before files in YAML within the same config and number the command names.
choices.explanation: The processing order of sections within a config cannot be changed by YAML order or command names alone.

learning.reason: A configSet runs multiple configurations in the specified order, avoiding reliance on the fixed processing order within a single configuration.
learning.concept: cfn-init configuration blocks and the ordering of configSets

category: 構成管理とIaC
examDomain: 構成管理とIaC
title: Source-controlled settings are not taking effect in production
prompt: An operator previously set a specific environment option directly in the Elastic Beanstalk console. The same setting is now declared in .ebextensions, but the environment retains the old value even after a new application version is deployed. How can the team ensure that this setting is updated only through source control going forward?

choices.text: Remove the directly applied option value and deploy an application version that includes the specified .ebextensions file.
choices.explanation: A setting applied individually to the environment has higher precedence. Removing the direct value allows the lower-precedence declaration to take effect.

choices.text: Save the current environment configuration as a saved configuration, then reapply that same configuration before deploying.
choices.explanation: Reapplying the previous setting does not switch management to the source-controlled configuration.

choices.text: Move the setting to the file that sorts last alphabetically in .ebextensions and redeploy to the same environment.
choices.explanation: The processing order of source-side configuration files does not give them higher precedence than a directly applied value.

choices.text: Keep the directly applied value and change the application deployment policy to Immutable so that the instances are replaced.
choices.explanation: Replacing the instances does not change the precedence of the environment option settings.

learning.reason: A setting applied individually to the environment has higher precedence. Removing the direct value allows the lower-precedence declaration to take effect.
learning.concept: Precedence of values applied directly to an environment and values in .ebextensions

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Prepare DynamoDB for a forecasted traffic surge
prompt: An on-demand DynamoDB table will immediately receive read traffic far above its current warm throughput when an event starts. Traffic is distributed appropriately, and the account has sufficient quota. How can you increase the read capacity that is ready to respond in advance, without sending production traffic as a rehearsal?

choices.text: Raise the table's maximum on-demand read throughput to the forecast peak and leave its warm throughput unchanged.
choices.explanation: The maximum acts as a traffic ceiling; setting it does not prepare the table to handle the specified throughput immediately.

choices.text: Switch the table to provisioned mode with a low capacity setting, then switch it back to on-demand just before the event starts.
choices.explanation: Passing through a low setting does not guarantee that the table can handle the forecast peak in advance.

choices.text: Create a DynamoDB throttling alarm and raise the dashboard threshold to match the load immediately after it starts.
choices.explanation: This changes the monitored threshold but does not increase the table's ability to handle the surge.

choices.text: Before the event, raise the table's read warm throughput to the forecast peak and confirm that the change has taken effect.
choices.explanation: You can warm the table in advance to a specified read rate instead of waiting for it to reach a past peak naturally.

learning.reason: You can warm the table in advance to a specified read rate instead of waiting for it to reach a past peak naturally.
learning.concept: Read throughput ready to respond after warming an on-demand table in advance

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Stop only new connections before regional maintenance
prompt: Global Accelerator has endpoint groups in two healthy Regions. Before planned maintenance in one Region, you need to stop sending new connections there while keeping existing long-lived TCP connections open until clients close them. What should you change before maintenance begins?

choices.text: Stop the listeners on all load balancers in the maintenance Region and leave the group healthy.
choices.explanation: This can also terminate connections that are still active in the maintenance Region, so clients cannot simply close them when they are done.

choices.text: Set the traffic dial for the maintenance Region to 0%, and keep its endpoints in place until the connections have ended.
choices.explanation: When another Region is healthy, new connections are sent there. Changing the dial does not end existing connections.

choices.text: Disable Global Accelerator and switch DNS to the load balancer in the healthy Region.
choices.explanation: This stops the entire accelerator, so existing connections cannot be maintained, including those associated with the other group.

choices.text: Set the traffic dial for the healthy Region to 100% and leave the maintenance Region at its default of 100%.
choices.explanation: A 100% dial for the healthy Region is the share of traffic directed to that group; it does not prevent new connections to the maintenance Region.

learning.reason: When another Region is healthy, new connections are sent there. Changing the dial does not end existing connections.
learning.concept: Traffic dials affect new connections

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Keep a DNS failover control path available during a widespread outage
prompt: You use ARC routing controls for DNS failover. During a production outage, even if one Region's API endpoint is unreachable, operators must be able to change the state of the same routing control through a reachable Region. Which procedure should you prepare in advance?

choices.text: Record only the nearest cluster endpoint in advance, and retry DNS resolution for that hostname if the request fails.
choices.explanation: Retries remain concentrated on that Region's endpoint, so recovery through another Region is not possible.

choices.text: Create a new cluster through the management API during the failover and use its endpoint to update the original cluster's state.
choices.explanation: The new cluster does not hold the original routing control's state, and this approach depends on a control-plane operation during the outage.

choices.text: When a Regional outage is detected, stop updates to ARC and extend the TTL of the same Route 53 health check.
choices.explanation: Extending the TTL does not change the routing control's state.

choices.text: Record all cluster data plane endpoints and try another endpoint if one does not respond.
choices.explanation: Using multiple Regional data planes for the same cluster avoids pinning the control path to a single Region.

learning.reason: Using multiple Regional data planes for the same cluster avoids pinning the control path to a single Region.
learning.concept: Multiple data plane endpoints for ARC routing controls

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Gradually warming up newly registered healthy targets
prompt: An Application Load Balancer (ALB) target group uses round robin and already has healthy targets. A newly registered target becomes slow because its startup cache is cold if it receives its normal share of traffic immediately after passing health checks. Without changing the application, how can you increase the target's traffic share over a set period after registration?

choices.text: Increase the deregistration delay for targets to suppress initial requests to the new target.
choices.explanation: Deregistration delay lets in-flight requests finish on a target that is being removed.

choices.text: Increase the ECS health check grace period so ECS takes longer to decide that a new task has failed.
choices.explanation: This changes how long ECS waits before marking a task unhealthy, but it does not change the traffic share sent by an ALB after it considers the target healthy.

choices.text: Enable ALB sticky sessions and set the cookie expiration to match the warm-up period.
choices.explanation: Sticky sessions keep existing sessions on a particular target; they do not increase a new target's traffic share over time.

choices.text: Configure slow start for the target group and specify the required warm-up period.
choices.explanation: Traffic is increased gradually after the new target becomes healthy.

learning.reason: Traffic is increased gradually after the new target becomes healthy.
learning.concept: Slow start on an ALB with existing healthy targets

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Redundant brokers do not automatically reconnect JMS clients
prompt: Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ is configured in active/standby mode. Production JMS clients are configured with only the single OpenWire URL for the current active broker, and a maintenance failover caused it to stop. Which configuration lets the clients automatically reconnect to another endpoint while retaining the protocol and broker?

choices.text: Put both OpenWire URLs in the client's failover URI.
choices.explanation: If the client loses its current connection, it can retry connections to known endpoints, including the other one.

choices.text: Have the client retry the fixed URL for the active broker whenever maintenance occurs, and increase the retry count.
choices.explanation: Even with repeated retries, the client cannot try the other URL that is reachable after the roles switch.

choices.text: Store both URLs, but specify only the usual active-side URL as the client's JMS connection endpoint.
choices.explanation: Even if an unused URL is in a configuration file, the client that creates the connection uses only the single endpoint it was given.

choices.text: Connect to a single URL normally and redeploy the standby-side configuration each time maintenance failover occurs.
choices.explanation: This waits for an operational change, so the client does not automatically track the broker's role change as required.

learning.reason: If the client loses its current connection, it can retry connections to known endpoints, including the other one.
learning.concept: Using both ActiveMQ endpoints with the client's failover transport

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Replicate data created before replication was configured
prompt: You added a replication rule between versioning-enabled S3 buckets. New objects are replicated, but objects that existed before the rule was configured and their earlier versions are missing from the recovery destination. How can you backfill the existing data as replicas while preserving the original keys and versions?

choices.text: Run S3 Batch Replication with a manifest that includes the target keys and versions.
choices.explanation: The objects and versions that existed before the rule was configured can be replicated by the target rule without rewriting them in the source bucket.

choices.text: Disable the rule on the existing bucket, then enable it again to make it scan all stored versions.
choices.explanation: Enabling the rule does not retroactively replicate objects or earlier versions that existed before it was configured.

choices.text: Overwrite the existing objects in the source bucket using the same keys so live replication transfers everything.
choices.explanation: Overwriting creates new versions and does not meet the requirement to backfill the existing versions without changing them.

choices.text: Synchronize the buckets with AWS CLI s3 sync, then add replication metadata afterward.
choices.explanation: A regular copy handles current objects but does not reproduce version replication as replicas.

learning.reason: The objects and versions that existed before the rule was configured can be replicated by the target rule without rewriting them in the source bucket.
learning.concept: Live replication and Batch Replication of existing objects

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Use an archived disk snapshot in a recovery exercise
prompt: EBS snapshots kept for long-term compliance retention are in the archive tier. In an exercise next week, you will create a volume from one of these snapshots once, then return it to archive storage without further action. What should you do in advance?

choices.text: Enable Fast Snapshot Restore for the target Availability Zone while the snapshot is archived, then create the volume as soon as restoration starts.
choices.explanation: This acceleration setting does not eliminate the requirement to restore the snapshot to the standard tier first.

choices.text: Keep the snapshot in the archive tier, copy it to another Availability Zone, and create a volume from that copy.
choices.explanation: An archived snapshot cannot be used to create a volume or copy it until it has been restored.

choices.text: Temporarily restore it to the standard tier for the exercise's usage period, then create the volume after the restore completes.
choices.explanation: You can use the snapshot in the standard tier during that period; afterward, it returns to its original archive state.

choices.text: Restore it permanently to the standard tier and use a volume tag to specify the exercise period.
choices.explanation: A permanent restore switches the tier, and a volume tag does not automatically return the snapshot to archive storage.

learning.reason: You can use the snapshot in the standard tier during that period; afterward, it returns to its original archive state.
learning.concept: Temporary restoration of an archived EBS snapshot

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: RDS switchover is blocked by prechecks
prompt: An RDS Blue/Green deployment has prepared a new engine version for production. Switchover prechecks report a long-running write on the blue environment and replication lag. You want the managed switchover to succeed with synchronized data and a short outage. What should you do?

choices.text: Reschedule for a low-write period, let long-running transactions complete, and rerun the switchover after green has caught up.
choices.explanation: This can shorten the blue write barrier and synchronization time, making it easier to satisfy the guardrails.

choices.text: Restart the blue database and change the DNS target to green without checking replication status.
choices.explanation: A restart alone does not confirm that green has caught up, and changing DNS does not replace the managed switchover guardrails.

choices.text: Extend only the switchover timeout while replication is stopped, and proceed assuming green has the latest data.
choices.explanation: A longer timeout does not make green catch up if replication is stopped.

choices.text: Give the green endpoint to the application and begin writes immediately without running the RDS switchover.
choices.explanation: Switching before blue and green have caught up does not complete the managed switchover you need.

learning.reason: This can shorten the blue write barrier and synchronization time, making it easier to satisfy the guardrails.
learning.concept: RDS Blue/Green switchover guardrails and replication catch-up

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Keep a recovery node available for a Pod with a persistent volume
prompt: An EKS StatefulSet Pod has failed, and its PV referencing an existing EBS volume in us-east-1a is healthy. The current node group can scale only in us-east-1b and us-east-1c, and the Pod remains Pending with a volume node affinity conflict. How can you recover without migrating the data?

choices.text: Change the StorageClass to WaitForFirstConsumer so the existing PV's volume moves to the AZ of its next consumer.
choices.explanation: WaitForFirstConsumer controls when new volumes are provisioned; it does not move existing volumes.

choices.text: Add nodes in us-east-1b so the StatefulSet Pod is preferentially rescheduled onto one of them.
choices.explanation: An existing EBS volume cannot be attached directly to a node in another AZ.

choices.text: Remove the AZ condition from the PV's nodeAffinity so the scheduler can choose a Pod placement in us-east-1b or us-east-1c.
choices.explanation: Removing the scheduler constraint does not change the volume's AZ restriction.

choices.text: Provide node group capacity that can launch nodes in us-east-1a so the Pod can be placed in the AZ of its existing PV.
choices.explanation: An EBS volume attaches to EC2 in the same AZ, so the Pod can be scheduled while using its existing data.

learning.reason: An EBS volume attaches to EC2 in the same AZ, so the Pod can be scheduled while using its existing data.
learning.concept: The relationship between an EBS volume's AZ and the nodes where a Pod can be placed

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Retain the ability to restore to a selected point before retirement
prompt: An RDS DB instance is being retired. The audit team will later select one of the existing recoverable points from several days ago through just before deletion. Restoration is planned within the backup retention period in effect before the switchover. What should you specify before deleting the instance?

choices.text: Enable deletion protection, then delete the instance and take backups for the period during which protection was enabled.
choices.explanation: Deletion protection prevents a deletion operation; it is separate from specifying that recovery points be retained after the DB is retired.

choices.text: Create only a final manual snapshot at deletion and delete the automated backups.
choices.explanation: A final snapshot can restore the DB to the time it was taken, but it does not by itself let you select an arbitrary earlier point.

choices.text: Promote a read replica on the retirement date and record it as a recovery point from several days earlier.
choices.explanation: Promotion can preserve data as of the promotion time, but it does not provide the transaction log history needed to select an earlier point.

choices.text: Specify that automated backups be retained at deletion, then restore to the selected point within the remaining retention period.
choices.explanation: Retained automated backups include snapshots and transaction logs for the covered period, allowing a point to be selected within the recoverable range.

learning.reason: Retained automated backups include snapshots and transaction logs for the covered period, allowing a point to be selected within the recoverable range.
learning.concept: Point-in-time restore from RDS automated backups retained after deletion

category: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
examDomain: レジリエントなクラウドソリューション
title: Raise the standby Region's launch quota in advance
prompt: A disaster recovery Region runs the service at a small scale continuously. During a production outage, Auto Scaling must add compatible instances equivalent to 450 vCPU. The applicable On-Demand vCPU quota in the standby Region is currently 200, and the limit has produced errors in a test environment. What should you do to implement the recovery plan?

choices.text: Increase the Auto Scaling MaxSize and distribute launch requests across multiple AZs.
choices.explanation: Adding AZs within the same Region does not increase the account's governing regional quota.

choices.text: Raise the applicable quota in the production Region above 450 and transfer its 400 unused vCPU to the standby Region during an outage.
choices.explanation: The relevant EC2 limit applies per Region; unused capacity in the production Region cannot be transferred.

choices.text: Increase the group's desired capacity to the equivalent of 450 vCPU and rely on repeated recovery attempts to launch beyond the quota.
choices.explanation: Retrying launch attempts does not increase the required quota.

choices.text: Increase the applicable vCPU quota in the standby Region and test the recovery capacity there in advance, including the continuously running baseline.
choices.explanation: Limits from other Regions do not carry over, so you need sufficient quota for the relevant instance category in the recovery Region.

learning.reason: Limits from other Regions do not carry over, so you need sufficient quota for the relevant instance category in the recovery Region.
learning.concept: Region-specific Amazon EC2 On-Demand vCPU quotas

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: No access logs from an NLB that passes TLS through
prompt: You enabled legacy NLB access logs to S3, but they do not record the TLS version negotiated by HTTPS traffic forwarded through a TCP listener. Keep TLS termination on the server side. How can you record the result of the actual connection negotiation?

choices.text: Add the protocol field to VPC Flow Logs and read the TLS version from TCP flows.
choices.explanation: The protocol in flow logs identifies a value at the IP layer; it does not record the TLS version.

choices.text: Keep the current TCP listener and log the protocol and cipher suite on the backend that terminates TLS.
choices.explanation: The component that actually negotiates TLS can capture the connection details without moving the termination point.

choices.text: Change the NLB listener to TLS, configure the targets to use TLS as well, and enable legacy access logs.
choices.explanation: TLS from the client would terminate at the NLB, while TLS to the backend would be a separate connection, changing the end-to-end termination arrangement.

choices.text: Keep the NLB TCP listener and broaden the log bucket permissions so TLS details are added to existing log files.
choices.explanation: Granting more write permissions does not make a TCP listener generate legacy NLB TLS access logs.

learning.reason: The component that actually negotiates TLS can capture the connection details without moving the termination point.
learning.concept: Legacy NLB access logs cover traffic handled by TLS listeners.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Observe a specific path in seconds
prompt: You are investigating latency in some regions on a payment path behind CloudFront. You need to stream the required fields from edge requests for processing at intervals of a few seconds, and collect only 10% of the target cache behavior to control measurement costs. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Create a real-time logging configuration that sends the required fields to Kinesis at 10%, then associate it with the target behavior.
choices.explanation: Data reaches the stream at intervals of a few seconds, and you can specify the target behavior and collection rate.

choices.text: Send standard logs for the entire distribution to S3, then process 10% of the payment-path requests from object notifications.
choices.explanation: Reducing the processing scope afterward does not meet the requirement to obtain edge logs at intervals of a few seconds.

choices.text: Enable additional CloudFront CloudWatch metrics and save request-level details by country with 10% sampling.
choices.explanation: Aggregated metrics do not provide a stream of individual requests with the specified fields.

choices.text: Send origin access logs to Kinesis and inspect 10% of requests that reach the origin, including edge cache responses.
choices.explanation: Requests served from cache do not reach the origin, so this cannot measure all relevant edge requests.

learning.reason: Data reaches the stream at intervals of a few seconds, and you can specify the target behavior and collection rate.
learning.concept: Associating CloudFront real-time logs with a behavior and sampling requests.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Measure queue age and dropped events separately for asynchronous invocations
prompt: Asynchronous submissions to Lambda have increased. The caller receives only an acknowledgment of acceptance. Operations needs to visualize how long events remain queued before Lambda processes them and separately count events that were discarded without success after retries. Which metrics should you combine? Choose two.

choices.text: Use AsyncEventsDropped to count events discarded without successful processing.
choices.explanation: It counts events that are ultimately discarded, such as after reaching the maximum event age or retry limit.

choices.text: Use DestinationDeliveryFailures to count events discarded without successful processing.
choices.explanation: This metric counts failures to deliver a result to a destination; it is not the count of events discarded by Lambda itself.

choices.text: Use the function's Duration to measure queue wait time.
choices.explanation: Duration measures processing time inside the function, not how long an asynchronous event waits before invocation.

choices.text: Use ConcurrentExecutions to count the number of events still in the queue after failures.
choices.explanation: This metric measures concurrent invocations in progress; it does not directly show the number of queued events.

choices.text: Use AsyncEventAge to see the distribution of event queue wait times.
choices.explanation: It measures the time from when Lambda queues an event until the function is invoked.

learning.reason: AsyncEventsDropped counts events ultimately discarded after limits such as maximum event age or retries. AsyncEventAge measures how long Lambda waits between queuing an event and invoking the function.
learning.concept: Queue wait time and discarded-event counts for asynchronous events.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Keep log delivery interruptions from affecting request processing
prompt: ECS containers use the awslogs log driver in blocking mode. When log delivery pauses, writes to standard output stop and the application stops responding. Prioritize service availability during delivery interruptions, buffer logs within available memory, and allow some log loss during prolonged interruptions. How should you configure logging?

choices.text: Switch to non-blocking mode and keep the task's memory settings unchanged on the assumption that no logs will ever be lost.
choices.explanation: The buffer is finite, and logs can be dropped if it fills while delivery is interrupted. Protection cannot be guaranteed without accounting for capacity.

choices.text: Set the log driver to non-blocking and configure max-buffer-size based on the log rate during interruptions and the task's available memory.
choices.explanation: A memory buffer decouples the application from log delivery; if the buffer fills, processing continues at the cost of lost logs.

choices.text: Keep blocking mode and increase the number of ECS service restarts so tasks restart and restore log delivery.
choices.explanation: New tasks can also stall until the destination recovers, so application progress remains coupled to log delivery.

choices.text: Keep blocking mode and extend the CloudWatch Logs retention period to store logs during delivery delays.
choices.explanation: Retention applies after logs are delivered and does not change the wait on standard-output writes.

learning.reason: A memory buffer decouples the application from log delivery; if the buffer fills, processing continues at the cost of lost logs.
learning.concept: awslogs non-blocking mode and max-buffer-size.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Retrieve PostgreSQL logs from before log export began
prompt: After an incident involving RDS for PostgreSQL, you enabled CloudWatch Logs export. New logs are being centralized, but the logs from the time of the incident remain only as files on the DB instance that can be retrieved. How can you save the relevant historical logs now?

choices.text: Extend the retention period in CloudWatch Logs and wait for RDS to send the incident-time logs automatically.
choices.explanation: Changing the retention period does not ingest historical files from the DB instance.

choices.text: Disable and re-enable RDS log export to resend all retained files.
choices.explanation: Export covers logs from the time it is enabled; toggling it does not resend earlier files.

choices.text: Download the file for the incident time from the RDS database logs and place it in a location for investigation.
choices.explanation: Files generated before export began are not sent automatically, so retrieve the files that remain on the DB instance.

choices.text: Expand the time range in CloudWatch Logs Insights and search the centralized logs for files still on RDS.
choices.explanation: Insights searches events in the selected CloudWatch log groups; it cannot search files on the DB instance that have not been exported.

learning.reason: Files generated before export began are not sent automatically, so retrieve the files that remain on the DB instance.
learning.concept: When RDS PostgreSQL log export begins.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Correlate calls using an identifier received from the caller
prompt: When handling an inquiry about a public REST API, you receive an identifier from the caller that appears in the response and use it to match a single request in API Gateway access logs. The identifier must be generated by API Gateway and cannot be specified by the caller. Which log field and response header should you use?

choices.text: Include $context.requestId in the access logs and match it with x-amzn-RequestId in the response.
choices.explanation: The caller can override requestId with a valid UUID, so it does not meet the requirement for a caller-unspecified identifier.

choices.text: Include integration processing time in the logs and match requests using only the response time in milliseconds.
choices.explanation: Multiple calls can have the same value, so it is not an identifier for matching a specific request.

choices.text: Match $context.extendedRequestId with x-amz-apigw-id.
choices.explanation: The API Gateway generated identifier that the caller cannot override can be used in both places.

choices.text: Include the source IP address in the access logs and combine it with a correlation ID sent by the client.
choices.explanation: This still relies on a value assigned by the caller, and an IP address does not uniquely identify individual API calls behind NAT, for example.

learning.reason: The API Gateway generated identifier that the caller cannot override can be used in both places.
learning.concept: The REST API extendedRequestId and response header.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Logs used for forwarding create a forwarding loop
prompt: An account-level CloudWatch Logs subscription uses Lambda to transform logs and deliver them externally. Immediately after it was applied to all target log groups, the CloudWatch logs emitted by the transformation Lambda became its next input, and processing volume surged. What should you change while keeping collection for the application groups in place?

choices.text: Change the group selection criteria in the account-level policy to exclude the log groups used by the delivery path, including the transformation Lambda.
choices.explanation: This prevents delivery-processing logs from feeding back into the same forwarding flow while keeping the application groups in scope.

choices.text: Clear the policy's log content filter so that application logs and Lambda diagnostic logs are not missed.
choices.explanation: Allowing all content does not stop logs from the delivery path from being fed back as input.

choices.text: Keep the target groups and set the shortest retention period for the Lambda's CloudWatch logs.
choices.explanation: Retention controls deletion of past logs. It does not change the condition that new log lines feed back as input.

choices.text: Only lower the Lambda's reserved concurrency and leave the forwarding policy's targets unchanged.
choices.explanation: The recursive path remains, so lowering processing pressure does not stop subsequent log generation and redelivery.

learning.reason: This prevents delivery-processing logs from feeding back into the same forwarding flow while keeping the application groups in scope.
learning.concept: Exclude the delivery path itself from account-level forwarding.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Network Firewall flow logs are missing some traffic
prompt: In an authorized internal test, AWS Network Firewall FLOW logs include traffic that passed through state tracking, but not traffic that passed a stateless rule with PASS. You need to audit the target flows in CloudWatch Logs while keeping the original scope of allowed traffic. What should you change?

choices.text: Keep stateless PASS and extend the retention period for existing logs before running the next test.
choices.explanation: Retention applies to logs already emitted and does not change the processing path that emits flow logs.

choices.text: Send the target traffic to the stateful engine and apply the same allow conditions there.
choices.explanation: FLOW logs cover flows processed by the stateful engine, so change the processing path while preserving the allowed scope.

choices.text: Keep stateless PASS and change the log destination from CloudWatch Logs to S3.
choices.explanation: Changing the destination does not generate FLOW records for traffic that does not pass through stateful processing.

choices.text: Keep stateless PASS and change the log type from FLOW to ALERT.
choices.explanation: Changing the log type does not provide audit records for flows whose processing ends at the stateless stage.

learning.reason: FLOW logs cover flows processed by the stateful engine, so change the processing path while preserving the allowed scope.
learning.concept: The source of FLOW logs and forwarding traffic to stateful processing.

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Investigate Real-Browser Latency That Synthetic Tests Miss
prompt: Synthetic monitoring shows that the purchase flow in an online store web app succeeds, but users of a particular mobile browser report slow performance. You want to collect actual page loads and JavaScript errors from a sample of user sessions without asking users to reproduce the issue. What should you implement?

choices.text: Break down Application Load Balancer target response times by browser and estimate the frequency of JavaScript errors.
choices.explanation: Target response time does not measure browser rendering or JavaScript errors themselves.

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch RUM app monitor, integrate the client into the site, and configure the percentage of sessions to monitor.
choices.explanation: It collects performance and error data from browsers that actually use the site, at the sampling rate you specify.

choices.text: Increase X-Ray sampling on the server to match actual request traffic and capture page loads without adding browser instrumentation.
choices.explanation: Increasing server-side traces cannot observe client-side activity when the client does not send telemetry.

choices.text: Set a mobile viewport size for a CloudWatch Synthetics canary and save a sample of its runs.
choices.explanation: A device-like test is possible, but it does not directly collect page loads from actual visitors' browsers.

learning.reason: It collects performance and error data from browsers that actually use the site, at the sampling rate you specify.
learning.concept: CloudWatch RUM browser telemetry and session sampling

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Measure First-Byte Latency Only for a Specific S3 Prefix
prompt: A single S3 bucket contains high-priority reports/ objects alongside a large volume of routine traffic. You need to aggregate, at one-minute granularity, how long requests for reports/ take to begin receiving a response from S3, without incurring extra costs or noise from other keys. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Enable request metrics for the entire bucket and select only reports/ using a TotalRequestLatency dimension.
choices.explanation: There is no prefix filter setting here, so no time series for that filter is generated. TotalRequestLatency is a different metric that includes the full transfer. The required identifier is TotalRequestLatency.

choices.text: Collect CloudTrail S3 data events for reports/ and aggregate event timestamps as the time to the first response byte.
choices.explanation: Recorded event timestamps are not durations and do not provide a first-byte measurement.

choices.text: Use FirstByteLatency from request metrics filtered to reports/.
choices.explanation: This measures, for requests to the target keys, the time from receipt of a request until S3 begins sending the response.

choices.text: Add a reports/ tag to S3 storage metrics and monitor changes in BucketSizeBytes at one-minute intervals.
choices.explanation: Storage size does not represent a time series for the time until a response begins.

learning.reason: This measures, for requests to the target keys, the time from receipt of a request until S3 begins sending the response.
learning.concept: S3 request metric configuration and FirstByteLatency

category: モニタリングとログ記録
examDomain: モニタリングとログ記録
title: Identify Which EBS Limit Was Reached
prompt: During an investigation on a Nitro-based EC2 instance, the volume's VolumeThroughputExceededCheck was 1 for a one-minute period, while VolumeIOPSExceededCheck was 0 and the corresponding instance-side EBS limit-exceeded metric was also 0. Assuming the block device is healthy, which setting should you prioritize for review?

choices.text: Replace the Nitro instance with a type that has higher EBS bandwidth and keep the same volume settings.
choices.explanation: The instance-side bandwidth was not exceeded; the volume itself remains a possible limit.

choices.text: Increase only the IOPS provisioned for the EBS volume.
choices.explanation: The observation does not indicate an IOPS limit was exceeded, and this does not address the throughput limit.

choices.text: Review the throughput provisioned for the EBS volume.
choices.explanation: The only metric indicating an attempted limit exceedance is for volume throughput; neither volume IOPS nor the instance-side limit was exceeded during the same period.

choices.text: Increase the volume capacity and extend the file system in the operating system, while keeping the throughput setting unchanged.
choices.explanation: The metrics do not indicate a capacity limit, and keeping the setting unchanged does not directly address the measured throughput constraint.

learning.reason: The only metric indicating an attempted limit exceedance is for volume throughput; neither volume IOPS nor the instance-side limit was exceeded during the same period.
learning.concept: Distinguishing EBS volume limits from EC2 bandwidth and IOPS limits

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Create One Ticket per AWS Health Communication During a Regional Outage
prompt: For a single account, create incident tickets from AWS Health notifications that fit on one page. Receive events in both the usual Region and the AWS-designated backup Region so that you still receive communications if one is unavailable. Retain separate progress communications for the same Health event, while preventing duplicate tickets for the same communication. Which two actions should you take?

choices.text: Use the outer EventBridge id as the deduplication key shared across both Regions.
choices.explanation: The field AWS Health recommends for identifying the same communication across both paths is detail.communicationId.

choices.text: Persist only the Health event's eventArn and discard every notification with an ARN already seen.
choices.explanation: This could also discard separate progress communications belonging to the same event.

choices.text: Create EventBridge rules in both the target Region and the backup Region, and forward them to the same ticket-processing system.
choices.explanation: If the usual event path is unavailable, the backup path can ingest the same type of communication.

choices.text: Use detail.communicationId as the deduplication key in ticket processing and allow each communication to be processed only once.
choices.explanation: This suppresses duplicates when the same communication arrives on both paths while distinguishing separate communications for the same event.

choices.text: Create a rule only in the target Region and increase the number of retries for the destination.
choices.explanation: Retries to a target cannot replace the event path itself if its Region is unavailable.

learning.reason: If the usual event path is unavailable, the backup path can ingest the same type of communication. Using detail.communicationId suppresses duplicates when the same communication arrives on both paths while distinguishing separate communications for the same event.
learning.concept: AWS Health backup Regions and detail.communicationId

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Restrict only the recovery runbook’s data changes to outside business hours
prompt: The same Systems Manager Automation runbook can be started by both events and an operator. Diagnostics are always allowed, but the step that updates a database row may run only when an approved Change Calendar is OPEN. What should you implement, regardless of when the alarm starts the runbook?

choices.text: Set an outside-business-hours schedule on the event source rule, and use the original procedure for manual starts.
choices.explanation: Scheduling only the event source does not enforce the restriction for manual runs or when the time changes during a run.

choices.text: Associate only the suppression of result notifications with the Change Calendar, and run diagnostics and updates at any time.
choices.explanation: Suppressing notifications does not change the conditions for performing the database update.

choices.text: Add a decision step immediately before the update that calls GetCalendarState, and proceed to the update step only if the result is OPEN.
choices.explanation: Regardless of how the run starts, each execution can check the calendar state at the time it is about to perform the update.

choices.text: Set the runbook’s maximum execution time to the end of business hours, and always run the update step.
choices.explanation: The maximum execution time does not check whether the calendar is OPEN or control whether the update starts.

learning.reason: Regardless of how the run starts, each execution can check the calendar state at the time it is about to perform the update.
learning.concept: Check the current Change Calendar state within the runbook

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: ECS Exec cannot be added to existing ECS tasks that are already running
prompt: You enabled ECS Exec on a Fargate ECS service after checking the task role and network requirements for ECS Exec to investigate an incident. The tasks that were already running do not have ExecuteCommandAgent. What should you do to use ECS Exec on the next task started for the investigation?

choices.text: Start a new deployment on the service with ECS Exec enabled, then connect after confirming that the management agent is running on the new task.
choices.explanation: ECS Exec cannot be added to existing tasks after they start, so use a new task launched with the setting enabled.

choices.text: Change the ECS cluster’s Exec log destination to a new log group, then retry running the command on the original task.
choices.explanation: The logging configuration does not replace the task settings needed to enable a connection or start the agent.

choices.text: Send an ECS Exec command to the container in the existing task and wait for the agent to start on the first connection.
choices.explanation: A connection request does not add the management agent to a task that started with ECS Exec disabled.

choices.text: Change a tag on the task definition used by the existing task, then retry ECS Exec on the original task.
choices.explanation: Changing a tag does not change the ECS Exec setting that was in effect when the existing task started.

learning.reason: ECS Exec cannot be added to existing tasks after they start, so use a new task launched with the setting enabled.
learning.concept: Enabling ECS Exec applies to newly started tasks

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Block I/O stops even though the system and OS are healthy
prompt: A Nitro-based EC2 instance passes both system and instance status checks, but the application hangs while reading from and writing to a volume. You want to check the infrastructure-side reachability and I/O status of the attached EBS volume, separately from CPU load or application errors. What should you check?

choices.text: Set an alarm only on StatusCheckFailed_System and treat a value of 0 as confirmation that the volume is also connected properly.
choices.explanation: The result of the check for an attached volume is reported separately from the host infrastructure system check.

choices.text: Confirm that StatusCheckFailed_Instance is 0 and rule out a possible halt in volume I/O.
choices.explanation: Passing the OS or instance status check does not determine the result of the separate check for attached EBS volumes.

choices.text: Assume there is no storage reachability problem when EC2 CPUUtilization is low, and restart the application.
choices.explanation: CPU utilization does not measure volume reachability or whether I/O completes.

choices.text: Check EC2 StatusCheckFailed_AttachedEBS and compare it with the state of the EBS volume during the same period.
choices.explanation: This separately checks whether attached EBS volumes are reachable and can complete I/O.

learning.reason: This separately checks whether attached EBS volumes are reachable and can complete I/O.
learning.concept: EC2 attached EBS status check

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Reconstruct the route configuration from when the incident occurred
prompt: A misconfiguration in a route table interrupted connectivity, and an operator has already repaired it. AWS Config had been recording the configuration history for the resource before the incident. For the post-incident analysis, you want to compare the route table’s destinations and targets before and after the repair. Which record should you use?

choices.text: Open the resource timeline for the route table in AWS Config and compare the configuration items from during the incident and after the repair.
choices.explanation: You can compare configuration values recorded at different points in time. You can select a past configuration even if the current configuration has been restored.

choices.text: Retrieve the list of destinations and targets from the state history of a route table alarm in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: Alarm state transitions do not store all resource properties as the configuration at that point in time.

choices.text: Use an advanced query in AWS Config to retrieve the current routes from the aggregator and treat the results as the values from the time of the incident.
choices.explanation: The current configuration retrieved by an advanced query cannot restore the values from before the repair.

choices.text: Build all route table entries, including routes that did not forward traffic, from the destination field in VPC Flow Logs.
choices.explanation: Flow logs record observed traffic, but they do not store the contents of the configured route table.

learning.reason: You can compare configuration values recorded at different points in time. You can select a past configuration even if the current configuration has been restored.
learning.concept: Past configuration items on the resource timeline

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Diagnose a root volume offline after losing the management path
prompt: An EBS-backed EC2 Linux instance can no longer boot after an OS configuration change, and it does not accept Session Manager connections. Before replacing it with a standby instance, diagnose and repair it offline while preserving its original root volume. Stopping the instance is approved, and you will use an AWS Support managed runbook. Which option should you choose?

choices.text: Send a normal online diagnostic command to the existing EC2 instance with Run Command, and wait for the original OS agent to complete it.
choices.explanation: If the OS cannot boot and the instance cannot communicate as a managed node, it cannot process an online command.

choices.text: Run AWSSupport-ExecuteEC2Rescue to diagnose the original root volume from a helper instance.
choices.explanation: Even if SSM Agent is not running on the failed instance, the helper instance can work with its existing root volume.

choices.text: Keep rebooting the EC2 instance and wait for the OS configuration on the same root volume to be repaired automatically on another host.
choices.explanation: Rebooting does not fix the changed OS configuration or diagnose the original disk.

choices.text: Create a new EC2 instance from an AMI, delete the failed instance at the same time, and switch the diagnostic target.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the goal of preserving the target volume and diagnosing the existing OS.

learning.reason: Even if SSM Agent is not running on the failed instance, the helper instance can work with its existing root volume.
learning.concept: Offline EC2Rescue and root-volume repair with a helper instance

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: A message expires soon after moving to the DLQ
prompt: The retention period is 4 days for an SQS standard queue and 5 days for its DLQ. A message stays in the source queue for 3 days, then fails and moves to the DLQ; you want it to remain there for at least 4 days from that point for investigation. It expires even though ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage is still low in the DLQ. How should you fix this?

choices.text: Extend only the source queue's retention period, and operate on the assumption that the 5-day retention period starts over when the message reaches the DLQ.
choices.explanation: For standard queues, the original enqueue timestamp is preserved when a message moves to a DLQ, and changing the setting does not reset it.

choices.text: Set the DLQ retention period to cover the maximum time in the source queue plus the investigation period.
choices.explanation: For standard queues, expiration is calculated from the original enqueue time. For example, allowing up to 4 days in the source queue and 4 days for investigation requires a longer retention period that includes some margin.

choices.text: Wait until ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage exceeds 4 days, then start checking once the message has spent 4 days in the DLQ.
choices.explanation: The DLQ age metric and the expiration clock have different starting points, so the message may not remain until then.

choices.text: Keep the DLQ retention period at 5 days and set the visibility timeout to 4 days so the message is hidden during the investigation.
choices.explanation: The visibility timeout controls how long a message is hidden from other consumers; it does not extend the message's retention period.

learning.reason: For standard queues, expiration is calculated from the original enqueue time. For example, allowing up to 4 days in the source queue and 4 days for investigation requires a longer retention period that includes some margin.
learning.concept: For standard queues, moving a message to a DLQ does not reset the expiration clock

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Log Express successes and failures without sensitive payloads
prompt: You need to investigate intermittent failures in a Step Functions Express workflow. You must see successful and failed steps from start to finish without including sensitive input and output data in the logs. Which settings should you configure if you do not want to change the workflow type? Select TWO.

choices.text: Call GetExecutionHistory, as you would for Standard, on the Express execution ARN and disable CloudWatch Logs output.
choices.explanation: GetExecutionHistory does not support Express workflows.

choices.text: Set the log level to ERROR and assume that the final event will summarize every step that completed successfully.
choices.explanation: ERROR does not capture every successful transition, so the successful path leading to a failure might be unclear.

choices.text: Set includeExecutionData to false in the logging configuration.
choices.explanation: This disables the setting that includes execution-time input and output payloads in log events.

choices.text: Grant the execution role the required log-delivery permissions, set CloudWatch Logs as the destination, and set the level to ALL.
choices.explanation: This provides the execution-history logging destination for Express. ALL records events for successful progress as well as failures.

choices.text: Enable workflow metrics in case logging is unavailable, and reconstruct state transitions from CloudWatch aggregates alone.
choices.explanation: Aggregated metrics alone cannot reconstruct every state traversed by a single execution.

learning.reason: Disable the setting that includes execution-time input and output payloads in log events. CloudWatch Logs provides the execution-history logging destination for Express. ALL records events for successful progress as well as failures.
learning.concept: Express execution history in CloudWatch Logs and payload settings

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: An alarm suppressed for maintenance still triggers remediation
prompt: An SNS notification and a separate EventBridge rule that captures state-change events from the same CloudWatch alarm both trigger automatic remediation. During maintenance, DisableAlarmActions suppressed the SNS notification, but remediation still ran. How can you stop only remediation during maintenance while keeping the alarm evaluation active?

choices.text: Disable the EventBridge rule that starts remediation for the duration of the maintenance window.
choices.explanation: Stopping the alarm's actions and stopping a separate route that subscribes to state changes are different operations.

choices.text: Change the subscription filter for the SNS subscription that is not used for remediation, and leave the EventBridge rule's original conditions in place.
choices.explanation: SNS subscription settings do not change how a separate EventBridge rule matches events or handles remediation.

choices.text: Call DisableAlarmActions on the same alarm repeatedly to suppress both SNS and EventBridge subscriptions.
choices.explanation: Stopping the alarm's own actions does not stop state-change events from being sent to EventBridge.

choices.text: Stop the feature that generates the alarm metric and restart it after maintenance.
choices.explanation: This could stop remediation, but it could also disrupt monitoring evaluation and data, contrary to the requirement to keep evaluation active.

learning.reason: Stopping the alarm's actions and stopping a separate route that subscribes to state changes are different operations.
learning.concept: Alarm actions and EventBridge delivery of state changes

category: インシデントとイベントへの対応
examDomain: インシデントとイベントへの対応
title: Restart only an auxiliary container within a task
prompt: A Fargate task has an optional auxiliary container that runs for a long time. After it has run for at least a specified period, you want to restart only this container within the same task after a transient failure. A known exit code, 78, for a configuration error must not trigger a restart. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Make the auxiliary container essential and increase the ECS service desiredCount so another task starts when it becomes unhealthy.
choices.explanation: This can replace a task, but it does not restart only the auxiliary container within the same task.

choices.text: Set the auxiliary container's startup dependency to HEALTHY and use another task container as the restart trigger.
choices.explanation: Startup dependencies control the initial startup order; they do not conditionally restart a container that has exited.

choices.text: Change the check interval in the auxiliary container's healthCheck and replace exit code 78 with a port timeout.
choices.explanation: A health check interval cannot specify a process exit code to exclude from restarts.

choices.text: Enable restartPolicy for the auxiliary container, set 78 in ignoredExitCodes, and set the minimum uptime in restartAttemptPeriod.
choices.explanation: This enables recovery at the container level based on the container's exit code and its continuous uptime before the restart.

learning.reason: Recovery can be handled at the container level based on the container's exit code and its continuous uptime before the restart.
learning.concept: ECS container restart policy: ignored exit codes and uptime

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Shorten the account session for selected operational roles
prompt: In an organization that uses IAM Identity Center, keep the portal sign-in duration and the account sessions for read-only users unchanged, but make the AWS account role used for production write access expire one hour after access is obtained. Do not change the permissions or account assignments. What should you change?

choices.text: Directly modify only the role that IAM Identity Center created in the target account, without reprovisioning the permission set from AWS.
choices.explanation: Session requirements for managed roles are configured and delivered through permission sets. Editing a generated role is not the authoritative way to manage it.

choices.text: Set the IAM Identity Center portal sign-in session to one hour and leave the permission sets for all accounts unchanged.
choices.explanation: This affects the portal-wide session; it does not configure the AWS account session for only the target permission set.

choices.text: Set the session duration of the permission set for production write access to one hour, then provision the update to the assigned AWS account.
choices.explanation: This adjusts the session for the AWS account role obtained through that permission set without affecting other permission sets or the portal session duration.

choices.text: Keep the permission set unchanged and set a one-hour timeout for every AWS service the role can access.
choices.explanation: A service's processing timeout is separate from the expiration of AWS credentials obtained through IAM Identity Center.

learning.reason: This adjusts the session for the AWS account role obtained through the permission set without affecting other permission sets or the portal session duration.
learning.concept: Portal sessions and permission set sessions for AWS accounts

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス

title: Existing encrypted data became inaccessible after expiration
prompt: Data was encrypted with a symmetric KMS key that uses imported key material. The material expired, and the key entered the PendingImport state. The key and a preserved copy of the original material are still available. What should you do to decrypt the existing data using its original encryption context?

choices.text: Reimport the same preserved key material into the original KMS key, then decrypt with the key once it is available.
choices.explanation: Even if the key material expired and was deleted, restoring the same material to the same key can restore the ability to decrypt existing ciphertext.

choices.text: Generate new random key material, import it into the original KMS key, and use it to decrypt the existing ciphertext.
choices.explanation: The existing ciphertext corresponds to the original material. Importing new material alone cannot decrypt the original data.

choices.text: Enable the original key with EnableKey and decrypt using the existing key policy as is.
choices.explanation: Simply enabling a key in PendingImport because its key material is missing does not restore the material needed for decryption.

choices.text: Create a new AWS-generated key and point the application's KMS alias to it to decrypt the data.
choices.explanation: Changing the alias does not change the key material used to create the existing ciphertext.

learning.reason: Even if the key material expired and was deleted, restoring the same material to the same key can restore the ability to decrypt existing ciphertext.
learning.concept: Expiration of imported key material and reimporting the same material

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Continuously scan function code beyond its libraries
prompt: Amazon Inspector's Lambda standard scanning checks the packages used by ZIP functions with supported runtimes. You want to keep standard scanning enabled while automatically checking for unsafe API use and other issues in your own code in those same supported functions. What should you enable?

choices.text: Keep the functions as ZIP packages and enable Amazon ECR enhanced scanning.
choices.explanation: Enhanced scanning targets container images in ECR; it does not scan custom code in ZIP functions.

choices.text: Keep standard scanning enabled and move all dependency packages to Lambda layers.
choices.explanation: Using layers does not extend standard scanning to vulnerability analysis of your own code.

choices.text: Expand Inspector coverage to agentless EC2 scanning and inspect the Lambda code through the same EC2 snapshots.
choices.explanation: Scanning managed EC2 instances cannot inspect custom code in ZIP functions hosted by the Lambda service.

choices.text: Enable Lambda code scanning in addition to Lambda standard scanning.
choices.explanation: This allows application code in supported functions to be analyzed while standard scanning continues to check packages.

learning.reason: This allows application code in supported functions to be analyzed while standard scanning continues to check packages.
learning.concept: What Lambda standard scanning and Lambda code scanning cover

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Keep an ALB certificate eligible for automatic renewal
prompt: A public Application Load Balancer (ALB) uses a DNS-validated public certificate issued by ACM for TLS. The DNS administrator is about to remove the validation CNAME as a temporary record. Which two conditions must remain in place for ACM to automatically renew the active certificate? Select two.

choices.text: Delete the validation CNAME and keep only the alias record that routes traffic to the ALB.
choices.explanation: A traffic-routing record does not replace the ACM validation CNAME.

choices.text: Keep the required ACM validation CNAME resolvable in public DNS.
choices.explanation: ACM can verify domain control through DNS when it renews the certificate.

choices.text: Delete the validation CNAME and specify the current certificate ARN again after the certificate expires.
choices.explanation: Specifying the ARN again does not renew ACM validation or the certificate’s expiration date.

choices.text: Replace the ACM-issued certificate with a certificate from another provider, import it into ACM, and retain the same renewal method.
choices.explanation: Imported certificates are not eligible for ACM-managed renewal.

choices.text: Keep the ACM-issued certificate associated with an active ALB listener.
choices.explanation: A certificate in use by an integrated AWS service meets the usage condition for managed renewal.

learning.reason: ACM must be able to verify domain control through DNS when it renews the certificate, and the certificate must be in use by an integrated AWS service.
learning.concept: Managed renewal conditions for DNS-validated ACM certificates

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
