title: Rate-limit requests to the login path by source
prompt: An ALB with an AWS WAF web ACL is seeing a sharp increase in authentication attempts from the same source. Limit requests to /login by source IP and do not count requests for static files. Assume AWS WAF can directly inspect the trusted source IP. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Use a scope-down statement to limit the rule to /login, but aggregate all matching requests together.
choices.explanation: Aggregating all requests as one unit does not apply a separate limit to each user source.

choices.text: Use a rule that matches only the URI and counts abnormal RequestBody content, then have it switch automatically to Block after a threshold.
choices.explanation: A normal path match and the Count action alone do not configure blocking when an IP-specific rate limit is reached.

choices.text: Apply an IP-based rule to the entire web ACL and switch its action from Count to Block.
choices.explanation: Changing the action alone does not exclude static-file requests from the rate aggregation.

choices.text: Set the rate-based rule’s aggregation key to the source IP and use a scope-down statement that matches the URI path /login.
choices.explanation: This counts requests for the specified path separately by source IP and excludes other paths from the rate aggregation.

learning.reason: This counts requests for the specified path separately by source IP and excludes other paths from the rate aggregation.
learning.concept: Aggregation keys and scope-down statements in rate-based rules

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Detect permissions beyond a reviewed IAM policy in CI
prompt: A CI check for IAM policies reports syntax problems, but a syntactically valid permission expansion passed review. Using the current policy as the baseline, you want to mechanically detect when a replacement candidate adds new permissions before it is attached. What should you add?

choices.text: Scan existing resources with an external-access analyzer and replace the policy if the count of external findings does not increase.
choices.explanation: A check for external exposure does not compare the new permissions in the candidate IAM policy against the baseline policy.

choices.text: Before changing permissions, compare only IAM service last-accessed timestamps and do not add permissions that have never been used.
choices.explanation: Usage data cannot determine the set of operations a candidate that has not yet been deployed would newly allow.

choices.text: Pass the current policy and its replacement candidate to IAM Access Analyzer’s CheckNoNewAccess and require review if it allows new access.
choices.explanation: This compares the access allowed by the candidate with the current permissions, rather than just comparing textual differences.

choices.text: Run ValidatePolicy separately on both policies and treat them as equivalent if neither has a syntax error.
choices.explanation: Running the same check separately does not determine whether the candidate expands the baseline’s allowed access.

learning.reason: This compares the access allowed by the candidate with the current permissions, rather than just comparing textual differences.
learning.concept: Comparing allowed access with an existing policy using a custom policy check

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Scan an S3 object that predates protection
prompt: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 scans new uploads. You also need a scan result for a specific object version that existed before you enabled the protection configuration. You have met the requirements for a supported Region, permissions, and the object. How should you proceed without changing the original key or object version?

choices.text: Copy the object to its own key and upload it again, then treat the result as the scan result for the original version.
choices.explanation: If versioning is enabled, this creates a new version, so the scan would not preserve the specified original version.

choices.text: Send S3 events to a different GuardDuty Region and wait for a scan result for the object in the original bucket.
choices.explanation: Forwarding events does not submit a GuardDuty scan request for the specified version.

choices.text: Disable and recreate the new-upload protection plan, then wait for all existing versions to be rescanned automatically.
choices.explanation: Reconfiguring the plan does not start an on-demand scan of existing versions.

choices.text: Request an on-demand S3 malware scan from GuardDuty, specifying the existing object key and target version.
choices.explanation: This scans the specified existing object without requiring a new upload to trigger a scan.

learning.reason: This scans the specified existing object without requiring a new upload to trigger a scan.
learning.concept: GuardDuty upload-time scanning and on-demand S3 scans

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Reverting a shared policy for multiple roles
prompt: A customer managed IAM policy is used by 12 roles. Immediately after v4 was made the default version, required read access was lost. The validated v3 remains as a nondefault version of the same policy. How can you restore access while keeping each role attachment and the same policy ARN?

choices.text: Use SetDefaultPolicyVersion to make v3 the default.
choices.explanation: This restores the effective permission definition to the validated version without changing the role attachments.

choices.text: Reattach the same policy ARN to every role and specify v3 as a parameter for each attachment.
choices.explanation: An individual policy version is not specified when attaching a managed policy; attachments use the policy's default version.

choices.text: With v4 still the default, delete it using DeletePolicyVersion so that v3 automatically becomes the default.
choices.explanation: The version being deleted must be nondefault, so the current default version cannot be deleted first.

choices.text: Create a new managed policy with the contents of v3 and replace the attachments on the roles one by one.
choices.explanation: This might restore access, but it would not preserve the policy ARN or the existing attachments.

learning.reason: This restores the effective permission definition to the validated version without changing the role attachments.
learning.concept: All attachments to a managed policy use its default version.

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Recovering backups with approval when the production organization is inaccessible
prompt: Recovery points are stored in an AWS Backup logically air-gapped vault. To prepare for a situation where the production account's administrative path is unavailable, you want a recovery account in a separate organization to obtain restore access to the vault after approval by multiple people. Which actions should you configure in advance? Select TWO.

choices.text: Create a Multi-party approval team in the recovery-side organization, then share the team through AWS RAM with the vault-owning account and the recovery account.
choices.explanation: This keeps recovery-access decisions in an organization separate from production and makes the appropriate team available to both accounts.

choices.text: Add permanent vault-policy allows directly for each recovery operator so that everyone can restore independently.
choices.explanation: Individual standing permissions do not require approval by multiple people before a restore.

choices.text: Move the recovery points to a standard backup vault and configure Vault Lock, which automatically grants the recovery account restore access with approval.
choices.explanation: Vault Lock protects retention; it does not create multi-party-approved access for the recovery account.

choices.text: Grant restore permissions only to administrators in the original production account, then have the recovery side contact those administrators during an incident.
choices.explanation: This depends on a production-side administrative path that may be unavailable and does not implement approval by multiple people in a separate organization.

choices.text: Associate an approval team with the vault and set up a process for the recovery account to request restore access.
choices.explanation: This provides a path to restore access only when the request is approved.

learning.reason: Keep recovery-access decisions in an organization separate from production and make the appropriate team available to both accounts. A request can provide a path to restore access only after it is approved.
learning.concept: Associating a multi-party approval team in the recovery organization with the target vault

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Granting different S3 prefixes to groups of analysts
prompt: IAM principals using the same analytics application are allowed different S3 prefixes depending on their group. The application should not use its regular credentials to read all the data; instead, it should request short-lived read credentials that match the registered location and permissions. Which configuration should you use?

choices.text: Reissue the application's IAM access key every day in case it is exposed, and let all users read every prefix with the same key.
choices.explanation: Replacing a key frequently does not create temporary credentials with a per-user read scope.

choices.text: Configure locations and per-principal read grants with S3 Access Grants, then use temporary credentials from GetDataAccess to read the permitted prefixes.
choices.explanation: The requested access scope is checked against the granted access, and temporary credentials can be obtained for that scope.

choices.text: Create per-user prefix metrics with S3 Storage Lens and use the metrics configuration ID as credentials for the data.
choices.explanation: Storage Lens is an analytics service; it does not issue temporary credentials for accessing S3.

choices.text: Give the application read access to all data and hide keys from each listing on the client according to the user's group.
choices.explanation: Hiding entries in the user interface does not restrict the application's credential scope.

learning.reason: The requested access scope is checked against the grants, and temporary credentials are obtained for that scope.
learning.concept: Scoped credentials with S3 Access Grants and GetDataAccess

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Standardizing ownership of artifacts uploaded from another account
prompt: A production team's AWS account uploads artifacts to a general-purpose S3 bucket owned by a storage team. The storage team wants to own both existing and future artifacts without relying on the uploader's ACL settings, and manage access using only bucket and IAM policies. What should they configure?

choices.text: Enable only S3 Block Public Access on the bucket and leave Object Ownership and the current ACLs unchanged.
choices.explanation: Controlling public access is separate from standardizing ownership of objects created across accounts.

choices.text: Set the bucket's Object Ownership to Bucket owner enforced, and organize upload permissions and user permissions in policies.
choices.explanation: The bucket owner controls the objects, and ACLs can be removed from access management.

choices.text: Keep Object writer and require the uploader to attach an ACL granting the bucket owner full control to every upload request.
choices.explanation: The uploader remains the object owner, and access still depends on ACLs.

choices.text: Set Bucket owner preferred and transfer ownership of objects for which the client specifies bucket-owner-full-control.
choices.explanation: This path depends on ACL type and client configuration, so it does not meet the requirement to manage access uniformly without ACLs.

learning.reason: The bucket owner controls the objects, and ACLs can be removed from access management.
learning.concept: S3 Object Ownership with Bucket owner enforced and ACLs disabled

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Share an EBS Snapshot Encrypted with the Default Key Across Accounts
prompt: A recovery account must be able to create a copy of an EBS snapshot. The original snapshot is encrypted with the owning account's AWS managed key, aws/ebs. Keep the original snapshot and ensure the copy remains encrypted. Which two actions should be taken? Select 2.

choices.text: Share the copy with the recovery account and grant that account permission to use the KMS key required to copy the shared snapshot.
choices.explanation: Both permission to access the snapshot and permission to handle the encryption of its contents are required.

choices.text: Copy the snapshot in the original account and encrypt it with a customer managed KMS key that the account can manage.
choices.explanation: A snapshot encrypted with the default AWS managed key cannot be shared. Create a copy encrypted with a different key for sharing.

choices.text: Make the original encrypted snapshot public and assume the recovery account will automatically receive permission to use the encryption key.
choices.explanation: Encrypted snapshots cannot be made public, and public access settings do not grant KMS permissions.

choices.text: Specify a customer managed key only at the destination so the copy can be made without handling the original AWS managed key; do not prepare a copy in the original account.
choices.explanation: Specifying encryption for the destination copy alone does not let another account read an original snapshot that cannot be shared.

choices.text: Edit the key policy for the original aws/ebs key to add the recovery account as a new allowed principal.
choices.explanation: Users cannot modify the key policy of an AWS managed key to share it with another account.

learning.reason: Both permission to access the snapshot and permission to handle the encryption of its contents are required. A snapshot encrypted with the default AWS managed key cannot be shared. Create a copy encrypted with a different key for sharing.
learning.concept: Sharing permissions for encrypted snapshots and customer managed KMS keys

category: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
examDomain: セキュリティとコンプライアンス
title: Migrate an Internal Automated Job Away from Long-Term Access Keys
prompt: A worker in an on-premises data center sends audit results to S3. An existing internal certificate authority issues short-lived X.509 certificates. The job must not contain long-term AWS access keys; it must authenticate with a certificate and obtain temporary credentials for a least-privilege IAM role. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Create an EC2 instance profile and have the on-premises worker retrieve credentials using the EC2 metadata IP address.
choices.explanation: The on-premises worker is not running on the target EC2 instance and cannot authenticate itself through that instance's metadata.

choices.text: Register the internal certificate authority as a trust anchor in IAM Roles Anywhere, then use a profile with a trust policy scoped to the target worker.
choices.explanation: The issued certificate can authenticate the worker and provide temporary credentials for an authorized IAM role.

choices.text: Set the worker certificate's serial number as the ExternalId for STS AssumeRole and call AssumeRole without initial AWS credentials.
choices.explanation: ExternalId is a trust condition; it does not authenticate the caller of AWS APIs from a certificate.

choices.text: Import the same certificate into ACM and specify its ARN as the access key for the standard AWS CLI.
choices.explanation: An ACM certificate ARN does not provide access keys for making AWS API calls.

learning.reason: The issued certificate can authenticate the worker and provide temporary credentials for an authorized IAM role.
learning.concept: Certificates, trust anchors, and profiles in IAM Roles Anywhere
